items.desc: הגמרא פותחת בקביעת שיעורים: נקב הוושט ודרוסתו במשהו, נקב הקנה בכאיסר, ודרוסתו במשהו. הטעם: הזוהר (הסימנים) נשרף והולך.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by stating that a perforated windpipe (veshet) is invalid with any amount (bemashehu), and a trampled one (druṣa) is also invalid with any amount.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בקביעת שיעור נקב הוושט ודרוסתו במשהו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks about the measure for a trampled windpipe (kaneh), noting that a perforated one is invalid with a coin (issar), and inquiring about the trampled one.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בקביעת שיעור נקב הוושט ודרוסתו במשהו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that both are invalid with any amount because the force of the trampling spreads and causes damage.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בקביעת שיעור נקב הוושט ודרוסתו במשהו.

items.text: מחלוקת על בדיקת דרוסה: רב נחמן ורב יצחק
items.text_en: Rav Nachman's ruling on the inspection of a druṣa
items.desc_en: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta sits before Rav Nachman and states that a druṣa requires inspection opposite the intestines. Rav Nachman swears that Rav taught this from the 'kapa' to the 'atma'. The Gemara clarifies that 'kapa' refers to the skull (kapa democha), not the hand (kapa dida), meaning from the skull to the spine.
items.desc: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא אמר בשם רב נחמן שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים. רב נחמן עצמו אמר: 'האלהים! מורי בה רב מכפא ועד אטמא'. הגמרא מבהירה ש'כפא' הכוונה לכפא דמוחא (הגולגולת).

sub.text: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא בשם רב נחמן
sub.text_en: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta
sub.desc_en: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta states before Rav Nachman that a druṣa requires inspection opposite the intestines.
sub.desc: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא יושב לפני רב נחמן ואומר בשמו שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים, ורב נחמן משיב בשבועה שמורי בה רב מכפא ועד אטמא.

sub.text: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא בשם רב נחמן
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman swears that Rav taught this ruling from the 'kapa' to the 'atma'.
sub.desc: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא יושב לפני רב נחמן ואומר בשמו שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים, ורב נחמן משיב בשבועה שמורי בה רב מכפא ועד אטמא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that 'kapa' refers to the skull (kapa democha), not the hand (kapa dida), meaning from the skull to the spine.

items.text: עדות רב חייא בר יוסף על רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש
items.text_en: Rav Chiyya bar Yosef's report to Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
items.desc_en: When Rav Chiyya bar Yosef ascended, he found Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish discussing the same ruling about druṣa requiring inspection opposite the intestines. He told them that Rav taught from the kapa to the atma. Reish Lakish dismissively asks 'Who is Rav and who is Rav? I don't know him!' Rabbi Yochanan rebukes him, saying that the student (Rav) who served Rabbi (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi) should be known, and that he himself served Rabbi in a standing position while that student served in a seated position, and that student was a great man.
items.desc: רב חייא בר יוסף מצא את רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש שאמרו שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים, וסיפר להם שרב נחמן אמר 'מכפא ועד אטמא'. ריש לקיש תמה: 'מנו רב ומנו רב?' רבי יוחנן הגן על רב נחמן, ואמר ששימש את רבי רבה, והוא גבר בכולא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Chiyya bar Yosef finds Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish discussing the same ruling about druṣa requiring inspection opposite the intestines, and tells them that Rav taught from the kapa to the atma.
sub.desc: רב חייא בר יוסף עלה ומצא את רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש יושבים ואומרים שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים.

sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish dismissively asks 'Who is Rav and who is Rav? I don't know him!'
sub.desc: רב חייא בר יוסף עלה ומצא את רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש יושבים ואומרים שדרוסה צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan rebukes Reish Lakish, saying that the student (Rav) who served Rabbi (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi) should be known, and that he himself served Rabbi in a standing position while that student served in a seated position, and that student was a great man.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן הגן על רב נחמן ואמר ששימש את רבי רבה והוא גבר בכולא.

items.text: Reish Lakish's tradition about a shemuṭa and sheḥuṭa
items.text_en: Reish Lakish's tradition about a shemuṭa and sheḥuṭa
items.desc_en: Immediately, Reish Lakish opened and said: 'But remember that man for good, for a tradition was said in his name: A shemuṭa (a detached organ) that is then sheḥuṭa (slaughtered) is kosher, because it is impossible for a shemuṭa to become sheḥuṭa.' Rabbi Yochanan disagrees, saying: 'Let him bring and surround (i.e., it is invalid).'

sub.desc_en: Reish Lakish opens by citing a tradition in the name of a certain man: a shemuṭa (detached organ) that is then sheḥuṭa (slaughtered) is kosher, because it is impossible for a shemuṭa to become sheḥuṭa.
Rabbi Yochanan objects, saying 'Let him bring and surround' (i.e., the ruling is invalid).

items.text: Rav Nachman's distinction regarding grasping the simanim
items.text_en: Rav Nachman's distinction regarding grasping the simanim
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman says: They only taught (that it is impossible) when he did not grasp the simanim (the signs, i.e., the windpipe and esophagus), but if he grasped the simanim and slaughtered, it is possible for a shemuṭa to become sheḥuṭa. The Gemara then asks: 'This is the general rule' – what does it come to include? It comes to include the seven traditions (shav shema'tata) that follow.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman distinguishes: the rule that a shemuṭa cannot become sheḥuṭa applies only when the slaughterer did not grasp the simanim (the trachea and esophagus), but if he grasped them and slaughtered, it is possible.
The Gemara asks: the phrase 'this is the general rule' — what does it come to include?
The Gemara answers: it comes to include the seven traditions (shav shema'tata) that follow.

items.text: מעשים שאין מוסיפים על הטריפות
items.text_en: Two cases of adding to terefot: the gid nashya and the kidney
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings two cases: The house of Yosef the Rishba struck the gid nashya (sciatic nerve) and killed animals; they came before Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, who said: 'Is there adding to the terefot? You have only what the Sages enumerated!' Similarly, Rav Pappa bar Abba the Rishba struck the kidney and killed animals; they came before Rabbi Abba, who said the same. The Gemara objects: 'But we see that it dies!' The answer: They have a tradition that if one applies a remedy, it lives.
items.desc: שני מעשים: דבי יוסף רישבא מחאו בגידא נשיא וקטלי, ורב פפא בר אבא רישבא מחאו בכוליא וקטלי. בשני המקרים אמרו החכמים (רבי יהודה בן בתירא ורבי אבא): 'וכי להוסיף על הטריפות יש? אין לך אלא מה שמנו חכמים!' הגמרא מקשה: והא קא חזינן דקא מתה! ומתרצת: גמירי דאי בדרי לה סמא – חייא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara recounts that the house of Yosef the Rishba struck the gid nashya (sciatic nerve) and killed animals, and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira ruled that one may not add to the terefot (list of terminal conditions).
sub.desc: מביא מעשה ראשון: דבי יוסף רישבא מחאו בגידא נשיא וקטלי, ורבי יהודה בן בתירא אמר שאין להוסיף על הטריפות.

sub.text: מעשה דרב פפא בר אבא רישבא
sub.desc_en: The Gemara recounts a parallel case where Rav Pappa bar Abba the Rishba struck the kidney and killed animals, and Rabbi Abba gave the same ruling.
sub.desc: מביא מעשה שני: רב פפא בר אבא רישבא מחאו בכוליא וקטלי, ורבי אבא אמר שאין להוסיף על הטריפות.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects: But we see that the animal dies from such a strike!
sub.desc: מקשה: הרי אנו רואים שהבהמה מתה, ואם כן מדוע אין זה נחשב טריפה?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers: They have a tradition that if one applies a remedy, the animal lives.
sub.desc: מקשה: הרי אנו רואים שהבהמה מתה, ואם כן מדוע אין זה נחשב טריפה?

items.text: משנת 'ואלו כשרות בבהמה'
items.text_en: Mishnah: List of kosher conditions in an animal
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists cases where an animal is kosher despite defects: a perforated or cracked windpipe (up to the size of an Italian issar per Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel), a fractured skull without piercing the brain membrane, a pierced heart without entering its chamber, a broken spine without severing the spinal cord, a missing liver with an olive-sized remnant remaining, the mesus and the beit hakosot (the stomach and the abomasum) that perforated into each other, a removed spleen, removed kidneys, a removed lower jaw, a removed womb, and a 'charuta' (a wound) by Heaven. The Mishnah concludes with a dispute about a flayed animal: Rabbi Meir validates it, while the Sages invalidate it.
items.desc: המשנה מונה את המקרים הכשרים בבהמה: ניקבה הגרגרת או נסדקה, נפחתה הגולגולת ולא ניקב קרום המוח, ניקב הלב ולא לבית חללו, נשברה השדרה ולא נפסק החוט, ניטלה הכבד ונשתייר כזית, המסס ובית הכוסות שניקבו זה לתוך זה, ניטל הטחול, ניטלו הכליות, ניטל לחת התחתון, ניטלה האם, וחרותה בידי שמים. הגלודה – רבי מאיר מכשיר וחכמים פוסלים.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by listing kosher conditions in an animal: a perforated or cracked windpipe, a fractured skull without piercing the brain membrane, a pierced heart without entering its chamber, a broken spine without severing the spinal cord, and a missing liver with an olive-sized remnant remaining.

The Mishnah continues listing kosher conditions: the mesus and the beit hakosot that perforated into each other, a removed spleen, removed kidneys, a removed lower jaw, a removed womb, and a 'charuta' (a wound) by Heaven.
The Mishnah concludes with a dispute about a flayed animal: Rabbi Meir validates it, while the Sages invalidate it.

items.text: מחלוקת רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש על דיוק המשנה
items.text_en: Gemara: Dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish on the Mishnah's implication
items.desc_en: The Gemara states: It was said: Rabbi Yochanan said: 'These are terefot' is precise (meaning only those listed are terefot), and Reish Lakish said: 'These are kosher' is precise (meaning only those listed are kosher). The Gemara asks: What do they disagree about? They disagree about the statement of Rav Mattana, who said: 'This buka (a hole) in the atma (spine) that moved from its place is a terefah.' Rabbi Yochanan holds that 'These are terefot' is precise, so the Tanna taught terefot and taught 'This is the general rule' (implying the list is exhaustive).
items.desc: אתמר: רבי יוחנן אמר 'אלו טריפות' דווקא, וריש לקיש אמר 'אלו כשרות' דווקא. הגמרא מבארת במאי פליגי: בדרב מתנא שאמר 'האי בוקא דאטמא דשף מדוכתיה – טריפה'. רבי יוחנן סובר שתנא טריפות ותנא 'זה הכלל'.

sub.desc_en: The gemara reports a dispute: Rabbi Yochanan says the Mishnah's phrase 'אלו טרפות' (these are terefot) is precise (exhaustive), while Reish Lakish says 'אלו כשרות' (these are kosher) is precise (exhaustive).
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת במחלוקת בין רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש: רבי יוחנן מפרש 'אלו טריפות' דווקא, וריש לקיש מפרש 'אלו כשרות' דווקא.

sub.desc_en: The gemara asks: What is the practical disagreement between them? It answers that they dispute the ruling of Rav Mattana, who said a hole in the spine that moved from its place is a terefah.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת במה נחלקו רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש.

sub.desc_en: The gemara explains: Rabbi Yochanan holds that 'אלו טרפות' is precise, so the Tanna listed terefot and also stated 'זה הכלל' (this is the general rule), implying the list is exhaustive and excluding Rav Mattana's case.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת במחלוקת בין רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש: רבי יוחנן מפרש 'אלו טריפות' דווקא, וריש לקיש מפרש 'אלו כשרות' דווקא.

items.text: מחלוקת רב מתנא וריש לקיש בזה הכלל
items.text_en: Dispute between Rav Mattana and Resh Lakish about the Mishnah's rule
items.desc_en: Rav Mattana and Resh Lakish argue whether the Mishnah's general principle includes or excludes Rav Mattana's case of a shifted lung lobe. Rav Mattana holds that the Mishnah's list of tereifot is exclusive, so his case is kosher; Resh Lakish holds that the Mishnah's list of kosher cases is exclusive, so Rav Mattana's case is tereifah.
items.desc: רב מתנא וריש לקיש נחלקו בפירוש המשנה: האם 'זה הכלל' בא לרבות או למעט את דין בוקא דאטמא. רב מתנא סובר שהכלל כולל אותו, וריש לקיש סובר שאינו בכלל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara presents Rav Mattana's position: the Mishnah's list of טריפות (terefot) is exclusive, so his case of a shifted lung lobe is kosher.
sub.desc: רב מתנא טוען שדין בוקא דאטמא נכלל ב'זה הכלל' שבמשנת טרפות, ולפיכך הוא כשר.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish argues that the Mishnah's list of kosher cases is exclusive, so Rav Mattana's case is tereifah.
sub.desc: ריש לקיש חולק על רב מתנא וסובר שבוקא דאטמא אינו בכלל 'זה הכלל', ולפיכך הוא טרפה.

items.text: דין בוקא דאטמא
items.text_en: Rav Mattana and Rava's dispute on the shifted lung lobe
items.desc_en: Rav Mattana rules that a lung lobe that has shifted from its place is tereifah, while Rava rules it is kosher. Rava adds that if its bronchus is severed it is tereifah, but the halakhah concludes that even if severed it is kosher until it decays.
items.desc: רב מתנא ורבא נחלקו בדין בוקא דאטמא ששף מדוכתיה: רב מתנא פוסל, רבא מכשיר. נפסקה הלכה שאף אם נפסק ניבו כשרה עד שתתעכל.

sub.desc_en: Rav Mattana rules that a lung lobe (בוקא דאטמא) that shifted from its place is tereifah.
sub.desc: רב מתנא פוסל בוקא דאטמא ששף מדוכתיה.

sub.desc_en: Rava counters that a shifted lobe is kosher, but if its branch (ניב) is severed it is tereifah.
sub.desc: רב מתנא פוסל בוקא דאטמא ששף מדוכתיה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that even a severed branch is kosher until it rots away.
sub.desc: רב מתנא פוסל בוקא דאטמא ששף מדוכתיה.

sub.desc_en: The halakhah concludes that even if the bronchus is severed, the animal is kosher until the lobe decays (מִתְעַכְלָא אִתְעֲכוֹלֵי).
sub.desc: רב מתנא פוסל בוקא דאטמא ששף מדוכתיה.

items.text: שיעור חסרון בבוקא דאטמא
items.text_en: Ze'iri defines the measure of the missing part
items.desc_en: Ze'iri states that for those who do not see a specific measure, the measure is a Kurdinai dinar, which is a small p'shita coin found among the p'shita coins of Pumbedita.
items.desc: זעירי קובע שיעור לחסרון: דינר קורדינאה, שהוא כפשיטה זוטרתי הנמצאת בין פשיטי דפומבדיתא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: how much must the lobe be missing to be considered tereifah?
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהו השיעור המינימלי של חסרון בבוקא דאטמא.

sub.desc_en: Ze'iri answers that the measure is a Kurdish dinar, which is like a small p'shita coin found among the Pumbeditan p'shita coins.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהו השיעור המינימלי של חסרון בבוקא דאטמא.

items.text: Rabbi Chana Patura'ah's story about Bar Nappacha
items.text_en: Rabbi Chana Patura'ah's story about Bar Nappacha
items.desc_en: Rabbi Chana Patura'ah recounts that Bar Nappacha asked him about the Kurdinai dinar for measuring tereifot, and when he tried to stand before him, Bar Nappacha told him to sit, as craftsmen are not required to stand before Torah scholars while engaged in their work.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chana Patura'a recounts that Bar Nappacha asked him for a Kurdish dinar to measure tereifot, and when he tried to stand out of respect, Bar Nappacha told him craftsmen need not stand for Torah scholars while working.

items.text: Gemara questions the exception for craftsmen
items.text_en: Gemara questions the exception for craftsmen
items.desc_en: The Gemara challenges the story with a Mishnah that requires craftsmen to stand before Torah scholars. Rabbi Yochanan resolves that they stand before the scholars themselves but not before Torah scholars (i.e., students). Rabbi Yosei bar Avin praises the mitzvah at its time, and the Gemara suggests an alternative reason: to avoid causing them to stumble in the future.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges the story by citing a Mishnah that requires craftsmen to stand before Torah scholars and greet them.
Rabbi Yochanan resolves that craftsmen stand before the scholars themselves but not before Torah scholars (i.e., students).
Rabbi Yosei bar Avin praises the mitzvah at its time, noting that craftsmen stand before the scholars but not before Torah students.
The Gemara suggests an alternative reason for the exception: to avoid causing the craftsmen to stumble in the future.

items.text: Rav Nachman's principle on inclusive language
items.text_en: Rav Nachman's principle on inclusive language
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman states that 'like a sela' means more than a sela, and 'like an issar' means more than an issar. The Gemara infers that Rav Nachman holds that the term 'ad' (until) does not include the endpoint.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman states that the phrase 'like a sela' means more than a sela, and 'like an issar' means more than an issar.
The Gemara infers from Rav Nachman's statement that he holds the term 'עד' (until) does not include the endpoint.

items.text: Rava's objections to Rav Nachman from Mishnayot
items.text_en: Rava's objections to Rav Nachman from Mishnayot
items.desc_en: Rava challenges Rav Nachman's principle with three Mishnaic examples: a rope from a bed up to five handbreadths is pure, and from five to ten is impure. The Gemara deflects each by interpreting the numbers as inclusive of the upper limit, not the lower.

sub.desc_en: Rava challenges Rav Nachman by citing a Mishnah: a rope from a bed up to five handbreadths is pure, implying the limit is inclusive of the lower bound.
The Gemara deflects by interpreting 'five' as inclusive of the upper limit, not the lower.
Rava cites another Mishnah: from five to ten handbreadths is impure, implying the upper limit is inclusive of the lower bound.
The Gemara deflects again by interpreting 'ten' as inclusive of the upper limit.
Rava cites a third Mishnah about small clay vessels that sit without support, implying the same principle.

items.text: Clarifying the direction of volume measurements
items.text_en: Clarifying the direction of volume measurements
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether the terms 'log', 'se'ah', and 'sata'im' in the mishnah refer to upper or lower limits. After a series of attempts to prove they are lower limits, a baraita is cited that explicitly states they are lower limits. The Gemara resolves the contradiction by explaining that the earlier statements were for stringency, citing Rabbi Avahu's principle that all measures of the Sages are for stringency except for the size of a gris for stains.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether the term 'log' in the mishnah's range 'from the size of a small smear to a log' means a lower limit (i.e., up to a log).
The Gemara rejects the interpretation, asserting that 'log' is an upper limit (i.e., up to a log, not including a log).
The Gemara brings a supporting baraita: 'from a log to a se'ah — a quarter-log,' and asks whether 'se'ah' is a lower limit.
The Gemara again rejects, stating that 'se'ah' is an upper limit.
The Gemara brings another baraita: 'from a se'ah to two se'ah — a half-log,' and asks whether 'two se'ah' is a lower limit.
The Gemara rejects again, stating that 'two se'ah' is an upper limit.
The Gemara objects by citing a baraita that explicitly states 'log — lower limit, se'ah — lower limit, two se'ah — lower limit,' contradicting the previous answers.

The Gemara resolves the contradiction by explaining that the baraita with lower limits is for stringency (לחומרא), citing Rabbi Avahu's principle that all measures of the Sages are for stringency except for the size of a gris for stains, which is for leniency.

items.text: דיוק מברייתא אחרת
items.text_en: Supporting the principle from a baraita
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the baraita itself supports the principle that measures are for stringency, as it teaches that five is an upper limit and ten is a lower limit.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה דיוק מברייתא נוספת המוכיחה את הכלל של שיעורים להחמיר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the baraita itself supports the principle that measures are for stringency, as it teaches that five is an upper limit and ten is a lower limit.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה דיוק מברייתא נוספת המוכיחה את הכלל של שיעורים להחמיר.

items.text: The law of a missing or punctured spleen
items.text_en: The law of a missing or punctured spleen
items.desc_en: Rav Avira reports in the name of Rava that the mishnah's ruling that an animal is kosher if the spleen is removed applies only to removal, but if it is punctured, the animal is a treifah. Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or bar Zevida) challenges this from a baraita that permits eating the fetus but forbids eating the spleen and kidneys, implying the animal itself is permitted. The Gemara answers that the baraita's case is different (punctured vs. cut) or that the baraita's wording is due to the structure of the teaching.

sub.text: Rav Avira in the name of Rava
sub.text_en: Rav Avira in the name of Rava
sub.desc_en: Rav Avira reports in Rava's name that the mishnah's leniency for a removed spleen applies only to removal (ניטל), but if the spleen is punctured (ניקב), the animal is a טריפה (treifah).

sub.text: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida)
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida)
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or bar Zevida) objects from a baraita that permits eating the fetus but forbids eating the spleen and kidneys, implying the animal itself is permitted even if the spleen is cut.
The Gemara answers that the baraita actually forbids the animal itself as well, but the wording is structured to match the opening clause about the fetus.
Alternatively, the Gemara resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between a punctured spleen (ניקב), which is a טריפה, and a cut spleen (נחתך), which is permitted.

items.text: דין נטילת כליות
items.text_en: The law of a diseased kidney
items.desc_en: Rachish bar Pappa reports in the name of Rav that if one kidney is diseased, the animal is a treifah. The Gemara adds that in the West they say this applies only if the disease has reached the core.
items.desc: רכיש בר פפא בשם רב אומר שלקתה בכליה אחת טרפה, ובמערבא מפרשים שזה דווקא כשהגיעה הלקותא.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states the case of the kidneys being removed.
sub.desc: רכיש בר פפא מוסר בשם רב שכליה שלקתה באחת מהן עושה את הבהמה טרפה.

sub.text_en: Rachish bar Pappa in the name of Rav
sub.desc_en: Rachish bar Pappa reports in the name of Rav that if one kidney is diseased, the animal is a טריפה (ritually unfit).
sub.desc: רכיש בר פפא מוסר בשם רב שכליה שלקתה באחת מהן עושה את הבהמה טרפה.

sub.desc_en: The Sages of the West add that this applies only when the disease has reached the core of the kidney.
sub.desc: רכיש בר פפא מוסר בשם רב שכליה שלקתה באחת מהן עושה את הבהמה טרפה.

items.text: דין נקב בכוליא – מחלוקת רב עוירא ורכיש בר פפא
items.text_en: Location of the 'place of the groove' and ruling of Rav Nechunya
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that the 'place of the groove' is the white of the kidneys. Rav Nechunya reports that he asked all the slaughterers of the West and they said the halakha follows Rachish bar Pappa, not Rav Avira. However, Rav Avira's ruling is only applied leniently when the perforation is on the thick side; if on the thin side, it is a terefah, unless a gold dinar's thickness remains.
items.desc: רב נחוניה שאל את כל הטבחים במערב ואמרו שהלכה כרכיש בר פפא. רב עוירא מודה רק בקולשיה, אבל בסומכיה טריפה, ואם נשתייר כעובי דינר זהב – כשרה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks where the 'place of the groove' is and answers that it is the white of the kidneys.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת היכן מקום החריץ בכוליא, ומשיבה: במקום הלבן שבמותניים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nechunya reports that he asked all the slaughterers of the West and they said the halakha follows Rachish bar Pappa, not Rav Avira.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת היכן מקום החריץ בכוליא, ומשיבה: במקום הלבן שבמותניים.

sub.text_en: Gemara's clarification of Rav Avira's ruling
sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that Rav Avira's ruling is only applied leniently when the perforation is on the thick side; if on the thin side, it is a terefah, unless a gold dinar's thickness remains.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת: רב עוירא עצמו מודה רק בקולשיה, אבל בסומכיה טריפה, ואם נשתייר כעובי דינר זהב – כשרה.

items.text: כלל הפוסל בריאה כשר בכוליא – דחיית רבי תנחומא
items.text_en: General rule about terefot: lung vs. kidney, and objection
items.desc_en: In the West they said: Whatever disqualifies in the lung is kosher in the kidney, since a perforation is invalid in the lung but kosher in the kidney. Rabbi Tanchuma objects: Is that a rule? The 'mugla' (a certain lung condition) is kosher in the lung but invalid in the kidney! And clear water is kosher in both. Rav Ashi responds: Do you compare terefot to each other? We do not say one terefah is similar to another, because cutting here kills, cutting there it lives.
items.desc: במערב אמרו שכל הפוסל בריאה כשר בכוליא, שהרי נקב פסול בריאה וכשר בכוליא. רבי תנחומא מקשה ממוגלא שכשרה בריאה ופסולה בכוליא, וממים זכין שכשרים בשניהם. רב אשי דוחה שאין דנים טריפות זו מזו.

sub.desc_en: The Sages of the West state a general rule: whatever disqualifies the lung is kosher in the kidney, and certainly whatever is kosher in the lung is kosher in the kidney.
sub.desc: הצגת הכלל: כל הפוסל בריאה כשר בכוליא, עם דוגמת נקב.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Tanchuma objects: Is this a rule? The 'mugla' (a certain lung condition) is kosher in the lung but invalid in the kidney, and clear water is kosher in both.
sub.desc: הקשה רבי תנחומא על הכלל ממוגלא שכשרה בריאה ופסולה בכוליא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi responds: Do you compare terefot to each other? We do not say one terefah is similar to another, because cutting here kills and cutting there it lives.
sub.desc: הקשה רבי תנחומא על הכלל ממוגלא שכשרה בריאה ופסולה בכוליא.

items.text: דין מים זכין – צלולים ולא סרוחים
items.text_en: Clarification about clear water in the kidney
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that clear water in the kidney is kosher only if it is clear, but if it is murky, it is a terefah. And even if clear, only if it does not stink; if it stinks, it is a terefah.
items.desc: מים זכין כשרים רק כשהם צלולים, אבל עכורים – טריפה. גם בצלולים, אם סרוחים – טריפה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that clear water in the kidney is kosher only if it is clear, but if murky or stinking, it is a terefah.
sub.desc: הגמרא פוסקת שמים זכין כשרים רק כשהם צלולים, אבל עכורים או סרוחים – טריפה.

items.text: שיעור הקטנת הכוליה
items.text_en: Kidney that shrank
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states: If the kidney shrank, in a small animal up to the size of a bean (k'fol), in a large animal up to the size of a medium grape.
items.desc: הכוליה שהקטינה: בדקה – עד כפול, בגסה – עד כענבה בינונית.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states the measure for a shrunken kidney: in a small animal up to the size of a bean, in a large animal up to the size of a medium grape.
sub.desc: התנא קובע שיעורים להקטנת הכוליה: בדקה עד כפול, ובגסה עד כענבה בינונית.

items.text: נטילת הלחי התחתון – דין רבי זירא
items.text_en: Lower jaw removed
items.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira says: They only taught that the animal is kosher if the lower jaw is removed when it can live by being fed and having its throat filled, but if it cannot, it is a terefah.
items.desc: רבי זירא אומר: לא שנו אלא שיכולה לחיות על ידי לעיטה והמראה, אבל אם אינה יכולה – טריפה.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states the case of an animal whose lower jaw was removed.
sub.desc: רבי זירא מבחין בין מקרה שהבהמה יכולה לחיות על ידי לעיטה והמראה, שאז כשרה, לבין מקרה שאינה יכולה, שאז טריפה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira qualifies the Mishnah: the animal is kosher only if it can survive by being fed and having its throat filled; otherwise it is a terefah.
sub.desc: רבי זירא מבחין בין מקרה שהבהמה יכולה לחיות על ידי לעיטה והמראה, שאז כשרה, לבין מקרה שאינה יכולה, שאז טריפה.

items.text: נטילת האם – היא טרפחת ושלפוחית
items.text_en: The mother (spleen) removed
items.desc_en: It was taught: The 'mother' (spleen) is the same as the 'tarpechat' and the 'shalpuchit'.
items.desc: תנא: האם היא טרפחת היא שלפוחית.

sub.desc_en: A Tanna teaches that the 'mother' (spleen) is identical to the 'tarpechat' and the 'shalpuchit'.
sub.desc: התנא מבהיר שהאם, הטרפחת והשלפוחית הם אותו איבר.

items.text: חרותה – דיני צמיקת הריאה ומבחן המים
items.text_en: Shriveled lung (charutah): dispute and test
items.desc_en: A shriveled lung caused by Heaven is kosher; by human action, it is a terefah. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Even by any creature. A dilemma is raised: does he argue on the first clause leniently or on the latter stringently? A baraisa resolves it: he says 'even by any creature' (stringent). Rabba bar bar Chanah found rams with shriveled lungs and was told a test: in summer, put them in white baskets with cold water for a day; if they heal, it is by Heaven and kosher; if not, terefah. In winter, use warm baskets with lukewarm water.
items.desc: חרותה בידי שמים כשרה, בידי אדם טריפה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר אף בידי כל הבריות. נסתפקו אם הוא מקל או מחמיר. ברייתא מבהירה שהוא מחמיר. רבה בר בר חנה מצא אילים צמוקי ריאה ושאל: בקיץ – מים קרים, בחורף – מים פושרים, ואם חוזרת לבריאות – כשרה.

sub.desc_en: The Tanna Kamma rules that a shriveled lung caused by Heaven is kosher, but if caused by human action it is a terefah.
sub.desc: פותחת בדין חרותה: בידי שמים כשרה, בידי אדם טריפה.

sub.desc_en: The baraisa defines a shriveled lung and adds Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar's position that even if caused by any creature it is a terefah.
sub.desc: פותחת בדין חרותה: בידי שמים כשרה, בידי אדם טריפה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a dilemma: does Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar argue on the first clause leniently or on the latter clause stringently?
sub.desc: מסתפקים אם רבי שמעון בן אלעזר מקל (שהרי בידי אדם טריפה, וכל הבריות כמוהו) או מחמיר (שהרי בידי שמים כשרה, וכל הבריות טריפה).

sub.desc_en: A baraisa resolves the dilemma by citing Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar's statement in the context of the stringent clause, showing he argues stringently.
sub.desc: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר מוסיף שגם בידי כל הבריות (חיות) טריפה.

sub.text_en: Story of Rabba bar bar Chanah
sub.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah found rams with shriveled lungs and was told a practical test: in summer use white baskets with cold water, in winter warm baskets with lukewarm water, to determine if the condition is from Heaven (kosher) or not (terefah).
sub.desc: מעשה ברבה בר בר חנה שמצא אילים צמוקי ריאה, ושאל בבית המדרש; השיבו לו מבחן מים: בקיץ מים קרים, בחורף מים פושרים, ואם הריאה חוזרת לבריאות – כשרה, ואם לא – טריפה.

items.text: גלודה – מחלוקת רבי מאיר וחכמים, וחזרתו
items.text_en: The gludah (animal whose skin was removed): dispute and retraction
items.desc_en: The Sages taught: Regarding the gludah, Rabbi Meir permits and the Sages prohibit. Elazar the Scribe and Yochanan ben Gudgada testified it is invalid. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says Rabbi Meir retracted. But does Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar hold that Rabbi Meir disputed? Another baraisa says Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said they did not dispute; Rabbi Oshaya testified in the name of Rabbi Tarfon that it is invalid, but if a selah-sized piece remains, it is kosher. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak explains: 'They did not dispute' means Rabbi Meir did not persist in his dispute.
items.desc: תנו רבנן: גלודה – רבי מאיר מכשיר וחכמים פוסלים, ואלעזר ספרה ויוחנן בן גודגדא העידו שפסולה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אמר שחזר בו רבי מאיר. רב נחמן בר יצחק מבאר: 'לא נחלקו' – לא עמד רבי מאיר במחלוקתו.

sub.desc_en: The baraita opens with the dispute about the gludah (animal whose skin was removed): Rabbi Meir permits, the Sages prohibit, and Elazar the Scribe and Yochanan ben Gudgda testified it is invalid.
sub.desc: הברייתא מציגה את מחלוקת רבי מאיר וחכמים בגלודה, ומביאה עדות של אלעזר ספרה ויוחנן בן גודגדא שפסולה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar states that Rabbi Meir retracted his position.
sub.desc: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר קובע שרבי מאיר חזר בו ממחלוקתו והסכים לפסול גלודה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar implies that Rabbi Meir initially disputed the halacha.
sub.desc: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר קובע שרבי מאיר חזר בו ממחלוקתו והסכים לפסול גלודה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects by citing another baraita where Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says they did not dispute, and Rabbi Oshaya testified in the name of Rabbi Tarfon that the gludah is invalid unless a selah-sized piece remains.
sub.desc: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר קובע שרבי מאיר חזר בו ממחלוקתו והסכים לפסול גלודה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak resolves the contradiction: 'They did not dispute' means Rabbi Meir did not persist in his dispute, i.e., he retracted.
sub.desc: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר קובע שרבי מאיר חזר בו ממחלוקתו והסכים לפסול גלודה.

items.text: Location of the selah-sized remnant on the gludah
items.text_en: Location of the selah-sized remnant on the gludah
items.desc_en: The Master said: If a selah-sized piece remains, it is kosher. Where? Rav Yehuda said Shmuel said: Along the entire spine. A dilemma: is it lengthwise and narrow, so that when joined it is a selah, or the width of a selah along the entire spine? Rabbi Nehorai in the name of Shmuel clarifies: The width of a selah along the entire spine.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Master's statement that if a selah-sized remnant remains on the gludah, the animal is kosher.
The Gemara asks where on the gludah this selah-sized remnant must be located.
Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel answers that the remnant must be along the entire spine.
The Gemara raises a dilemma: is the remnant lengthwise and narrow, so that when joined it equals a selah, or is it the width of a selah along the entire spine?
Rabbi Nehorai in the name of Shmuel resolves the dilemma: the remnant must be the width of a selah along the entire spine.

items.text: Other opinions on the remnant location and an unresolved dilemma
items.text_en: Other opinions on the remnant location and an unresolved dilemma
items.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah says: The heads of the vertebrae. Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai says: The place of the navel. Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael asks: If the place of the spine was removed but all else remains, or the place of the navel, or the heads of the vertebrae, what is the ruling? The dilemma stands unresolved (teiku).

sub.desc_en: Rabba bar bar Chanah states that the remnant location for the spinal column is the heads of the vertebrae (ראשי פרקים).

sub.text: Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai
sub.text_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos, citing Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai, states that the remnant location is the place of the navel (מקום טיבורו).

sub.text: Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael's dilemma
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael's dilemma
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yannai bar Rabbi Yishmael raises an unresolved dilemma: if the place of the spine, the place of the navel, or the heads of the vertebrae were removed but all else remains, what is the ruling?
The Gemara concludes that the dilemma stands unresolved (תיקו).

items.text: עור בית הפרסות בגלודה – מחלוקת רב ורבי יוחנן
items.text_en: Does the skin of the house of the hooves protect in gludah?
items.desc_en: Rav says: All skin protects in gludah except the skin of the house of the hooves. Rabbi Yochanan says: Even the skin of the house of the hooves protects. Rabbi Assi asked Rabbi Yochanan: Does the skin of the house of the hooves protect? He said: It protects. Rabbi Assi challenged: Did you not teach us that these whose skins are like their flesh include the skin of the house of the hooves? Rabbi Yochanan replied: Do not provoke me, for I teach it as an individual opinion.
items.desc: רב אמר: כל העור מציל בגלודה חוץ מעור בית הפרסות. רבי יוחנן אמר: אפילו עור בית הפרסות מציל. רבי אסי שאל את רבי יוחנן, והשיב שמציל. רבי אסי הקשה מברייתא שאלו שעורותיהן כבשרן, ורבי יוחנן ביקש שלא יקניטנו כי הוא שונה אותה ביחיד.

sub.desc_en: Rav states that all skin protects in gludah except the skin of the house of the hooves.
sub.desc: רב פותח וקובע שכל העור מציל בגלודה חוץ מעור בית הפרסות.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan counters that even the skin of the house of the hooves protects.
sub.desc: רב פותח וקובע שכל העור מציל בגלודה חוץ מעור בית הפרסות.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Assi asks Rabbi Yochanan whether the skin of the house of the hooves protects in gludah.
sub.desc: רבי אסי שואל את רבי יוחנן אם עור בית הפרסות מציל בגלודה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan answers that it does protect.
sub.desc: רבי אסי שואל את רבי יוחנן אם עור בית הפרסות מציל בגלודה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Assi challenges Rabbi Yochanan by citing a baraita that lists the skin of the house of the hooves among those whose skins are like their flesh.
sub.desc: רבי אסי שואל את רבי יוחנן אם עור בית הפרסות מציל בגלודה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan warns Rabbi Assi not to provoke him, explaining that he teaches the baraita as an individual opinion.
sub.desc: רבי אסי שואל את רבי יוחנן אם עור בית הפרסות מציל בגלודה.

items.text: ברייתא על עור תחת האליה ועורות שכבשרן
items.text_en: Supporting baraisa about skins that are like flesh
items.desc_en: A baraisa is cited: One who slaughters an olah to burn a kezayit from the skin under the tail outside its place is invalid but not liable to karet; outside its time is piggul and liable to karet. Eliezer ben Yehuda of Eivlayim in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, and similarly Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of Kfar Ichus in the name of Rabbi Shimon, say: The skin of the house of the hooves, the skin of the head of a tender calf, the skin under the tail, and all that the Sages listed regarding impurity – these are skins that are like their flesh.
items.desc: תניא: השוחט עולה להקטיר כזית מעור תחת האליה – דיני פיגול. אליעזר בן יהודה ורבי שמעון בן יהודה מוסיפים: עור בית הפרסות, עור ראש עגל הרך, ועור תחת האליה – אלו שעורותיהן כבשרן.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited: One who slaughters an olah to burn a kezayit from the skin under the tail outside its place is invalid but not liable to karet; outside its time is piggul and liable to karet.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בדין השוחט עולה להקטיר כזית מעור תחת האליה, ומבחינה בין פיגול לשאר פסולים.

sub.text: אליעזר בן יהודה ורבי שמעון בן יהודה
sub.text_en: Eliezer ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon
sub.desc_en: Eliezer ben Yehuda of Eivlayim in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, and similarly Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of Kfar Ichus in the name of Rabbi Shimon, list the skins that are like their flesh: the skin of the house of the hooves, the skin of the head of a tender calf, the skin under the tail, and all that the Sages listed regarding impurity.
sub.desc: אליעזר בן יהודה ורבי שמעון בן יהודה מוסיפים בשם רבי יעקב ורבי שמעון את רשימת העורות הנחשבים כבשר, הכוללת עור בית הפרסות, עור ראש עגל הרך, ועור תחת האליה.

items.text: פתיחת המשנה: טרפות העוף
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah: Treifot in birds
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists the signs of treifot in birds, including a weasel's bite on the head, perforation of the crop or intestines, and a fall into fire. It also discusses the case of a bird that was trampled or crushed and then slaughtered after a day.
items.desc: הקטע הראשון הוא המשנה המפרטת את סוגי הטרפות בעוף, כולל נקב הוושט, פסוקת הגרגרת, מכה בראש מחולדה, נקב בקורקבן ובמעיים, נפילה לאש, דריסה וריצוץ.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah lists the signs of treifot in birds, including a weasel's bite on the head, perforation of the crop or intestines, and a fall into fire; it also discusses the case of a bird that was trampled or crushed and then slaughtered after a day.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת הטרפות בעוף, ומפרטת את הסימנים לפסול או לכשרות.

items.text: Gemara: Rav, Shmuel, and Levi on checking the wound
items.text_en: Gemara: Rav, Shmuel, and Levi on checking the wound
items.desc_en: Rav, Shmuel, and Levi state that one inserts a hand inside and checks: if blood bubbles up, it is a treifa; otherwise, it is kosher. The Gemara questions this based on a dispute about whether the inner membrane must be perforated, and resolves that if the outer membrane is perforated, the inner one will burst due to its softness.

sub.desc_en: Rav, Shmuel, and Levi state the method for checking a wound: insert the hand and see if blood bubbles up — if so, it is a treifa; otherwise, it is kosher.

The Gemara questions the check: according to the opinion that only the inner membrane must be perforated, the test works; but according to the opinion that the outer membrane alone suffices, why not worry that the outer is perforated while the inner is not?
The Gemara answers: if the outer membrane were perforated, the inner one, due to its softness, would burst, so the test remains valid.

items.text: Ze'iri: No checking for a weasel bite
items.text_en: Ze'iri: No checking for a weasel bite
items.desc_en: Ze'iri states that there is no checking for a weasel bite because its teeth are thin. Rav Oshaya adds that the teeth are both thin and curved, making detection impossible.

sub.desc_en: Ze'iri states that there is no checking for a weasel bite because its teeth are thin.
The Gemara questions why thin teeth alone would preclude checking.
Rav Oshaya answers that the teeth are both thin and curved, making detection impossible.

items.text: Retraction and dispute about checking method
items.text_en: Retraction and dispute about checking method
items.desc_en: When Ze'iri went to Nehardea, he sent a message retracting his earlier statement, reporting that Reish Lakish said one checks with the hand but not with a nail, while Rabbi Yochanan said even with a nail. The Gemara connects this to a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya about checking with hand versus needle, with each criticizing the other's method.

sub.desc_en: Ze'iri, upon arriving in Nehardea, sends a message retracting his earlier statement about checking for a weasel bite.

sub.text: Ze'iri's report of Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan
sub.text_en: Ze'iri's report of Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan
sub.desc_en: Ze'iri reports that Reish Lakish said one checks with the hand but not with a nail, while Rabbi Yochanan permits even a nail.

sub.text: Gemara's connection to a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya
sub.text_en: Gemara's connection to a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya
sub.desc_en: The Gemara connects this dispute to a parallel disagreement between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya about checking with hand versus needle, each criticizing the other's method.

items.text: Clarification and identification of Rabbi Yehuda's position
items.text_en: Clarification and identification of Rabbi Yehuda's position
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the term 'neveilot' since the bird is slaughtered, and corrects it to 'treifot' due to possible perforation of the brain membrane. It then concludes that Rabbi Yehuda is the one who checks with the hand, citing a baraita where Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in his name that one checks with the hand but not with a nail.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects to the term 'neveilot' (carcasses) since the bird was properly slaughtered.
The Gemara corrects the term to 'treifot' (torn animals), explaining that the concern is a possible perforation of the brain membrane.
The Gemara concludes that Rabbi Yehuda is the one who checks with the hand, citing a baraita where Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in his name that one checks with the hand but not with a nail.

items.text: Contradiction in the baraita resolved
items.text_en: Contradiction in the baraita resolved
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes a contradiction in the baraita: it first says one checks with the hand, implying checking is possible, but then says if the bone is broken even without membrane perforation, it is a treifa, implying no checking. It resolves that the latter case refers to a water bird, whose membrane is soft.

sub.desc_en: Gemara's answer: That hen at Rav Chana's, sent to Rav Matna. Bone broke without brain membrane perforation — he koshered it. He said: Levi teaches: treifot listed for animals correspond for birds, plus bird — broken bone even without membrane perforation! He said: there for waterfowl, having no membrane. No membrane? Rather say: because its membrane is soft.

items.text: מעשה בתרנגולת ושאלת רב נחמן
items.text_en: Rav Nachman and Rav Anan: Dispute about checking method
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman tells Rav Anan that both Shmuel and Rav check with the hand and declare kosher, but Levi's baraita lists a broken bone without membrane perforation as a treifa. Rav Anan resolves that this applies only to a water bird with a soft membrane. A similar case of a hen from Rav Chana's house is brought, where Rav Matna declared it kosher, and the same resolution is given.
items.desc: רב נחמן שואל את רב ענן על שיטת שמואל ורב, ומביא ברייתא של לוי הסותרת לכאורה. רב ענן מתרץ שמדובר בעוף מים. בהמשך, מעשה בתרנגולת שנשבר עצמה והכשירה רב מתנה, ושוב מתרצים בעוף מים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman tells Rav Anan that both Shmuel and Rav check with the hand and declare kosher.
sub.desc: רב נחמן מקשה על רב ענן מברייתא של לוי הסותרת לכאורה את שיטת שמואל ורב המכשירים בשבירת עצם.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman objects by citing Levi's baraita that lists a broken bone without membrane perforation as a treifa.
sub.desc: רב ענן מתרץ שהברייתא עוסקת בעוף מים שאין לו קרום, ולכן אינו סותר את דברי שמואל ורב.

sub.desc_en: Rav Anan answers that the baraita applies only to a water bird, which has no membrane.
sub.desc: רב נחמן מקשה על רב ענן מברייתא של לוי הסותרת לכאורה את שיטת שמואל ורב המכשירים בשבירת עצם.

sub.desc_en: The gemara rejects the idea that a water bird has no membrane at all.
sub.desc: רב ענן מתרץ שהברייתא עוסקת בעוף מים שאין לו קרום, ולכן אינו סותר את דברי שמואל ורב.

sub.desc_en: Rav Anan resolves that the baraita refers to a water bird whose membrane is soft.
sub.desc: רב נחמן מקשה על רב ענן מברייתא של לוי הסותרת לכאורה את שיטת שמואל ורב המכשירים בשבירת עצם.

items.text: שיטות בדיקה נוספות: שמשא, מיא, וכו'
items.text_en: Various methods of checking
items.desc_en: The Gemara records that Rav Sheizvi checks in the sun, Rav Yeimar checks in water, and Rav Acha bar Yaakov checks... (the text is cut off).
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה שיטות בדיקה שונות: רב שיזבי בודק בשמש, רב יימר במים, ורב אחא בר יעקב בודק בדרך אחרת (הקטע נקטע).

sub.text_en: Rav Sheizvi, Rav Yeimar, Rav Acha bar Yaakov
sub.desc_en: Rav Sheizvi checks in sun, Rav Yeimar checks in water, Rav Acha bar Yaakov checks (text cut off).
sub.desc: רב שיזבי מציע שיטת בדיקה בשמש.

items.text: פתיחת הסוגיה: גילא דחיטתא
items.text_en: Opening statement about geese
items.desc_en: Rav Sheizvi states that their geese are like waterfowl, implying a leniency regarding their kashrut status.
items.desc: פתיחה קצרה העוסקת בגילא דחיטתא, כנראה הקדמה לדיון על שינויי צבע.

sub.desc_en: The gemara opens with a brief phrase about wheat bran, setting the context for the discussion about geese.
sub.desc: פותח בביטוי 'גילא דחיטתא' כהקדמה לדיון על שינויי צבע.

items.text: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling on green discoloration from fire
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling on green discoloration from fire
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua rules that if a bird fell into fire, the measure of its green discoloration is like the measure of its perforation – minimal, i.e., any green color renders it tereifah.

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheizvi states that our geese are comparable to waterfowl.

sub.text: Rabbi Yochanan citing Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan citing Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua rules that for a bird that fell into fire, the measure of its green discoloration is like the measure of its perforation – minimal, i.e., any green color renders it tereifah.

items.text: Inquiry about green liver opposite the intestines
items.text_en: Inquiry about green liver opposite the intestines
items.desc_en: Rav Yosef asks Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi whether a liver that turned green opposite the intestines is tereifah. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi rules it is tereifah, and Rava explains that such greenness indicates the bird fell into fire and the intestines were burned.

sub.text: Rav Yosef son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's question
sub.text_en: Rav Yosef son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's question
sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, asks his father whether a liver that turned green opposite the intestines renders the animal a טריפה (torn animal).
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi answers that it is a טריפה (torn animal).
Rav Yosef objects: even if the liver were entirely removed, the animal would be kosher, so why is green discoloration worse?
Rava resolves that green discoloration of the liver opposite the intestines indicates the animal fell into fire, which compromised the intestines, making it a טריפה (torn animal).

items.text: מעשה בתרנגולת עם ירוקין
items.text_en: Case of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's hen and the distinction of organs
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi sent a hen with green spots to Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, who declared it kosher. The Gemara clarifies that the mishnah's rule 'green ones are invalid' applies only to the gizzard, heart, and liver, not to other organs.
items.desc: רבי יהושע בן לוי שלח תרנגולת לרבי אלעזר הקפר, שהכשירה למרות שהיו בה ירוקין, תוך הגבלה ש'ירוקין פסולין' נאמר רק בקורקבן, לב וכבד, ומביא ברייתא תומכת.

sub.text_en: Story of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rabbi Elazar HaKappar
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi sent a hen to Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, who saw green discoloration but declared it kosher.
sub.desc: רבי יהושע בן לוי שלח תרנגולת לרבי אלעזר הקפר, שהכשירה למרות שהיו בה ירוקין.

sub.desc_en: The gemara objects: we learned in a mishnah that green (discolored) organs are invalid.
sub.desc: רבי יהושע בן לוי שלח תרנגולת לרבי אלעזר הקפר, שהכשירה למרות שהיו בה ירוקין.

sub.desc_en: The gemara answers that the rule of green organs being invalid applies only to the gizzard, heart, and liver, not to the intestines.
sub.desc: רבי יהושע בן לוי שלח תרנגולת לרבי אלעזר הקפר, שהכשירה למרות שהיו בה ירוקין.

sub.desc_en: A baraita supports this distinction, stating that the rule about green organs applies only to the gizzard, heart, and liver.
sub.desc: רבי יהושע בן לוי שלח תרנגולת לרבי אלעזר הקפר, שהכשירה למרות שהיו בה ירוקין.

items.text: מעשה בתרנגולת עם אדומין
items.text_en: Case of Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef's hen and red discoloration
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef sent a hen with red spots to Rabbi Avahu, who ruled it tereifah. The Gemara explains that red spots that turned green or green that turned red are tereifah, and the mishnah's leniency applies only to the gizzard, heart, and liver.
items.desc: רבי יצחק בר יוסף שלח תרנגולת לרבי אבהו, שטרפה בגלל אדמימות, תוך הבהרה ש'אדומין כשרים' נאמר רק בלב, קורקבן וכבד, אך אדומין שהוריקו או ירוקין שהאדימו טריפה.

sub.text_en: Story of Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef and Rabbi Avahu
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef sent a hen to Rabbi Avahu, who saw red discoloration and declared it a טריפה (torn animal).
sub.desc: רבי יצחק בר יוסף שלח תרנגולת לרבי אבהו וטען שהיא טריפה בגלל אדמימות.

sub.desc_en: The gemara objects: we learned in a mishnah that red organs are kosher.
sub.desc: רבי יצחק בר יוסף שלח תרנגולת לרבי אבהו וטען שהיא טריפה בגלל אדמימות.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Avahu answers that red organs that turned green or green organs that turned red are a טריפה (torn animal), and the rule of red being kosher applies only to the heart, gizzard, and liver.
sub.desc: רבי יצחק בר יוסף שלח תרנגולת לרבי אבהו וטען שהיא טריפה בגלל אדמימות.

items.text: דין אדומין שהוריקו וחזרו והאדימו
items.text_en: Rav Shmuel bar Chiya and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak on boiling and color change
items.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Chiya in the name of Rabbi Mani rules that if red spots turned green but returned to red after boiling, they are kosher because smoke entered them. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak adds that if red spots that never turned green become green after boiling, they are tereifah because their shame is revealed. Rav Ashi concludes one should only eat after boiling, but we do not assume a prior defect.
items.desc: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני מכשיר אדומין שהוריקו, שלקו וחזרו והאדימו, כי קוטרא עייל בהו. רב נחמן בר יצחק טורף אדומין שלא הוריקו, שלקו והוריקו, כי איגלאי בהתייהו. רב אשי פוסק לאכול רק בשלקא, אך מסייג שאין מחזיקים ריעותא.

sub.text: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני
sub.text_en: Rav Shmuel bar Chiya citing Rabbi Mani
sub.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Chiya in the name of Rabbi Mani rules that red organs that turned green but returned to red after cooking are kosher, because smoke entered them (causing the temporary green).
sub.desc: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני פוסק שאדומין שהוריקו וחזרו והאדימו כשרים, ומסביר שהסיבה היא שהעשן נכנס בהם.

sub.text: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak adds that red organs that never turned green but turned green after cooking are a טריפה (torn animal), because their defect was revealed.
sub.desc: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני פוסק שאדומין שהוריקו וחזרו והאדימו כשרים, ומסביר שהסיבה היא שהעשן נכנס בהם.

sub.text: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני
sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi rules that one should only eat fowl after cooking (boiling) to check for hidden defects.
sub.desc: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני פוסק שאדומין שהוריקו וחזרו והאדימו כשרים, ומסביר שהסיבה היא שהעשן נכנס בהם.

sub.text: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני
sub.desc_en: The gemara rejects Rav Ashi's ruling, stating that we do not presume a defect (without evidence).
sub.desc: רב שמואל בר חייא בשם רבי מני פוסק שאדומין שהוריקו וחזרו והאדימו כשרים, ומסביר שהסיבה היא שהעשן נכנס בהם.

items.text: דין דרסה וטריפה בכותל
items.text_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos on trampling and striking against a wall
items.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antignos in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai rules that both cases (trampling and striking against a wall) require examination.
items.desc: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס בשם רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי קובע שדרסה וטריפה בכותל, בין במקרה זה ובין במקרה אחר, צריכה בדיקה.

sub.text: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס בשם רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי
sub.text_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonos citing Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonos, in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yannai, rules that both a fowl that was trampled and one that was struck against a wall require examination.
sub.desc: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס בשם רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי קובע שדרסה וטריפה בכותל, בין במקרה זה ובין במקרה אחר, צריכה בדיקה.

items.text: משנה: אלו כשרות בעוף
items.text_en: Mishnah: Which defects are kosher in birds
items.desc_en: The mishnah lists defects that are kosher in birds: a perforated or cracked windpipe, a weasel's bite on the head that does not render it tereifah, a perforated crop (Rabbi says even if removed), intestines that came out but were not perforated, broken wings or legs, and plucked feathers (Rabbi Yehuda says if the down is removed it is invalid).
items.desc: המשנה מונה מקרים שבעוף כשרים: ניקבה הגרגרת או נסדקה, הכתה חולדה על ראשה במקום שאינו עושה אותה טריפה, ניקב הזפק (ורבי אומר אפילו ניטל), יצאו בני מעיה ולא ניקבו, נשברו גפיה ורגליה, נמרטו כנפיה (ורבי יהודה פוסל אם ניטלה הנוצה).

sub.desc_en: The mishnah lists cases where a fowl is kosher: perforation or cracking of the trachea, etc.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah continues: a weasel struck its head in a place that does not render it a טריפה (torn animal), or the crop was perforated.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) says: even if the crop was entirely removed, the fowl is kosher.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah continues: its intestines came out but were not perforated, its wings were broken, its legs were broken.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah continues: its feathers were plucked.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehuda says: if the down feather was removed, the fowl is invalid.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת המקרים שבעוף כשרים, הכוללת ניקב הגרגרת, נסדקה, הכאת חולדה, ניקב הזפק, יציאת בני מעיים, שבירת גפיים ורגליים ומריטת כנפיים.

items.text: גמרא: מעשה בהוראת טרפחת כרבי בזפק
items.text_en: Gemara: Precedent of Rabbi Simai and Rabbi Tzadok regarding the crop
items.desc_en: A baraisa recounts that Rabbi Simai and Rabbi Tzadok went to intercalate the year in Lod and stayed in Ono, where they ruled regarding the tarpechach (crop) like Rabbi (who permits even if removed). The Gemara questions whether they ruled leniently on the tarpechach like Rabbi on the crop, or only on the tarpechach but not on the crop itself. The question remains unresolved (teiku).
items.desc: תנו רבנן: מעשה ברבי סימאי ורבי צדוק שהורו בטרפחת כרבי בזפק. נשאלה שאלה: האם הורו בטרפחת לאיסור כרבי בזפק להיתר, או להיתר כרבי בזפק? תיקו.

sub.desc_en: A baraisa recounts that Rabbi Simai and Rabbi Tzadok, while on a mission to intercalate the year, ruled regarding the tarpechach (crop) like Rabbi's lenient position on the crop (זפק).
sub.desc: הברייתא מביאה מעשה שבו רבי סימאי ורבי צדוק הורו בטרפחת כדעת רבי בזפק.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an unresolved question: did they rule leniently on the tarpechach like Rabbi on the crop, or only on the tarpechach but not on the crop itself?
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה ספק: האם הורו בטרפחת לאיסור כרבי בזפק להיתר, או להיתר כרבי בזפק?

sub.desc_en: The question remains unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה ספק: האם הורו בטרפחת לאיסור כרבי בזפק להיתר, או להיתר כרבי בזפק?

items.text: דין גגו של זפק
items.text_en: Rabbah on the roof of the crop
items.desc_en: Rabbah (or Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi) states that the roof of the crop is judged like the esophagus. Rav Bibi bar Abaye clarifies: any part that stretches with it.
items.desc: רבה (או רבי יהושע בן לוי) אומר שגגו של זפק נידון כוושט. רב ביבי בר אביי מבאר: כל שנמתח עמו.

sub.desc_en: Rabba (or alternatively Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi) states that the roof of the crop is judged like the esophagus.
sub.desc: רבה (או רבי יהושע בן לוי) קובע שגגו של זפק דינו כוושט.

sub.desc_en: The gemara asks: where (which part of the crop is considered like the esophagus)?
sub.desc: רבה (או רבי יהושע בן לוי) קובע שגגו של זפק דינו כוושט.

sub.desc_en: Rav Beivai bar Abaye answers: any part that stretches with it (the esophagus) is considered like the esophagus.
sub.desc: רבה (או רבי יהושע בן לוי) קובע שגגו של זפק דינו כוושט.

items.text: דין יצאו בני מעיה והפך בהם
items.text_en: Intestines that came out: turning them over
items.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak rules that the mishnah's leniency applies only if one did not turn the intestines over, but if turned over, it is tereifah, citing the verse 'He made you and established you' to teach that God created supports in man such that if any is reversed, one cannot live. A baraisa adds that Rabbi Meir expounded the same verse to refer to the body as a container for all, from which come priests, prophets, officers, and kings.
items.desc: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק מפרש שיצאו בני מעיה כשרים רק אם לא הפך בהם, אך אם הפך בהם טריפה, על פי הפסוק 'הוא עשך ויכוננך'. ברייתא מוסיפה דרשת רבי מאיר על הפסוק.

sub.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak rules that the mishnah's leniency for intestines that came out applies only if one did not turn them over; if turned over, it is a טריפה (terefah), citing the verse 'הוּא עָשְׂךָ וַיְכֹנְנֶךָ' to teach that God created supports in man that if any is reversed, one cannot live.
sub.desc: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק מבחין בין יציאת בני מעיים בלא הפיכה, שכשרה, לבין הפיכתם, שהופכת את הבהמה לטריפה, ומביא ראיה מהפסוק 'הוא עשך ויכוננך' המלמד על כונניות בגוף האדם.

sub.desc_en: A baraita adds that Rabbi Meir expounded the same verse to refer to the body as a container for all, from which come priests, prophets, officers, and kings.
sub.desc: ברייתא מביאה דרשת רבי מאיר על הפסוק 'הוא עשך ויכוננך', המפרש את הכונניות ככרכה הכוללת בתוכה כהנים, נביאים, שרים ומלכים, ומחזקת את דברי רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק.

items.text: מעשה ברומאה ובנפל מאיגרא
items.text_en: Story of a Roman who saw a man fall from a roof
items.desc_en: A Roman saw a man fall from a roof, his stomach burst and intestines came out; he brought his son and slaughtered the animal before him (the story is incomplete, likely illustrating a point about tereifah).
items.desc: סיפור על רומאי שראה אדם שנפל מגג, בקע כריסו ויצאו מעיו, והביא בנו ושחטו לפניו.

sub.text_en: Story of a Roman and a man who fell
sub.desc_en: A story is told of a Roman who saw a man fall from a roof, his belly split and intestines came out; the Roman brought his son and slaughtered the animal in front of him.
sub.desc: מביא סיפור על רומאי שראה אדם שנפל מגג, בקע כריסו ויצאו מעיו, והביא בנו ושחטו לפניו.

items.text: Opening anecdote about a bird with a dislocated leg
items.text_en: Opening anecdote about a bird with a dislocated leg
items.desc_en: A story is told of a bird whose leg was dislocated; the wound was stitched to its stomach, and it was deemed kosher. This sets the stage for the discussion on dislocated limbs.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara recounts a story of a bird whose leg was dislocated, its wound stitched to its stomach, and it was deemed kosher.

items.text: Rava's ruling on a bird with broken legs
items.text_en: Rava's ruling on a bird with broken legs
items.desc_en: A basket of birds with broken legs came before Rava; he examined the צומת הגידין (the sinew junction) and declared them kosher.

sub.desc_en: A basket of birds with broken legs came before Rava; he examined the צומת הגידין (sinew junction) and declared them kosher.

items.text: Rav and Shmuel's rulings on dislocated limbs
items.text_en: Rav and Shmuel's rulings on dislocated limbs
items.desc_en: Rav rules that a dislocated foreleg in an animal is kosher, but a dislocated thigh in an animal or bird is a treifah, and a dislocated wing in a bird is a treifah due to concern for lung puncture. Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan say it must be examined.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda reports Rav's rulings: a dislocated foreleg in an animal is kosher, but a dislocated thigh in an animal or bird is a treifah, and a dislocated wing in a bird is a treifah due to concern for lung puncture.
Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan rule that the animal must be examined (rather than automatically declared a treifah).

items.text: Dispute about the bird's lung
items.text_en: Dispute about the bird's lung
items.desc_en: Chizkiyah says a bird has no lung (i.e., it does not render it treifah), while Rabbi Yochanan says it does, located like a rose leaf between the wings. The Gemara clarifies that Chizkiyah means the lung does not fall out or become forbidden, because the ribs protect it.

sub.desc_en: Chizkiyah states that a bird has no lung (i.e., it does not render the bird a treifah), while Rabbi Yochanan says it does, located like a rose leaf between the wings.
The Gemara asks what Chizkiyah means by 'a bird has no lung' — does he mean it has no lung at all, which is contradicted by observation?
The Gemara answers that Chizkiyah means the lung does not render the bird a treifah, and cites a baraita of Levi listing treifot in animals and birds.
The Gemara concludes that Chizkiyah means the lung does not fall out or become forbidden, and Rav Chanah explains the reason: most of the ribs protect it.

items.text: Critique of Chizkiyah's view
items.text_en: Critique of Chizkiyah's view
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that Rabbi Yochanan's statement implies Chizkiyah thought there is no lung at all, but the Western sages say in the name of Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Chanina that from Chizkiyah's words it is clear he was not expert in chickens.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers from Rabbi Yochanan's statement that Chizkiyah must have held there is no lung at all.

sub.text: Western sages in the name of Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Chanina
sub.text_en: Western sages in the name of Rabbi Yosi bar Rabbi Chanina
sub.desc_en: The Western sages resolve that from Chizkiyah's own words it is clear he was not expert in chickens, explaining his unusual view.

items.text: Rav Huna's ruling and contradiction with Rav
items.text_en: Rav Huna's ruling and contradiction with Rav
items.desc_en: Rav Huna reports that Rav ruled a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher. His son Rabbah bar Rav Huna objects, citing Rav Yehudah in Rav's name that it is treifah. Rav Huna responds that each river has its own course (i.e., different traditions).

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna reports that Rav ruled a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.
Rabbah bar Rav Huna objects, citing a tradition from Rav Yehudah in Rav's name that a dislocated thigh in a bird is treifah.
Rav Huna responds that each river has its own course, meaning different traditions exist.

items.text: Rabbi Abba's encounter and resolution of the contradiction
items.text_en: Rabbi Abba's encounter and resolution of the contradiction
items.desc_en: Rabbi Abba finds Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba examining the sinew junction and questions him, citing Rav Huna's lenient ruling. Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba cites a Mishnah and Rav's ruling that a cut below the knee is kosher, above is invalid, and similarly for birds. Rabbi Abba then distinguishes between a dislocated (שמוטה) and a cut (חתוכה) limb, resolving the contradiction.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba finds Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba examining the sinew junction (צומת הגידין).
Rabbi Abba questions why Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba is being so thorough, citing Rav Huna's ruling that a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher (כשרה).

Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba cites a Mishnah that an animal whose legs are cut below the knee is kosher, above is invalid, and similarly for the sinew junction, and Rav's extension that the same applies to birds.
The gemara notes that this creates a contradiction between Rav's two rulings (Rav Huna's lenient one and Rav's strict one), and Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba falls silent.

Rabbi Abba resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between a dislocated limb (שמוטה) and a cut limb (חתוכה), citing Rav's explicit statement that a dislocated limb is kosher and a cut limb is invalid, with the analogy that cutting in one place kills and in another does not.

items.text: Rabbi Zeira's conflicting report
items.text_en: Rabbi Zeira's conflicting report
items.desc_en: When Rabbi Abba ascended to Eretz Yisrael, he found Rabbi Zeira teaching that Rav Huna said in Rav's name that a dislocated thigh in a bird is treifah. Rabbi Abba challenges him, but the text is cut off.

sub.desc_en: When Rabbi Abba ascended to Eretz Yisrael, he found Rabbi Zeira teaching that Rav Huna said in Rav's name that a dislocated thigh in a bird is treifah, and Rabbi Abba challenges him, but the text is cut off.

items.text: Rav Huna's ruling on שמוטת ירך
items.text_en: Rav Huna's ruling on שמוטת ירך
items.desc_en: Rav Huna is asked about a bird with a dislocated thigh and rules it is kosher.

sub.desc_en: The narrator reports that they had an opening before Rav Huna, asked him about a bird with a dislocated thigh, and he ruled it is kosher.

items.text: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba's challenge and resolution
items.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba's challenge and resolution
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba is found examining the sciatic nerve and is challenged about Rav Huna's ruling. He cites a Mishnah and Rav's statement that a cut leg below the knee is kosher, but above is invalid, and Rav applies this to birds. The Gemara questions a contradiction in Rav's statements, and Rabbi Yirmeya clarifies that Rav distinguished between a dislocation (kosher) and a cut (invalid).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara recounts finding Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba examining the sciatic nerve and challenging him with Rav Huna's ruling that a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba responds by citing a Mishnah about a cut leg below the knee being kosher and above being invalid, and Rav's extension of this rule to birds.
The Gemara objects that Rav's statements contradict each other, and Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba is silent.
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba resolves the contradiction by clarifying that Rav distinguished between a dislocation (kosher) and a cut (invalid).

items.text: Conflicting traditions from Rav and Rabbi Yochanan
items.text_en: Conflicting traditions from Rav and Rabbi Yochanan
items.desc_en: The Gemara presents conflicting traditions: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi in the name of Rav and Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi in the name of Rabbi Yochanan both rule that a dislocated thigh is treifah. Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi adds that if Rabbi Yochanan had been in a place where colleagues permitted it, he would not have objected, citing a story where Rabbi Chanina brought a hen with a dislocated thigh to Rabbi, who permitted it.

sub.text: Gemara's question to Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi
sub.text_en: Gemara's question to Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi
sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi what he holds, and he cites conflicting traditions from Rav and Rabbi Yochanan that a dislocated thigh in a bird is טריפה (a terminal condition).

sub.text: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi's qualification and story
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi's qualification and story
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi adds that Rabbi Yochanan would not have objected if colleagues permitted it, citing a story where Rabbi Chanina brought a hen with a dislocated thigh to Rabbi, who permitted it, and Rabbi Chanina salted it and taught the ruling to students.

items.text: The halakha is established via Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
items.text_en: The halakha is established via Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
items.desc_en: The Gemara rejects all previous traditions and establishes the halakha based on a question from Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi about a perforated windpipe. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi cites a Mishnah, but Rabbi Yosei brings a counterexample of a sheep that survived. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi dismisses this, citing a widespread halakha that a dislocated thigh is treifah, and explains that the sheep survived only within twelve months.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara rejects all previous traditions and establishes the halakha based on a question from Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi about a perforated windpipe.
Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai asks Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi about the minimum size of a perforation in the windpipe that renders an animal a treifah.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi cites a Mishnah that the perforation must be as large as an Italian issar coin.
Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai objects with a counterexample of a sheep whose perforated windpipe was repaired with reed membranes and survived.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi dismisses the counterexample, citing a widespread halakha that a dislocated thigh is treifah, and explains that the sheep survived only within twelve months.

items.text: Story of Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta and the hen
items.text_en: Story of Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta and the hen
items.desc_en: The Gemara relates that Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta was engaged in other matters and did something to refute Rabbi Yehudah, who said that if the feather is removed the bird is invalid. Rabbi Shimon had a hen whose feather was removed; he placed it in an oven and covered it with a patch of Tarsian cloth, and its later wings grew larger than the first ones. The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Yehudah holds that a treifah improves, and if so, why would the later wings grow larger?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces a story about Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta, who acted to refute Rabbi Yehudah's ruling that a bird whose feather is removed is invalid.
The story details that Rabbi Shimon placed the hen in an oven, covered it with a patch of Tarsian cloth, and its later wings grew larger than the first ones.
The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Yehudah holds that a טריפה (ritually unfit animal) improves, and if so, why would the later wings grow larger than the first ones.

items.text: Explanation of 'engaged in other matters' and the ant story
items.text_en: Explanation of 'engaged in other matters' and the ant story
items.desc_en: Rav Mesharshiya explains that Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta was engaged in verifying the verse about the ant having no ruler. He went in the summer, spread his cloak over an anthill, and when an ant marked it, he moved the cloak, causing the ants to kill the marker. He concluded they have no king. Rav Acha bar Rava challenges this, suggesting they might have a king or a decree, but concludes to rely on Solomon's reliability.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what 'engaged in other matters' refers to in the context of Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta.
Rav Mesharshiya explains that Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta was verifying the verse about the ant having no ruler, and decided to test whether ants truly have no king.

The Gemara recounts how Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta spread his cloak over an anthill in summer, and when an ant marked it, he moved the cloak causing the ants to kill the marker, concluding they have no king.
Rav Acha bar Rava challenges the conclusion, suggesting the ants might have had a king present or a royal decree, or that the incident occurred during an interregnum.

sub.text: Resolution by Rav Acha bar Rava
sub.text_en: Resolution by Rav Acha bar Rava
sub.desc_en: Rav Acha bar Rava resolves that despite the objections, one should rely on the reliability of King Solomon's statement that ants have no ruler.

items.text: Signs of a treifah and the twelve-month rule
items.text_en: Signs of a treifah and the twelve-month rule
items.desc_en: Rav Huna states that the sign of a treifah is twelve months. The Gemara challenges this with a baraita that gives different signs: not giving birth, improving (kosher), or deteriorating (treifah). Rabbi says the sign is thirty days, but the Sages object that many survive two or three years. The Gemara then cites a Tannaitic dispute about a skull with a hole, where Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam brings a case of survival, but Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar dismisses it as happening in summer.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna states that the sign of a treifah (animal with a fatal condition) is that it lives no more than twelve months.

The Gemara challenges Rav Huna by citing a baraita that gives different signs for a treifah: inability to give birth, or improvement indicating kosher status, or deterioration indicating treifah status.
Rabbi (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi) offers a different sign: a treifah lives only thirty days.
The Sages object to Rabbi's thirty-day rule, noting that many treifot survive two or three years.

The Gemara cites a Tannaitic dispute about a skull with a hole: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshulam brings a case of survival, but Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar dismisses it as happening in summer, so the animal died when winter came.

items.text: Final ruling: a treifah gives birth and improves
items.text_en: Final ruling: a treifah gives birth and improves
items.desc_en: Rav Acha bar Yaakov rules that a treifah gives birth and improves. Amemar adds that eggs of a treifah are... (the text is cut off).

sub.desc_en: Rav Acha bar Yaakov rules that a טריפה (animal with a fatal defect) gives birth and improves, establishing the final הלכה (binding law).
Amemar adds that the eggs of a טריפה are... (the text is cut off, but the move extends the ruling to eggs).

items.text: Amemar's initial ruling on eggs of a tereifah
items.text_en: Amemar's initial ruling on eggs of a tereifah
items.desc_en: Amemar rules that the first egg of a tereifah is forbidden, but subsequent eggs are permitted because they involve a mixture of permitted and forbidden factors (zeh vazeh gorem).

sub.desc_en: Amemar rules that the first egg of a tereifah is forbidden, but subsequent eggs are permitted because they involve a mixture of permitted and forbidden factors (zeh vazeh gorem).

items.text: Rav Ashi's objection and resolution
items.text_en: Rav Ashi's objection and resolution
items.desc_en: Rav Ashi objects from the Mishnah that the egg of a tereifah is forbidden because it grew in prohibition. Amemar answers that the Mishnah refers to an egg that was already formed inside the mother (safna me'ara). The Gemara notes that if it were the first egg, the Mishnah should have said 'completed' (gamrah) rather than 'grew' (gadlah).

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi objects by citing a baraita that all eggs of a tereifah are forbidden because they grew in prohibition.
Amemar answers that the baraita refers to an egg that was formed from the ground (i.e., a fully developed egg laid after the animal became a tereifah), not the first egg.
The Gemara objects that Amemar could have answered that the Mishnah refers to the first egg (shichla kama).
The Gemara resolves that if it were the first egg, the Mishnah should have said 'completed' (gamrah) rather than 'grew' (gadlah).

items.text: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on offspring of a tereifah
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on offspring of a tereifah
items.desc_en: The Gemara analyzes the dispute about the offspring of a tereifah that became pregnant before being tereifah. Rabbi Eliezer forbids it as zeh vazeh gorem, while Rabbi Yehoshua permits it. The Gemara questions why they argue about offering it on the altar rather than about ordinary use, and explains that Rabbi Yehoshua's leniency is highlighted.

sub.desc_en: The gemara asks about a Mishnah where Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree about the offspring of a tereifah for the altar, and questions why they argue about altar use rather than ordinary consumption.
The gemara answers that the Mishnah chose the altar case to show the lenient power of Rabbi Yehoshua, who permits even for the altar.
The gemara objects that they could have argued about ordinary consumption to show the stringent power of Rabbi Eliezer.
The gemara resolves that the Mishnah prefers to highlight the lenient power, as leniency is more praiseworthy.
The Gemara answers that the Mishnah chose the altar case to highlight Rabbi Yehoshua's leniency, showing he permits even for sacred use.
The Gemara objects: they could have argued about ordinary use to highlight Rabbi Eliezer's stringency, showing he forbids even for common use.
The Gemara resolves that the Mishnah prefers to showcase the lenient position (כוח דהיתרא עדיף ליה).

items.text: Agreement on egg of a tereifah that was already formed
items.text_en: Agreement on egg of a tereifah that was already formed
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that both Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree that the egg of a tereifah that was already formed inside the mother (safna me'ara) is forbidden, because it is a single cause (chad gorem).

sub.desc_en: The gemara cites a baraita that all agree an egg formed from the ground (fully developed after tereifah) is forbidden because it has only one causative factor.

items.text: Rav Acha's version of Amemar's statement
items.text_en: Rav Acha's version of Amemar's statement
items.desc_en: Rav Acha holds like Rav Acha bar Yaakov and teaches Amemar's statement as previously stated.

sub.desc_en: The gemara reports that Rav Acha holds like Rav Acha bar Yaakov and teaches Amemar's ruling as stated above.

items.text: Ravina's version and Rav Ashi's objection
items.text_en: Ravina's version and Rav Ashi's objection
items.desc_en: Ravina does not hold like Rav Acha bar Yaakov and teaches Amemar's statement in a different version: eggs of a doubtful tereifah are left to see if the hen lays again. Rav Ashi objects from the Mishnah, and Amemar answers that it refers to the first egg, emending the text to 'completed' (gamrah).
