sub.desc_en: A baraita records that Bet Shammai limits covering to dirt alone, while Bet Hillel permits ash because it is called 'dirt' in the verse about the red heifer.
Beit Hillel responds that ash is also called dust, citing the verse 'מעפר שרפת' (from the dust of the burning).
Beit Shammai objects that the verse only calls it 'dust of burning,' not simply 'dust,' so ash is not included in the general term.

items.text: Additional materials added by later authorities
items.text_en: Additional materials added by later authorities
items.desc_en: A baraita states that they added to these materials: black, blue, crushed pottery, and some say also זרניך (a type of mineral).

sub.desc_en: A Tana lists additional materials added (black, blue, crushed limestone, and some say also zarneech).

items.text: Rava's aggadic teaching on Abraham's merit
items.text_en: Rava's aggadic teaching on Abraham's merit
items.desc_en: Rava teaches: In reward for Abraham saying 'ואנכי עפר ואפר' (I am dust and ashes), his children merited two commandments: the ashes of the red heifer and the dust of the sotah. The Gemara asks why not also include the dust of covering blood, and answers that there is no benefit (הנאה) from that mitzvah, only its performance.

sub.desc_en: Rava teaches that in reward for Abraham saying 'ואנכי עפר ואפר' (I am dust and ashes), his children merited two commandments: the ashes of the red heifer and the dust of the sotah.
The Gemara asks why the dust for covering blood is not also included as a third merit.
The Gemara answers that covering blood is only a preparation for the mitzvah (הכשר מצוה) with no benefit (הנאה), so it is not counted.

items.text: Rava's second aggadic teaching (incomplete)
items.text_en: Rava's second aggadic teaching (incomplete)
items.desc_en: Rava begins another teaching: In reward for Abraham saying... (the text cuts off).

sub.desc_en: Rava continues another homily related to Abraham's expression; the daf text is cut off, so the move is truncated.

items.text: שכר חוט התכלת ורצועת התפילין
items.text_en: Opening: The reward of Abraham's humility
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that Abraham's refusal to take even a thread or a shoelace from the king of Sodom earned his descendants two mitzvot: the thread of tekhelet and the strap of tefillin. It then questions what the thread of tekhelet represents, citing Rabbi Meir's teaching that tekhelet resembles the sea, which resembles the firmament, which resembles the sapphire stone, which resembles the Throne of Glory.
items.desc: אברהם אבינו סירב לקחת מחוט ועד שרוך נעל, ובזכות זה זכו בניו לשתי מצוות: חוט תכלת ורצועת תפילין. הגמרא מבארת את מעלת חוט התכלת שדומה לים ולרקיע ולכסא הכבוד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by stating that Abraham's refusal to take even a thread or shoelace earned his descendants the mitzvot of the thread of tekhelet and the strap of tefillin.
sub.desc: פותח בכך שבזכות שאברהם סירב לקחת מחוט ועד שרוך נעל, זכו בניו לשתי מצוות: חוט תכלת ורצועת תפילין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions what the thread of tekhelet represents, noting that the strap of tefillin is explained by a verse and a baraita.
sub.desc: מקשה: מובן שכוחה של רצועת תפילין נובע מהפסוק 'וראו כל עמי הארץ', אבל מה מיוחד בחוט התכלת?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita where Rabbi Meir explains that tekhelet resembles the sea, which resembles the firmament, which resembles the sapphire stone, which resembles the Throne of Glory.
sub.desc: משיב על ידי ברייתא: התכלת דומה לים, ים לרקיע, רקיע לאבן ספיר, ואבן ספיר לכסא הכבוד, ומכאן מעלתו.

items.text: קושי השבת גזל הנאכל
items.text_en: The difficulty of returning stolen food
items.desc_en: Rabbi Abba states that stolen food that has been eaten is particularly difficult to restore, as even completely righteous people cannot return it, citing Abraham's words to the king of Sodom.
items.desc: רבי אבא אומר שקשה להשיב גזל שנאכל, שאפילו צדיקים גמורים כמו אברהם אינם יכולים להחזירו, שנאמר 'בלעדי רק אשר אכלו הנערים'.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba states that stolen food that has been eaten is particularly difficult to restore, as even completely righteous people cannot return it, citing Abraham's words to the king of Sodom.
sub.desc: רבי אבא אומר שקשה להשיב גזל שנאכל, שאפילו צדיקים גמורים כמו אברהם אינם יכולים להחזירו, שנאמר 'בלעדי רק אשר אכלו הנערים'.

items.text: Humility of Israel's leaders vs. arrogance of the nations
items.text_en: Humility of Israel's leaders vs. arrogance of the nations
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon teaches that one should listen carefully to the aggadic teachings of Rabbi Eliezer ben Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. He then explains that God loves Israel because even when granted greatness, they humble themselves, citing Abraham, Moses, Aaron, and David. In contrast, the nations of the world become arrogant when given greatness, as exemplified by Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, and Hiram.

sub.text: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan teaches that one should listen carefully to the aggadic teachings of Rabbi Eliezer ben Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and then explains that God loves Israel because they humble themselves when granted greatness.
The gemara cites examples of Abraham, Moses, Aaron, and David, who humbled themselves when granted greatness by God.
The gemara contrasts the nations of the world, who become arrogant when granted greatness, citing Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, and Hiram.

items.text: The world endures through humility
items.text_en: The world endures through humility
items.desc_en: Rava (or Rabbi Yochanan) states that the praise of Moses and Aaron is greater than that of Abraham, as they said 'and we are nothing' while Abraham said 'dust and ashes'. Rava (or Rabbi Yochanan) further states that the world exists only for the sake of Moses and Aaron, based on a scriptural wordplay. Rabbi Ila'a and Rabbi Avahu then teach that the world endures through those who restrain themselves during conflict or make themselves as nothing.

sub.desc_en: Rava (or Rabbi Yochanan) states that the praise of Moses and Aaron is greater than that of Abraham, because Abraham said 'dust and ashes' while Moses and Aaron said 'and we are nothing'.

Rava (or Rabbi Yochanan) further states that the world exists only for the sake of Moses and Aaron, based on a scriptural wordplay linking 'and we are nothing' (וְנַחְנוּ מָה) to 'He hangs the earth on nothing' (עַל בְּלִימָה).
Rabbi Ila'a teaches that the world endures only for the sake of one who restrains himself (בּוֹלֵם) during conflict, interpreting 'עַל בְּלִימָה' (on nothing) as 'on one who restrains himself'.
Rabbi Avahu teaches that the world endures for one who makes himself as nothing (כְּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ), citing the verse 'וּמִתַּחַת זְרוֹעוֹת עוֹלָם' (and underneath are the everlasting arms).

items.text: The proper balance of silence and speech
items.text_en: The proper balance of silence and speech
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak interprets a verse to teach that a person should make themselves like a mute in worldly matters, but not in matters of Torah, and should not be arrogant.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak asks the meaning of the verse 'האמנם אלם צדק תדברון מישרים תשפטו בני אדם'.
Rabbi Yitzchak interprets that a person's craft in this world is to make themselves like a mute regarding worldly matters.
Rabbi Yitzchak qualifies that one might think this silence applies even to Torah matters, but the verse says 'צדק תדברון' (speak righteousness).
Rabbi Yitzchak further qualifies that one might think to be arrogant, but the verse says 'מישרים תשפטו בני אדם' (judge uprightly, sons of men).

items.text: כיסוי הדם בעפר עיר הנדחת
items.text_en: Using earth from an idolatrous city for covering blood
items.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira (or Rabbah bar Yirmeyah) questions the permissibility of covering blood with earth from an idolatrous city, which is forbidden for benefit. Ze'iri answers that the law applies only to the dust of its dust, which is not subject to the same prohibition. Rava offers a different principle: mitzvot are not given for benefit, so the prohibition does not apply.
items.desc: רבי זעירא אומר שמכסים דם חיה ועוף בעפר עיר הנדחת. הגמרא מקשה שהרי אסור בהנאה, ומתרצת: זעירי מפרש שמדובר בעפר קרקע העיר שלא נתחייב שריפה, ורבא אומר שמצוות לאו להנאה ניתנו.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira (or Rabbah bar Yirmeyah) proposes that one may cover blood with earth from an idolatrous city, and the Gemara objects that such earth is forbidden for benefit.
sub.desc: רבי זעירא (או רבה בר ירמיה) פותח ואומר שמכסים דם חיה ועוף בעפר עיר הנדחת.

sub.desc_en: Ze'iri answers that the permission applies only to the dust of its dust, which is not subject to the prohibition because it requires plucking before gathering and burning.
sub.desc: זעירי מתרץ: הכוונה לעפר קרקע העיר עצמה, שלא נתחייב בשריפה כי חסרה תלישה.

sub.desc_en: Rava offers a different principle: mitzvot are not given for benefit, so the prohibition does not apply.
sub.desc: רבא מתרץ באופן אחר: מצוות לאו להנאה ניתנו, ולכן מותר להשתמש בעפר האסור בהנאה לצורך כיסוי הדם.

items.text: דין שופר ולולב של עבודה זרה
items.text_en: Objection from shofar and lulav of idolatry
items.desc_en: Ravina teaches Rava's principle, and Rav Rechumi objects with a baraita stating that a shofar or lulav from idolatry may not be used, implying that if used, one does not fulfill the mitzvah. Ravina initially deflects, but a direct baraita contradicts him. Rav Ashi resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between the cases.
items.desc: רבינא אמר הלכה שמכסים באפר עיר הנדחת. רב רחומי הקשה מברייתא ששופר של עבודה זרה לא יתקע, ואם תקע לא יצא. הגמרא מתרצת תחילה שיצא, אך ברייתא אחרת סותרת. רב אשי מחלק בין כיסוי הדם לשופר ולולב, כי בשופר ולולב יש דין 'זה אלי ואנוהו' או דין ביטול.

sub.desc_en: Ravina sits and teaches Rava's principle that מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו (mitzvot were not given for benefit).
sub.desc: רבינא יושב ואומר את ההלכה שמכסים באפר עיר הנדחת, ורב רחומי מקשה מברייתא על שופר של עבודה זרה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Rechumi objects by citing a baraita that a shofar from idolatry may not be blown, implying that if blown, one does not fulfill the mitzvah.
sub.desc: רבינא יושב ואומר את ההלכה שמכסים באפר עיר הנדחת, ורב רחומי מקשה מברייתא על שופר של עבודה זרה.

sub.desc_en: Ravina deflects by interpreting the baraita as a לכתחילה (ideal standard) prohibition, but בדיעבד (after the fact) one fulfills the mitzvah.
sub.desc: רב רחומי מקשה: האם הברייתא 'לא יתקע' משמעה שאם תקע לא יצא? והגמרא דוחה: לא, הכוונה שאם תקע יצא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Rechumi raises a parallel case of a lulav from idolatry, and Ravina again deflects with the same distinction.
sub.desc: רב רחומי מקשה: האם הברייתא 'לא יתקע' משמעה שאם תקע לא יצא? והגמרא דוחה: לא, הכוונה שאם תקע יצא.

sub.desc_en: A direct baraita is cited that explicitly states that if one blew the shofar or took the lulav, one did not fulfill the mitzvah, contradicting Ravina's interpretation.
sub.desc: רב רחומי מקשה: האם הברייתא 'לא יתקע' משמעה שאם תקע לא יצא? והגמרא דוחה: לא, הכוונה שאם תקע יצא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between the cases: the shofar and lulav cases involve a different principle than the one Ravina was discussing.
sub.desc: רב אשי מחלק בין כיסוי הדם לשופר ולולב, ששם יש דין 'זה אלי ואנוהו' או דין ביטול.

items.text: סיום הדיון הקודם על כיסוי הדם
items.text_en: Transition from covering blood to sciatic nerve
items.desc_en: The Gemara concludes the discussion on covering blood, noting that any amount of blood that spurts out is valid for covering, unlike idolatry where a minimum measure is required. It then returns to the topic of covering blood.
items.desc: הקטע מסביר מדוע שופר ולולב של עבודה זרה פסולים, בניגוד לאפר לכיסוי הדם שאינו צריך שיעור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that for covering blood, any amount that spurts out is valid, unlike idolatry where a minimum measure is required, and then returns to the topic of covering blood.
sub.desc: מסביר מדוע שופר ולולב של עבודה זרה פסולים (צריכים שיעור והם נחשבים כתותים), ואילו אפר לכיסוי הדם כשר כי אין צריך שיעור.

items.text: משנת גיד הנשה
items.text_en: Mishnah: Laws of the sciatic nerve
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies in all places and times, to both non-sacred and consecrated animals, to cattle and undomesticated animals, to both hindquarters, but not to birds. It applies to a fetus, though Rabbi Yehuda disagrees. Butchers are not trusted regarding the sciatic nerve according to Rabbi Meir, but the Sages say they are trusted for it and for forbidden fat.
items.desc: המשנה מפרטת את תחולת איסור גיד הנשה: נוהג בארץ ובחו"ל, בפני הבית ושלא בפניו, בחולין ובמוקדשין, בבהמה ובחיה, בירך ימין ושמאל, ואינו נוהג בעוף. נוהג בשליל, ורבי יהודה חולק. טבחים אינם נאמנים לדברי רבי מאיר, וחכמים אומרים שנאמנים על הגיד ועל החלב.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve (גיד הנשה) applies in all places, to all animals, and to both hindquarters, but not to birds because they lack a spoon-shaped hip.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בפרטי איסור גיד הנשה.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah records a dispute: the first opinion holds that the sciatic nerve prohibition applies to a fetus, while Rabbi Yehuda says it does not apply to a fetus and its fat is permitted.
sub.desc: המשנה מביאה מחלוקת בין תנא קמא לרבי יהודה לגבי שליל.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah records another dispute: Rabbi Meir says butchers are not trusted regarding the sciatic nerve, while the Sages say they are trusted regarding both the sciatic nerve and the forbidden fat (חלב).
sub.desc: המשנה מביאה מחלוקת בין רבי מאיר לחכמים בדבר נאמנות טבחים.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא על מוקדשין ותירוץ ראשון
items.text_en: Gemara's question on consecrated animals
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks: Why does the Mishnah mention consecrated animals? If one consecrates an animal, does that remove the prohibition of the sciatic nerve? It suggests that if one holds that sinews impart flavor, then the prohibition of consecration would override the sciatic nerve, but the Mishnah should then say 'consecrated animals are subject to the sciatic nerve.' Rather, the Tanna holds that sinews do not impart flavor, so the sciatic nerve prohibition remains while the consecration prohibition does not apply.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע צריך לומר שגיד הנשה נוהג במוקדשין? הרי איסור מוקדשין חל על הגיד. מתרצת: התנא סובר שאין בגידים בנותן טעם, ולכן איסור מוקדשין אינו חל על הגיד, ורק איסור גיד הנשה קיים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah states that the sciatic nerve applies to consecrated animals, since consecration might supersede the prohibition, and if one argues that the prohibition of consecration takes effect on top of the sciatic nerve, the Mishnah should have said 'consecration applies to the nerve' rather than 'the nerve applies to consecrated animals'.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע צריך לומר שגיד הנשה נוהג במוקדשין? הרי איסור מוקדשין חל על הגיד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the Tanna holds that the sciatic nerve does not impart flavor (אין בגידין בנותן טעם), so the prohibition of the nerve remains while the prohibition of consecration does not apply to the nerve itself.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: התנא סובר שאין בגידים בנותן טעם, ולכן איסור מוקדשין אינו חל על הגיד, ורק איסור גיד הנשה קיים.

items.text: התנגדות לתירוץ הראשון
items.text_en: Objection from a baraita
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects: Does our Tanna really hold that sinews do not impart flavor? But we learned in a baraita: If a thigh was cooked with a sciatic nerve, if it imparts flavor, it is forbidden! This contradicts the assumption.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה על התירוץ: והרי משנה מפורשת (צ"ו ע"ב) שגיד הנשה נותן טעם, ולכן איסור מוקדשין חל עליו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects by citing a baraita that states if a thigh was cooked with a sciatic nerve, it is forbidden if the nerve imparts flavor, contradicting the claim that the nerve has no flavor.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על התירוץ הראשון: והרי משנה מפורשת (צ"ו ע"ב) שגיד הנשה נותן טעם, ולכן איסור מוקדשין חל עליו.

items.text: תירוץ שני: ולדות קדשים
items.text_en: Resolution: Fetal offspring of consecrated animals
items.desc_en: The Gemara resolves: Rather, we are dealing with fetal offspring of consecrated animals. The Tanna holds that the sciatic nerve applies to a fetus, and that fetal offspring of consecrated animals are sanctified while in their mother's womb, so both prohibitions (sciatic nerve and consecration) arise simultaneously.
items.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהמשנה עוסקת בולדות קדשים, והתנא סובר שגיד הנשה נוהג בשליל, וולדות קדשים קדושים במעי אמן, כך ששני האיסורים חלים יחד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the Mishnah deals with offspring of consecrated animals (ולדות קדשים), where the fetus is consecrated only in its mother's womb, so the prohibition of the sciatic nerve and the prohibition of consecration arise simultaneously.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהמשנה עוסקת בולדות קדשים, והתנא סובר שגיד הנשה נוהג בשליל, וולדות קדשים קדושים במעי אמן, כך ששני האיסורים חלים יחד.

items.text: קושיית הסיפא על התירוץ השני
items.text_en: Challenge: Contradiction from the Mishnah's structure
items.desc_en: The Gemara challenges: Can you interpret it as referring to a fetus? But from the fact that the latter clause teaches 'it applies to a fetus,' it implies that the first clause is not dealing with a fetus. The Gemara responds: The Mishnah means that this matter is a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מהסיפא 'נוהג בשליל' משמע שהרישא אינה עוסקת בשליל. מתרצת: הרישא היא מחלוקת בין רבי יהודה לרבנן.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the Mishnah's first clause cannot be about a fetus, since the later clause explicitly mentions 'applies to a fetus', implying the first clause is not about a fetus, and resolves that the Mishnah is presenting a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על התירוץ השני: מהסיפא 'נוהג בשליל' משמע שהרישא אינה עוסקת בשליל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara responds: The Mishnah means that this matter is a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis, not that the first clause excludes a fetus.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על התירוץ השני: מהסיפא 'נוהג בשליל' משמע שהרישא אינה עוסקת בשליל.

items.text: קושיית 'בהדי הדדי' מסוגיית נזיר
items.text_en: Support from a parallel sugya in Nazir
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether both prohibitions can arise simultaneously, citing a baraita about a nazirite shaving for impurity from a fetus whose limbs were not connected by sinews. Rabbi Yochanan explains that the case is a fetus whose limbs were not yet connected by sinews, showing that simultaneous prohibitions are possible.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: וכי אפשר ששני איסורים חלים יחד? והרי במשנת נזיר (מ"ט ע"ב) קשה על 'על המת' ו'על כזית מן המת', ורבי יוחנן מתרץ שמדובר בנפל שלא נתקשרו אבריו בגידין, שאין בו כזית בשר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects to the idea that two prohibitions can arise simultaneously, citing a Mishnah about a nazirite shaving for impurity from a corpse and from an olive's bulk of a corpse.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על האפשרות ששני איסורים חלים יחד, ומביאה ראיה ממשנת נזיר.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan answers that the Mishnah about the nazirite is necessary only for a stillborn whose limbs are not yet connected by sinews, showing that the principle of simultaneous prohibitions is not universally applicable.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן מתרץ שמדובר בנפל שלא נתקשרו אבריו בגידין, שאין בו כזית בשר.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan explains that the case is a fetus whose limbs were not yet connected by sinews, showing that simultaneous prohibitions are possible.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן מתרץ שמדובר בנפל שלא נתקשרו אבריו בגידין, שאין בו כזית בשר.

items.text: Initial challenge: consecration precedes, but sciatic nerve overrides
items.text_en: Initial challenge: consecration precedes, but sciatic nerve overrides
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first, yet the sciatic nerve overrides it because its prohibition applies to Noahides. This sets up the question of whose opinion this follows.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first, yet the sciatic nerve overrides it because its prohibition applies to Noahides.
The Gemara explains that even though the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first, the prohibition of the sciatic nerve overrides it because it applies to Noahides.

items.text: Identifying the Tanna: Rabbi Yehuda or not?
items.text_en: Identifying the Tanna: Rabbi Yehuda or not?
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks who holds this view, suggesting it is Rabbi Yehuda, but the mishnah (which says the nerve applies to both right and left thighs) does not follow Rabbi Yehuda. It resolves that this Tanna agrees with Rabbi Yehuda on one point but disagrees on another.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks who holds the view that the prohibition of the gid hanasheh (sciatic nerve) applies to consecrated animals, suggesting it is Rabbi Yehuda, but notes that the mishnah (which says the nerve applies to both right and left thighs) does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.
The Gemara resolves that this Tanna agrees with Rabbi Yehuda on one point (that the nerve applies to consecrated animals) but disagrees with him on another (that it applies to both thighs).

items.text: Two alternative resolutions: firstborn or offspring of consecrated animals
items.text_en: Two alternative resolutions: firstborn or offspring of consecrated animals
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Rabbi Yehuda's view about a non-kosher animal (a mere negative commandment) cannot be extended to consecrated animals (which carry karet). Two answers are given: either the case involves a firstborn animal, which is holy from the womb, or the offspring of consecrated animals are holy by their very nature.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Rabbi Yehuda's leniency regarding a non-kosher animal (a mere negative commandment) cannot be extended to consecrated animals, which carry the penalty of karet.
The Gemara answers that the case involves a firstborn animal (בכור), which is holy from the womb, so its sanctity is comparable to a non-kosher animal's prohibition.
An alternative answer is given: the offspring of consecrated animals are holy by their very nature (בהתהוותן), so the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to them.

items.text: Dispute between Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef and Rabbi Yochanan
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef and Rabbi Yochanan
items.desc_en: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef says the sciatic nerve prohibition applies only to consecrated animals that are eaten, not to those that are not eaten. Rabbi Yochanan says it applies to both.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef states that the sciatic nerve prohibition applies only to consecrated animals that are eaten, not to those that are not eaten.
Rabbi Yochanan counters that the sciatic nerve prohibition applies to both consecrated animals that are eaten and those that are not eaten.

items.text: Rav Pappa's reconciliations: lashes vs. offering
items.text_en: Rav Pappa's reconciliations: lashes vs. offering
items.desc_en: Rav Pappa says the two opinions do not actually dispute: one refers to lashes (for eating the nerve), the other to offering it on the altar. An alternative version says the dispute is about removing the nerve vs. offering it.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa reconciles the two opinions by saying one refers to lashes (for eating the nerve) and the other to offering it on the altar.
An alternative version states the dispute is about removing the nerve versus offering it on the altar.

items.text: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's analysis: offering on the altar is the dispute
items.text_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's analysis: offering on the altar is the dispute
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak argues that the dispute is specifically about offering the nerve on the altar. He cites a baraita that bones, sinews, horns, and hooves are included in the offering when attached, but if detached they must be removed. Rabbi holds that even detached they are offered, while the Rabbis require a verse to include attached ones.

sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak asserts that the dispute between Rabbi and the Rabbis is specifically about offering the nerve on the altar.
A baraita is cited, deriving from verses that attached bones, sinews, horns, and hooves are offered on the altar, but if detached they must be removed even from atop the altar.
The Gemara asks which Tanna holds that detached parts descend from the altar.
The Gemara answers that it is Rabbi, who holds that even detached parts are included in the offering, but the verse 'בשר ודם' is applied to popping parts.
Rabbi explains his position: one verse includes everything, another limits to flesh and blood, so attached parts are offered but detached ones descend.
The Rabbis argue that attached parts need no verse to include them, as they are part of the offering; the verse is only needed for detached parts.

items.text: Rabbi's view on attached limbs
items.text_en: Rabbi's view on attached limbs
items.desc_en: The Gemara begins to explain Rabbi's position that attached limbs are permissible and do not require a verse, but the text is cut off.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara begins to explain Rabbi's position that attached limbs are permissible and do not require a verse, but the text is cut off.

items.text: מחלוקת רבי ורבנן: גיד הנשה במחובר
items.text_en: Debate on the source for the sciatic nerve in a detached state
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that the verse 'על כן לא יאכלו בני ישראל' is needed to prohibit the sciatic nerve even when detached, while the Sages and Rabbi differ on the derivation from 'ממשקה ישראל'.
items.desc: רבי יהודה הנשיא ורבנן נחלקו אם גיד הנשה המחובר לבשר עולה למזבח. רבי דורש 'כל' לרבות גיד במחובר, ואילו רבנן דורשים 'ממשקה ישראל' – מן המותר לישראל, וגיד אסור באכילה. רבי משווה לחלב ודם שמותרים למזבח אף שאסורים באכילה, ורבנן דוחים שמצוותן בכך שאני.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that the verse is not needed to prohibit the sciatic nerve when attached, but only when detached.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת ומבארת שהפסוק 'כל' בא לרבות גיד הנשה במחובר לבשר.

sub.desc_en: The Sages derive from 'ממשקה ישראל' that the prohibition applies only to what is permitted to Israel.
sub.desc: רבנן דורשים 'ממשקה ישראל' – מן המותר לישראל, ולכן גיד האסור באכילה אינו עולה למזבח.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi compares the sciatic nerve to forbidden fat and blood, while the Sages distinguish that those have a different מצוה (commandment) context.
sub.desc: רבי משיב שגיד במחובר דומה לחלב ודם שמותרים למזבח אף שאסורים באכילה.

items.text: Rav Huna's ruling on the sciatic nerve of an olah
items.text_en: Rav Huna's ruling on the sciatic nerve of an olah
items.desc_en: Rav Huna states that the sciatic nerve of an olah is removed to the pile (תפוח) on the altar. Rav Chisda objects, noting that the verse says 'לא יאכלו' not 'לא יקריבו', and Rav Huna responds by citing the principle of 'ממשקה ישראל'.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna rules that the sciatic nerve of an olah is removed to the pile (תפוח) on the altar.

Rav Chisda objects that the verse says 'על כן לא יאכלו' (therefore the children of Israel shall not eat), not 'לא יקריבו' (shall not sacrifice), so the prohibition applies only to eating, not to offering.

Rav Huna responds by citing the principle of 'ממשקה ישראל' (from what is permitted to Israel), implying that only items permitted to Israelites may be offered on the altar, so the sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to Israelites, cannot be offered.

items.text: Support for Rav Huna from a baraita
items.text_en: Support for Rav Huna from a baraita
items.desc_en: A baraita is cited that supports Rav Huna: the sciatic nerve of a shelamim is swept to the canal, while that of an olah is brought up and removed to the pile. The Gemara explains why it is brought up first, citing Malachi 1:8.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited: the sciatic nerve of a shelamim is swept to the canal, and that of an olah is brought up; the Gemara asks whether 'brought up' means brought up and offered.
The Gemara rejects the inference: 'brought up' means brought up and then removed, and explains that it is brought up first only because of the verse 'Present it now to your governor' (Malachi 1:8).
A baraita is cited that explicitly supports Rav Huna: the sciatic nerve of a shelamim is swept to the canal, and that of an olah is removed to the pile.

items.text: לשון הוואי: תפוח, גפן ופרוכת
items.text_en: Discussion of hyperbolic language (לשון הוואי) in the Mishnah and baraitot
items.desc_en: The Gemara discusses the Mishnah's description of the pile (תפוח) as holding 300 kor, and Rava calls it exaggeration. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani cite examples of hyperbolic language in Torah, Prophets, and Sages, including the golden vine and the parochet.
items.desc: רבי אמי ורבי יצחק בר נחמני מביאים דוגמאות ללשון הוואי (הגזמה) בדברי חכמים, תורה ונביאים. שלוש דוגמאות מחכמים: תפוח (ערימת אפר על המזבח), גפן של זהב, ופרוכת – כולם מתוארים במידות מוגזמות. רבא מכנה זאת 'גוזמא'.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes a pile (תפוח) in the middle of the altar that sometimes held as much as 300 kor.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה משנה על תפוח האפר ורבא קובע שזה גוזמא – לשון הוואי.

sub.desc_en: Rava labels both the Mishnah's 300-kor figure and the description of watering the daily offering with a golden cup as גוזמא (hyperbole).
sub.desc: דוגמה נוספת לגוזמא: השקיית התמיד בכוס של זהב – רבא אומר גוזמא.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Ami establishes a general principle that Torah, Prophets, and Sages all employ לשון הוואי (hyperbolic language).
sub.desc: רבי אמי קובע כלל: תורה, נביאים וחכמים דיברו בלשון הוואי (הגזמה), ומביא דוגמאות.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites verses: 'cities great and fortified up to heaven' (Deut. 1:28) from Torah, and 'the earth split at their voice' (I Kings 1:40) from Prophets, as examples of hyperbolic speech.

sub.text: רבי יצחק בר נחמני אמר שמואל
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani citing Shmuel's list
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani reports in Shmuel's name that the Sages used hyperbole in three specific contexts, beginning with the pile (תפוח) just mentioned.
sub.desc: שמואל מונה שלושה מקומות בהם חכמים דיברו בלשון הוואי: תפוח, גפן ופרוכת.

sub.desc_en: The second example is the golden vine at the Temple entrance, where Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Tzadok relates an incident claiming 300 priests were needed to clear it.
sub.desc: הבאת הדוגמה השנייה: גפן של זהב במקדש, ומעשה ששלש מאות כהנים פינו אותה – לשון הוואי.

sub.desc_en: The third example is the parochet (curtain), described in extravagant dimensions and weight, requiring 300 priests to immerse it.
sub.desc: הבאת הדוגמה השלישית: פרוכת – עוביה, ארגתה, מידותיה ומספר הכהנים המטבילים אותה – לשון הוואי.

items.text: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages on the number of sciatic nerves
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages on the number of sciatic nerves
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states the prohibition applies to both thighs, but Rabbi Yehuda says it applies only to one, and the Sages disagree. The Gemara questions whether Rabbi Yehuda is certain or in doubt about which side is prohibited.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to both the right and left thighs.
The Gemara notes that the Mishnah does not follow Rabbi Yehuda's opinion.
A baraita is cited: Rabbi Yehuda says the prohibition applies only to one thigh, and common sense inclines toward the right.
The Gemara raises a question: Is Rabbi Yehuda certain about which thigh is prohibited, or is he in doubt and merely expressing a tendency?

items.text: Resolution of Rabbi Yehuda's position via a baraita on bones and sinews
items.text_en: Resolution of Rabbi Yehuda's position via a baraita on bones and sinews
items.desc_en: A baraita about burning bones and sinews with leftover sacrificial meat is analyzed. Rav Chisda explains it refers to the sciatic nerve according to Rabbi Yehuda, and the Gemara concludes that Rabbi Yehuda is uncertain, as otherwise the nerve would be eaten or discarded.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita about burning bones, sinews, and leftover sacrificial meat on the sixteenth, and questions which sinews are meant, rejecting possibilities until it suggests neck sinews.
Rav Chisda explains the baraita refers to the sciatic nerve according to Rabbi Yehuda, who holds the prohibition applies only to one thigh.
The Gemara objects that if Rabbi Yehuda were certain which thigh is forbidden, he would simply eat the permitted one or discard the forbidden one, rather than burning it with sacrificial leftovers.
Rav Ika bar Chanina resolves that Rabbi Yehuda is certain, but the case involves nerves that were initially distinguishable and then became mixed, necessitating burning.

items.text: הסברי רב אשי ורבינא למשנה
items.text_en: Two explanations of the Mishnah's need to mention the outer sinew
items.desc_en: Rav Ashi says the Mishnah only needed to permit the fat of the sinew, as a baraita already permits it but Israelites treat it as forbidden. Ravina says it was needed for the law of two sinews taught by Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel: the inner sinew is forbidden and liable for lashes, the outer is forbidden but not liable.
items.desc: רב אשי ורבינא מציעים הסברים שונים למשנה העוסקת בגיד הנשה של קרבן פסח. רב אשי מסביר שהמשנה עוסקת בשומן שסביב הגיד, ורבינא מסביר שהיא עוסקת בגיד החיצון האסור מדרבנן.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi explains that the Mishnah's mention of the outer sinew was only needed to permit its fat, since a baraita already permits it but Israelites treat it as forbidden.
sub.desc: רב אשי מסביר שהמשנה עוסקת בשומן שסביב גיד הנשה, שמותר מן התורה אך נאסר מנהג.

sub.text_en: Ravina citing Rav Yehuda said Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Ravina explains that the Mishnah was needed to teach the law of two sinews as stated by Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: the inner sinew is forbidden and liable for lashes, the outer is forbidden but not liable.
sub.desc: רבינא מסביר שהמשנה עוסקת בגיד החיצון האסור מדרבנן, כדברי רב יהודה בשם שמואל.

items.text: קושיה מברייתא על שיטת רבי יהודה
items.text_en: Proof that Rabbi Yehuda considers the outer sinew definitely forbidden
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Yehuda says one who eats from both sinews receives only forty lashes, not eighty. If he were uncertain about the outer sinew, this would be a doubtful warning, which he rejects. Therefore, he must consider it definitely forbidden. The Gemara then notes that this baraita follows a different Tanna of Rabbi Yehuda who accepts doubtful warnings.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה רבי יהודה פוטר מארבעים מלקות באכילת שני גידים, ומקשה: אם יש ספק איזה גיד אסור, הרי ההתראה היא ספק, ורבי יהודה פוסל התראת ספק. מתרצים שהברייתא סוברת כרבי יהודה אחר הסוברים שהתראת ספק שמה התראה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita: one who eats an olive's bulk from each sinew receives eighty lashes, but Rabbi Yehuda says he receives only forty.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא שבה רבי יהודה פוטר מארבעים מלקות באכילת שני גידים, ומקשה: אם יש ספק איזה גיד אסור, הרי ההתראה היא ספק, ורבי יהודה פוסל התראת ספק.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara argues: if Rabbi Yehuda considers the outer sinew definitely forbidden, the baraita works; but if he is uncertain, the warning would be a doubtful warning (התראת ספק), which he rejects.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שאם רבי יהודה מסתפק, ההתראה היא ספק, והוא פוסל התראת ספק.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited showing that Rabbi Yehuda holds that a doubtful warning (התראת ספק) is not a valid warning, exempting one who strikes or curses two people sequentially.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא המוכיחה שרבי יהודה פוסל התראת ספק.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the baraita follows a different Tanna of Rabbi Yehuda who accepts doubtful warnings (התראת ספק שמה התראה).
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שהברייתא סוברת כרבי יהודה אחר הסוברים שהתראת ספק שמה התראה.

items.text: ברייתא נוספת על לאו שאין בו מעשה
items.text_en: Supporting baraita about doubtful warnings
items.desc_en: A baraita is cited where Rabbi Yehuda says that a prohibition with a positive commandment after it does not incur lashes, but Rabbi Yaakov says it is because it is a prohibition without an action. This shows that Rabbi Yehuda does not accept doubtful warnings in that context.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא על הפסח, שבה רבי יהודה ורבי יעקב נחלקים בטעם הפטור ממלקות על הותרת הפסח. רבי יהודה סובר משום עשה אחר לא תעשה, ורבי יעקב סובר משום לאו שאין בו מעשה.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited where Rabbi Yehuda says that a prohibition with a positive commandment after it does not incur lashes.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בדברי רבי יהודה, הטוען שהפסוק בא לתת עשה אחר לא תעשה כדי לפטור ממלקות.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yaakov argues that the exemption is because it is a prohibition without an action, not because of the positive commandment.
sub.desc: רבי יעקב חולק על רבי יהודה וטוען שהפטור ממלקות נובע מכך שמדובר בלאו שאין בו מעשה.

items.text: Another proof from two sinews from two animals
items.text_en: Another proof from two sinews from two animals
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings another baraita: one who eats two sinews from two different animals receives eighty lashes, but Rabbi Yehuda says only forty. Since it specifies from two animals, both are definitely forbidden, and Rabbi Yehuda's ruling proves he considers the outer sinew definitely forbidden.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita: one who eats two sinews from two different animals receives eighty lashes, but Rabbi Yehuda says only forty.

The Gemara concludes: since the baraita specifies from two animals, both sinews are definitely forbidden, and Rabbi Yehuda's ruling of only forty proves he considers the outer sinew definitely forbidden.

items.text: Resolution: the case involves less than an olive's bulk
items.text_en: Resolution: the case involves less than an olive's bulk
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks: if the outer sinew is definitely forbidden, why does Rabbi Yehuda say only forty lashes? The answer is that the case involves less than an olive's bulk, and Rabbi Yehuda requires an olive's bulk for lashes, as per a baraita.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: if the outer sinew is definitely forbidden, why does Rabbi Yehuda say only forty lashes instead of eighty?
The Gemara answers: the case involves less than an olive's bulk of the sinew.
A baraita is cited: Rabbi Yehuda requires an olive's bulk for lashes, so with less than that he only gives forty lashes for the inner sinew.

items.text: Scriptural derivation for the inner sinew's prohibition
items.text_en: Scriptural derivation for the inner sinew's prohibition
items.desc_en: Rava explains that the verse 'the thigh' (hayarech) refers to the inner sinew, which is the main part of the thigh. The Rabbis derive that the prohibition spreads throughout the thigh, excluding the outer sinew.

sub.desc_en: Rava explains that the verse 'the thigh' (הַיָּרֵךְ) refers to the inner sinew, which is the main part of the thigh.
The Rabbis derive that the prohibition spreads throughout the thigh, excluding the outer sinew.

items.text: Aggadic interpretations of Jacob's wrestling
items.text_en: Aggadic interpretations of Jacob's wrestling
items.desc_en: Various Amoraim explain the wrestling match: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says it was like a friend embracing, with the angel's hand reaching Jacob's right hand. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says the angel appeared as a heathen, who should be placed to the right. Rav Shmuel bar Acha says he appeared as a Torah scholar, who should be to the right. The Rabbis say the angel came from behind and injured both sinews. The verse 'behe'avko imo' is also used to teach that the dust of their feet rose to the Throne of Glory.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interprets the wrestling as a friendly embrace, with the angel's hand reaching Jacob's right hand.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says the angel appeared as a heathen, who should be placed to the right.

sub.text: Rav Shmuel bar Acha (before Rav Pappa, in the name of Rava bar Ulla)
sub.text_en: Rav Shmuel bar Acha (before Rav Pappa, in the name of Rava bar Ulla)
sub.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Acha says the angel appeared as a Torah scholar, who should be to the right.
The Rabbis say the angel came from behind and injured both sinews.

sub.text: Gemara (citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's second statement)
sub.text_en: Gemara (citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's second statement)
sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that the Rabbis use the verse 'behe'avko imo' for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's other teaching, that the dust of their feet rose to the Throne of Glory.

items.text: Further aggadic teachings about the sinew and Jacob
items.text_en: Further aggadic teachings about the sinew and Jacob
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi explains why the sinew is called 'gid hanasheh' – it moved from its place and ascended. Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina says the verse 'davar shalach beYaakov' refers to the sinew, and its prohibition spread to all Israel. He also interprets 'utevoach tevach vehachen' as preparing the slaughter and removing the sinew, supporting that it was forbidden to Noahides. Rabbi Elazar says Jacob stayed behind for small jars, teaching that the righteous value their property more than their bodies to avoid theft. Rabbi Yitzchak says this teaches that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi asks why the sinew is called 'gid hanasheh' and answers that it moved from its place and ascended.
Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina interprets the verse 'דבר שלח ביעקב' as referring to the sinew, and 'ונפל בישראל' as its prohibition spreading to all Israel.
Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina interprets 'וטבח טבח והכן' as preparing the slaughter and removing the sinew, supporting that it was forbidden to Noahides (בני נח).
Rabbi Elazar says Jacob stayed behind for small jars, teaching that the righteous value their property more than their bodies to avoid theft.
Rabbi Yitzchak derives from the verse that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night.

items.text: מקורות לאיסור יציאת תלמיד חכם יחידי בלילה
items.text_en: Sources for the principle of early rising
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites verses to support the practice of rising early, with Rabbi Avahu, the Rabbis, and Rav each offering a different prooftext from the Torah.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה שלושה מקורות לפסוק 'הנה הוא זורה את גרן השעורים' המלמדים שתלמיד חכם לא יצא יחידי בלילה: רבי אבהו מפסוק וישכם אברהם בבקר, רבנן מפסוק לך נא ראה את שלום אחיך, ורב מפסוק ויזרח לו השמש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by citing the verse about Boaz winnowing barley at night, implying early rising.
sub.desc: פתיחה המצטטת את הפסוק מרות, המהווה בסיס לדרשת איסור יציאת תלמיד חכם יחידי בלילה.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Avahu cites the verse 'וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר' (Abraham rose early in the morning) as a prooftext for rising early.
sub.desc: רבי אבהו מביא ראיה מפסוק וישכם אברהם בבוקר, המלמד שתלמיד חכם לא יצא בלילה.

sub.desc_en: The Rabbis cite the verse 'לֶךְ נָא רְאֵה אֶת שְׁלוֹם אַחֶיךָ' (Go now, see the peace of your brothers) as a prooftext for rising early.
sub.desc: רבנן מביאים ראיה מפסוק לך נא ראה את שלום אחיך, המלמד שתלמיד חכם לא יצא בלילה.

sub.desc_en: Rav cites the verse 'וַיִּזְרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ' (the sun rose for him) as a prooftext for rising early.
sub.desc: רב מביא ראיה מפסוק ויזרח לו השמש, המלמד שתלמיד חכם לא יצא בלילה.

items.text: בירור הפסוק 'ויזרח לו השמש'
items.text_en: The sun shone for Jacob alone
items.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva recounts a question about the verse 'the sun shone for him' – did it shine only for Jacob? Rabbi Yitzchak explains that the sun shone for Jacob because he returned to pray at the place where his fathers prayed, and the earth contracted for him; God then made the sun set so Jacob would stay overnight.
items.desc: רבי עקיבא שואל את רבן גמליאל ורבי יהושע: וכי השמש זרחה רק ליעקב? רבי יצחק מסביר שהשמש שקעה מוקדם עבורו כדי שיישאר ללון במקום, ולאחר מכן זרחה מוקדם עבורו. הסיפור: יעקב שכח להתפלל במקום האבות, קפצה לו הארץ, התפלל, וביקש לחזור, אך ה' השהה אותו.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva recounts asking Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua about the verse 'וַיִּזְרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ' — did the sun shine only for Jacob, when it shines for the whole world?
sub.desc: רבי עקיבא שואל את רבן גמליאל ורבי יהושע: וכי השמש זרחה רק ליעקב?

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak explains that the sun that had set for Jacob's journey shone again for him, because when Jacob reached Haran he realized he had passed the place where his fathers prayed, and the earth contracted for him to return.
sub.desc: רבי יצחק מסביר שהשמש שקעה מוקדם עבור יעקב כדי שיישאר ללון, ומספר כיצד קפצה הארץ כשחזר להתפלל.

sub.desc_en: After Jacob prayed, he wanted to return, but the Holy One said: This righteous man came to my lodging — should he depart without staying overnight? Immediately the sun set.
sub.desc: לאחר שהתפלל, ביקש יעקב לחזור, אך ה' השהה אותו והשמש באה.

items.text: התקבצות האבנים למקום אחד
items.text_en: The stones became one stone
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak teaches that all the stones gathered and each wanted the righteous Jacob to rest his head on it, and they were all absorbed into one stone.
items.desc: רבי יצחק מסביר את הסתירה בין הפסוקים: 'ויקח מאבני המקום' ו'ויקח את האבן' – כל האבנים התקבצו למקום אחד וכל אחת רצתה שיניח עליה ראשו, ולבסוף נבלעו כולן באחת.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak teaches that all the stones gathered, each wanting Jacob to rest his head on it.
sub.desc: רבי יצחק מיישב את הסתירה בין הפסוקים בכך שכל האבנים התקבצו וכל אחת רצתה שיניח עליה ראשו, ולבסוף נבלעו כולן באחת.

sub.desc_en: A baraita adds that all the stones were absorbed into one.
sub.desc: רבי יצחק מיישב את הסתירה בין הפסוקים בכך שכל האבנים התקבצו וכל אחת רצתה שיניח עליה ראשו, ולבסוף נבלעו כולן באחת.

items.text: The width of the ladder
items.text_en: The width of the ladder
items.desc_en: A baraisa calculates the ladder's width as 8,000 parasangs based on the angels ascending and descending (four angels) and the verse describing an angel's body as tarshish (2,000 parasangs).

sub.desc_en: The baraita calculates the ladder's width as 8,000 parasangs by noting that the verse mentions 'ascending' (two angels) and 'descending' (two angels), and when they meet, there are four angels.
The baraita supports the calculation by citing the verse that an angel's body is like tarshish (תרשיש), and the tradition that tarshish measures 2,000 parasangs, so four angels yield 8,000 parasangs.

items.text: Angels look at the image above and below
items.text_en: Angels look at the image above and below
items.desc_en: The angels ascend and look at the divine image above, then descend and look at Jacob's image below; they sought to harm him, but God stood over him. Resh Lakish says this is like a father fanning his son.

sub.desc_en: A baraita describes that the angels ascend and look at the divine image above, then descend and look at Jacob's image below; they sought to harm him, but God stood over him.
Resh Lakish explains that God's standing over Jacob is like a father fanning his son to protect him.

items.text: The land folded under Jacob
items.text_en: The land folded under Jacob
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yitzchak explains that God folded all of Eretz Yisrael under Jacob so it would be easy for his children to conquer.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what is the greatness of the verse 'the land upon which you lie'.
Rabbi Yitzchak explains that God folded all of Eretz Yisrael under Jacob so it would be easy for his children to conquer.

items.text: The angel's fear of dawn and the three groups of angels
items.text_en: The angel's fear of dawn and the three groups of angels
items.desc_en: Jacob asks the angel if he is a thief or a gambler afraid of dawn; the angel replies he is an angel whose time to sing had never come until now. This supports Rav Chananel's statement that three groups of angels sing 'Kadosh' each day.

sub.desc_en: Jacob asks the angel if he is a thief or a gambler who fears the dawn.
The angel explains that he is an angel whose time to sing had never come until now.

sub.text: Gemara's support for Rav Chananel's statement
sub.text_en: Gemara's support for Rav Chananel's statement
sub.desc_en: The gemara cites Rav Chananel's tradition that three groups of angels sing 'Kadosh' each day, supported by the angel's statement.

items.text: Objection and resolution: frequency of angelic song
items.text_en: Objection and resolution: frequency of angelic song
items.desc_en: A challenge is raised: Israel is more beloved than angels because they praise God constantly, while angels only praise once a day/week/month/year/jubilee/ever. The Gemara resolves that the three groups say 'Kadosh', 'Kadosh Kadosh', and 'Kadosh Kadosh Kadosh' respectively, but notes the omission of 'Baruch'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita that Israel is more beloved than the ministering angels because Israel praises God constantly, while angels only praise once a day, week, month, year, shemittah, jubilee, or ever.
The baraita continues: Israel mentions God's name after two words (in 'שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳'), while angels only mention it after three words (in 'קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת').

The baraita adds that the ministering angels do not recite song above until Israel recites it below, as derived from the verse 'בְּרׇן יַחַד כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר' and then 'וַיָּרִיעוּ כׇּל בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים'.

The Gemara resolves the objection by reinterpreting the angelic song: one group says 'קָדוֹשׁ', one says 'קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ', and one says 'קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת', but then notes that the word 'בָּרוּךְ' is still missing from the angelic praise.

items.text: Interpretation of 'Baruch' and permission
items.text_en: Interpretation of 'Baruch' and permission
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the word 'Baruch' in the verse refers to the Ofanim, who say it, and alternatively, once permission is given, it is given.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the word 'Baruch' in the verse refers to the Ofanim, who say it.
The Gemara offers an alternative explanation: once permission is given, it is given.

items.text: Interpretation of Jacob's struggle with the angel
items.text_en: Interpretation of Jacob's struggle with the angel
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies ambiguous phrases in the verse about Jacob and the angel, determining that Jacob prevailed over the angel and that the angel wept to Jacob.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an ambiguity from the verse about Jacob and the angel: it is unclear who prevailed over whom.
The Gemara resolves the ambiguity by citing the verse 'כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים' (for you have striven with God), concluding that Jacob prevailed over the angel.
The Gemara raises a second ambiguity: it is unclear who wept to whom.
The Gemara resolves the second ambiguity by citing the angel's plea 'שַׁלְּחֵנִי' (send me away), concluding that the angel wept to Jacob.

items.text: Rabbah's hint about two leaders
items.text_en: Rabbah's hint about two leaders
items.desc_en: Rabbah interprets the verse 'for you have striven with God and with men' as a hint that two leaders will emerge from Jacob: the Exilarch in Babylonia and the Nasi in Eretz Yisrael, alluding to exile.

sub.desc_en: Rabbah interprets the verse 'for you have striven with God and with men' as a hint that two leaders will emerge from Jacob: the Exilarch in Babylonia and the Nasi in Eretz Yisrael, alluding to exile.

items.text: Interpretation of the three branches in Joseph's dream
items.text_en: Interpretation of the three branches in Joseph's dream
items.desc_en: Rav Chiyya bar Abba citing Rav identifies the three branches as three proud leaders from Israel each generation. Rava interprets them as three gentile leaders who advocate for Israel.

items.text: Dispute among Tannaim on the allegory of the vine
items.text_en: Dispute among Tannaim on the allegory of the vine
items.desc_en: Rabbi Eliezer interprets the vine as the world, the branches as the patriarchs, etc. Rabbi Yehoshua objects that dreams only show the future, and offers his own interpretation. Rabban Gamliel demands a unified interpretation, and Rabbi Elazar HaModai provides one.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Eliezer interprets the vine as the world, the branches as the patriarchs, the blossom as the matriarchs, and the grapes as the tribes.

Rabbi Yehoshua objects that dreams only show the future, not the past, and offers his own interpretation of the vine as Torah, the branches as Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, the blossom as the Sanhedrin, and the grapes as the righteous of each generation.

sub.text: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar HaModai
sub.text_en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar HaModai
sub.desc_en: Rabban Gamliel demands a unified interpretation, and Rabbi Elazar HaModai provides one: the vine is Jerusalem, the branches are the Temple, the king, and the high priest, the blossom is the young priests, and the grapes are the libations.

items.text: Further allegorical interpretations of the vine
items.text_en: Further allegorical interpretations of the vine
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interprets the vine as the Torah and the branches as the well, pillar of cloud, and manna. Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba interprets the vine as Israel, the branches as the three pilgrimage festivals, and the ripening grapes as Egypt's cup of poison.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interprets the vine as the Torah, the branches as the well, pillar of cloud, and manna, the blossom as the first fruits, and the ripened grapes as the libations.

Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba interprets the vine as Israel, the branches as the three pilgrimage festivals, the blossom as the time for Israel to be fruitful, and the ripened grapes as Egypt's time to drink the cup of poison.

items.text: Rava's three cups and confirmation of the interpretation
items.text_en: Rava's three cups and confirmation of the interpretation
items.desc_en: Rava explains the three cups of wrath Egypt drank. Rabbi Abba tells Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba that Rav taught these verses similarly in Aggadah.

sub.desc_en: Rava explains that the three cups mentioned in the context of Egypt correspond to three historical punishments: one in Moses' time, one in Pharaoh Necho's time, and one future cup with all nations.

sub.text: Rabbi Abba to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba
sub.text_en: Rabbi Abba to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba tells Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba that Rav taught these same verses in Aggadah in accordance with his interpretation.

items.text: Resh Lakish's allegory of Israel as a vine
items.text_en: Resh Lakish's allegory of Israel as a vine
items.desc_en: Resh Lakish compares Israel to a vine, with branches as householders, clusters as Torah scholars, leaves as amei ha'aretz, and tendrils as empty people. The Gemara notes that the scholars need the support of the simple folk.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish presents an allegory comparing Israel to a vine, with branches as householders, clusters as Torah scholars, leaves as amei ha'aretz, and tendrils as empty people.
The Gemara cites a message sent from the academy that the clusters (scholars) should pray for the leaves (simple folk), because without the leaves the clusters cannot survive.

items.text: Interpretation of the fifteen silver and the thirty righteous
items.text_en: Interpretation of the fifteen silver and the thirty righteous
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan interprets 'kirah' as a term of sale. The fifteen silver alludes to the 15th of Nisan and the righteous. The homer and letek of barley refer to 45 righteous people sustaining the world, with 30 in Eretz Yisrael and 15 outside. Abaye locates most in the synagogue of Tutei Aftei. Rabbi Yehuda says these are 30 righteous gentiles, while Ulla says they are 30 Noahide commandments.

sub.text: Rabbi Yochanan citing Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan citing Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan interprets 'כירה' (kirah) as a term of sale (מכירה), citing the verse 'בקברי אשר כריתי לי'.
The fifteen silver alludes to the 15th of Nisan (when Israel was redeemed from Egypt) and 'silver' refers to the righteous, as per the verse 'צרור הכסף לקח בידו'.

sub.text: Gemara's question (embedded in Rabbi Yochanan's statement)
sub.text_en: Gemara's question (embedded in Rabbi Yochanan's statement)
sub.desc_en: The homer and letek of barley refer to 45 righteous people sustaining the world, but it is unknown whether 30 are in Eretz Yisrael and 15 outside, or vice versa.
The verse 'ואקחה שלשים הכסף' resolves that 30 are in Eretz Yisrael and 15 outside.
Abaye locates most of these righteous in the synagogue of Tutei Aftei, citing the verse 'וישקלו את שכרי שלשים כסף'.
Rabbi Yehuda says these 30 are righteous gentiles upon whom the nations of the world are sustained.
Ulla says these are 30 Noahide commandments (שבע מצוות בני נח) that the Noahides accepted, but they only observe three.

items.text: Opening Mishnah and Gemara's question on birds
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah and Gemara's question on birds
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve does not apply to birds. The Gemara objects that birds do have a sciatic nerve, and resolves that they have it but it is not round (עגיל).

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve does not apply to birds.
The Gemara objects that birds visibly have a sciatic nerve.
The Gemara resolves that birds have a sciatic nerve but it is not round (עגיל), so the prohibition does not apply.

items.text: Rabbi Yirmeya's query on classification
items.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeya's query on classification
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya asks: if a bird has a round sciatic nerve but an animal does not, do we follow the individual's status or the species? The question remains unresolved (תיקו).

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya asks whether the classification of a bird's sciatic nerve follows the individual's status or the species, and the question remains unresolved (תיקו).

items.text: גיד הנשה בשליל
items.text_en: The prohibition applies to a fetus and Shmuel's ruling on its fat
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states the prohibition applies to a fetus. Shmuel rules that the fat of the fetus is permitted according to all opinions. The Gemara clarifies that this refers to the fat of the sciatic nerve, not the fetus itself, and cites a dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda regarding the fetus's fat.
items.desc: המשנה אומרת שגיד הנשה נוהג בשליל. שמואל אומר שחלבו מותר לדברי הכל. הגמרא מבררת על איזה חלב מדובר ומציגה את מחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה בשליל.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to a fetus (שליל).
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שגיד הנשה נוהג בשליל, ושמואל מוסיף שחלבו מותר לדברי הכל.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel rules that the fat of the fetus is permitted according to all opinions.
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שגיד הנשה נוהג בשליל, ושמואל מוסיף שחלבו מותר לדברי הכל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: whose fat is Shmuel referring to — the fat of the fetus or the fat of the sciatic nerve?
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת על איזה חלב אמר שמואל, ומציגה את מחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה בשליל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects: if Shmuel meant the fat of the fetus, there is a dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, so it cannot be permitted to all.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת על איזה חלב אמר שמואל, ומציגה את מחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה בשליל.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited: Rabbi Meir says the prohibition applies to the fetus and its fat is forbidden; Rabbi Yehuda says it does not apply and its fat is permitted.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת על איזה חלב אמר שמואל, ומציגה את מחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה בשליל.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar citing Rabbi Oshaya resolves the dispute: the disagreement applies only to a live nine-month-old fetus, and each sage follows his own general position.
sub.desc: רבי אלעזר בשם רבי אושעיא מיישב שהמחלוקת היא בבן תשעה חי, וכל אחד הולך לשיטתו.

items.text: חלב הגיד
items.text_en: Shmuel's ruling on the fat of the sciatic nerve
items.desc_en: The Gemara suggests Shmuel's ruling refers to the fat of the sciatic nerve itself. It cites a dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda: Rabbi Meir requires excavation of the nerve and permits its fat, while Rabbi Yehuda requires removal with the meat. The Gemara concludes that Shmuel agrees that for Rabbi Meir the fat is rabbinically prohibited, citing a baraita that Israelites treat it as forbidden.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה האם שמואל התכוון לחלב הגיד. מובאת ברייתא על חטיטת הגיד ומחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה. הגמרא מסיקה שרבי מאיר אוסר חלב הגיד מדרבנן.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether Shmuel's ruling refers to the fat of the sciatic nerve, noting that there is a dispute about it.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם שמואל התכוון לחלב הגיד, הרי יש מחלוקת תנאים בכך, ומביאה ברייתא על חטיטת הגיד ומחלוקת רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited showing the dispute between Rabbi Meir, who requires excavation of the nerve and cutting its fat from the root, and Rabbi Yehuda, who requires removing it with the meat.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את ההשגה: אי אפשר לומר שהברייתא כרבי יהודה, כי בברייתא אחרת מפורש שרבי מאיר אומר ששמנו מותר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that Shmuel's ruling indeed refers to the fat of the sciatic nerve, and Shmuel agrees that for Rabbi Meir the fat is rabbinically prohibited.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: שמואל מודה שלרבי מאיר חלב הגיד אסור מדרבנן, ומביאה ברייתא האומרת ששמנו מותר וישראל קדושים נהגו בו איסור.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited stating that the fat of the sciatic nerve is permitted by Torah law but Israelites treat it as forbidden.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: שמואל מודה שלרבי מאיר חלב הגיד אסור מדרבנן, ומביאה ברייתא האומרת ששמנו מותר וישראל קדושים נהגו בו איסור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers that the baraita aligns with Rabbi Meir, who holds the fat is permitted from the Torah but prohibited rabbinically.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: שמואל מודה שלרבי מאיר חלב הגיד אסור מדרבנן, ומביאה ברייתא האומרת ששמנו מותר וישראל קדושים נהגו בו איסור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that perhaps the baraita follows Rabbi Yehuda, but for Rabbi Meir the fat is even Torah-prohibited.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה: שמא הברייתא היא כרבי יהודה, אבל לרבי מאיר אסור מן התורה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara rejects the objection, citing a baraita where Rabbi Meir requires excavation of the nerve yet explicitly states its fat is permitted, confirming the earlier inference.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את ההשגה: אי אפשר לומר שהברייתא כרבי יהודה, כי בברייתא אחרת מפורש שרבי מאיר אומר ששמנו מותר.

items.text: מחלוקת רב ורב אושעיא על גדר הגיד
items.text_en: Debate on the tendrils of the sciatic nerve
items.desc_en: Rav and Ulla dispute the status of the nerve's tendrils (קנוקנות): Rav says the Torah only forbade the main nerve, while Ulla says it is like wood and the Torah prohibited it. Abaye supports Ulla by citing Rav Sheishet's analogy to the threads of forbidden fat (חלב), which are forbidden but not subject to karet.
items.desc: רב ורב אושעיא נחלקו: רב אומר שהתורה אסרה רק את הקנוקנות (החוטים הדקים), ואילו רב אושעיא אומר שהגיד עצמו אסור אף על פי שהוא כעץ. אביי מכריע כרב אושעיא.

sub.text: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא משם רב
sub.text_en: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta citing Rav
sub.desc_en: Rav states that the Torah only forbade the tendrils (קנוקנות) of the sciatic nerve, not the main nerve itself.
sub.desc: רב פוסק שהתורה אסרה רק את הקנוקנות שבגיד, לא את הגיד עצמו.

sub.text: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא משם רב
sub.desc_en: Ulla counters that the tendrils are like wood (i.e., part of the nerve) and the Torah prohibited them entirely.
sub.desc: רב פוסק שהתורה אסרה רק את הקנוקנות שבגיד, לא את הגיד עצמו.

sub.desc_en: Abaye supports Ulla by citing Rav Sheishet's ruling that the threads of forbidden fat (חלב) are forbidden but not subject to karet, applying the same logic to the tendrils of the sciatic nerve.
sub.desc: אביי מכריע כעולא, ומביא ראיה מדברי רב ששת ורב אסי על חוטין שבחלב.

items.text: חוטין שבחלב ולובן הכליה
items.text_en: Laws of threads in fat and kidney fat
items.desc_en: Rav Sheishet rules that threads in forbidden fat are forbidden but not subject to karet, and similarly for threads in the kidney. The whiteness of the kidney is disputed between Rabbi and Rabbi Chiya. The Gemara records practices of Rabbah, Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Asi regarding removal, and Abaye supports Rabbi Asi's view based on Shmuel's teaching.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה את דברי רב ששת בשם רב אסי על חוטין שבחלב ושבכליה, ומחלוקת רבי ורבי חייא בלובן הכליה. מסופר על מנהגי האמוראים בחטיטת לובן הכליה, ואביי מכריע כרבי אסי.

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheishet rules that threads in forbidden fat (חלב) are forbidden but not subject to karet.
sub.desc: רב ששת בשם רב אסי קובע שהחוטין שבחלב ושבכליה אסורים אבל אין חייבים עליהם.

sub.desc_en: Rav Sheishet extends the same rule to threads in the kidney fat.
sub.desc: רב ששת בשם רב אסי קובע שהחוטין שבחלב ושבכליה אסורים אבל אין חייבים עליהם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara reports a dispute between Rabbi and Rabbi Chiya regarding the whiteness of the kidney: one forbids it, the other permits it.
sub.desc: רב ששת בשם רב אסי קובע שהחוטין שבחלב ושבכליה אסורים אבל אין חייבים עליהם.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara records the practices of Rabbah, Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Asi regarding removal of the kidney's whiteness.
sub.desc: מתאר מנהגי אמוראים: רבא ורבי יוחנן מחטטים את לובן הכליה, ורבי אסי גוממו.

sub.desc_en: Abaye supports Rabbi Asi's view, citing a tradition from Shmuel via Rabbi Abba and Rav Yehuda.
sub.desc: מתאר מנהגי אמוראים: רבא ורבי יוחנן מחטטים את לובן הכליה, ורבי אסי גוממו.

items.text: Opening argument: fat covered by flesh is permitted
items.text_en: Opening argument: fat covered by flesh is permitted
items.desc_en: The Gemara begins by stating that fat covered by flesh is permitted, deriving that the Torah forbids fat on the flanks (על הכסלים) but not within them, and similarly fat on the kidneys (על הכליות) but not within them.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by stating that fat covered by flesh is permitted, deriving from the Torah's phrase 'על הכסלים' (on the flanks) and 'על הכליות' (on the kidneys) that only fat on the surface, not within, is forbidden.

items.text: Contradiction and resolution regarding fat covered by flesh
items.text_en: Contradiction and resolution regarding fat covered by flesh
items.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that fat covered by flesh is permitted, but a contradiction is raised from another statement by the same chain that the תַּרְבָּא דְּתוּתֵי (fat of the folds) is forbidden. Abaye resolves that in a live animal the fat is separated (פָּרוֹקֵי מִיפַּרְקָא), and Rabbi Yochanan confirms this tradition from the study hall.

sub.text: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.text_en: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that fat covered by flesh is permitted.
The Gemara raises a contradiction: the same chain of tradition also rules that the תַּרְבָּא דְּתוּתֵי (fat of the folds) is forbidden.
Abaye resolves the contradiction by explaining that in a live animal the fat is separated (פָּרוֹקֵי מִיפַּרְקָא), so the fat of the folds is not covered by flesh.
Rabbi Yochanan confirms that this tradition was taught in the study hall, that in a live animal the fat is separated.

items.text: Rulings on specific fats: meses, beit hakosot, and kelibotsta
items.text_en: Rulings on specific fats: meses, beit hakosot, and kelibotsta
items.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that fat on the meses (hemes) and beit hakosot (the place of the cups) is forbidden and carries karet, and this is the fat on the innards (על הקרב). Similarly, the fat of kelibotsta (a specific organ) is forbidden and carries karet, and this is the fat on the flanks (על הכסלים).

sub.text: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.text_en: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that the fat on the meses (hemes) and beit hakosot (the place of the cups) is forbidden and carries karet, identifying it as the fat on the innards (על הקרב).

sub.text_en: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the same chain rules that the fat of kelibotsta (a specific organ) is forbidden and carries karet, identifying it as the fat on the flanks (על הכסלים).

items.text: Discussion of forbidden sinews (chutin) in the hand
items.text_en: Discussion of forbidden sinews (chutin) in the hand
items.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that the sinews in the hand (חוּטִין שֶׁבַּיָּד) are forbidden. Rav Safra questions whether the Torah forbade eating meat entirely, and Rava responds by comparing to the prohibition of blood: if cut and salted, even for a pot it is fine.

sub.text: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.text_en: Rabbi Abba citing Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda citing Shmuel rules that the sinews in the hand (חוּטִין שֶׁבַּיָּד) are forbidden.
Rav Safra questions whether the Torah forbade eating meat entirely, implying that if sinews are forbidden, one could never eat meat.
Rava responds by comparing to the prohibition of blood: if the sinews are cut and salted, even for a pot it is fine, just as blood is permitted after salting.

items.text: Ruling on the head of the intestine (reish me'aya)
items.text_en: Ruling on the head of the intestine (reish me'aya)
items.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel rules that the head of the intestine (רֵישׁ מְעַיָּא) requires scraping (גְּרִירָה) and this is the fat on the small intestines (על הדקין).

sub.text: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel
sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel rules that the head of the intestine (רֵישׁ מְעַיָּא) requires scraping (גְּרִירָה) and this is the fat on the small intestines (על הדקין).

items.text: Sinews in the tail (chutin sheba'okez) and their details
items.text_en: Sinews in the tail (chutin sheba'okez) and their details
items.desc_en: Rav Yehuda rules that the sinews in the tail (חוּטִין שֶׁבָּעוֹקֶץ) are forbidden. There are five sinews in the double (בכפלא): three on the right and two on the left. The three split into two each, the two split into three each. The practical difference: if pulled while still warm they come out easily, otherwise one must dig after them.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda rules that the sinews in the tail (חוּטִין שֶׁבָּעוֹקֶץ) are forbidden, and details their number and arrangement: five sinews in the double (בכפלא), three on the right and two on the left, with specific splitting patterns, and a practical difference regarding removal while warm versus requiring digging afterward.

items.text: חמישה חוטין האסורים
items.text_en: Abaye's classification of five sinews: some due to fat, some due to blood
items.desc_en: Abaye (or Rav Yehuda) states that there are five sinews: three due to fat (תַּרְבָּא) and two due to blood (דְּמָא). Those of the spleen, double, and kidneys are due to fat; those of the hand and cheek are due to blood. The practical difference: those due to blood can be remedied by cutting and salting, but those due to fat have no remedy.
items.desc: אביי או רב יהודה מונים חמישה חוטין האסורים: שלושה משום חלב ושניים משום דם. החוטין שמשום דם ניתנים לתיקון על ידי חיתוך ומליחה, אך אלה שמשום חלב אין להם תקנה.

sub.desc_en: Abaye (or Rav Yehuda) states that there are five sinews: three due to fat (תַּרְבָּא) and two due to blood (דְּמָא), listing the specific sinews for each category.
sub.desc: אביי (או רב יהודה) מונה חמישה חוטין האסורים: שלושה משום חלב (של טחול, כפל וכליות) ושניים משום דם (של יד ולוע).

sub.text_en: Gemara's explanation of the practical difference
sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains the practical difference: sinews due to blood can be remedied by cutting and salting, but those due to fat have no remedy.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבארת את הנפקא מינה בין החוטין: אלו שמשום דם ניתנים לתיקון על ידי חיתוך ומליחה, ואילו אלו שמשום חלב אין להם תקנה.

items.text: חמישה קרומים האסורים
items.text_en: Rav Kahana's classification of five membranes (keramei)
items.desc_en: Rav Kahana (or Rav Yehuda) states that there are five membranes (קְרָמֵי): three due to fat and two due to blood. Those of the spleen, double, and kidneys are due to fat; those of the eggs (testicles) and the mokra (a specific organ) are due to blood.
items.desc: רב כהנא או רב יהודה מונים חמישה קרומים האסורים: שלושה משום חלב ושניים משום דם, ומפרט את מקומותיהם.

sub.desc_en: Rav Kahana (or Rav Yehuda) classifies five membranes (קְרָמֵי): three due to fat and two due to blood, specifying which organs each category applies to.
sub.desc: רב כהנא (או רב יהודה) מונה חמישה קרומים האסורים: שלושה משום חלב ושניים משום דם, ומפרט את מקומותיהם.

items.text: קרום שעל הטחול
items.text_en: Story of Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and the spleen membrane
items.desc_en: Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya was peeling a spleen for Levi the son of Rav Huna bar Chiyya, and fat was rising from the top. He was told to cut deeper. His father found him and said that the father of his mother (Rav Yirmeya bar Abba) said in the name of Rav that the Torah only forbade the membrane on the teat (על הדד) alone. A contradiction is raised from Rav Hamnuna's baraita that the membrane on the spleen is forbidden but not liable, and the Gemara questions if it refers to the teat or the entire spleen. The response is: if it was taught, it was taught.
items.desc: מעשה ברב יהודה בר אושעיא שקלף טחול, ונחלקו אם יש להסיר רק את הקרום העליון או גם התחתון. רב הונא בר חייא אומר בשם רב שרק העליון אסור, אך רב המנונא מביא ברייתא שאוסרת את כולו.

sub.text_en: Narrative (Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and Levi)
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya was peeling a spleen for Levi, and fat rose from the top; Levi told him to cut deeper.
sub.desc: מסופר שרב יהודה בר אושעיא קלף טחול ללוי, ולוי ביקש שיוריד גם מהחלק התחתון; אביו רב הונא בר חייא אמר לו בשם רב (דרך רב ירמיה בר אבא) שהתורה אסרה רק את הקרום שעל החלק העליון (הדד).

sub.text_en: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba citing Rav
sub.desc_en: His father found him and said that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said in the name of Rav that the Torah only forbade the membrane on the teat (על הדד) alone.
sub.desc: מסופר שרב יהודה בר אושעיא קלף טחול ללוי, ולוי ביקש שיוריד גם מהחלק התחתון; אביו רב הונא בר חייא אמר לו בשם רב (דרך רב ירמיה בר אבא) שהתורה אסרה רק את הקרום שעל החלק העליון (הדד).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a contradiction from Rav Hamnuna's baraita that the membrane on the spleen is forbidden but not liable, and questions whether it refers to the teat or the entire spleen.
sub.desc: לוי מקשה מברייתא של רב המנונא שאסרה את כל קרום הטחול, ומדייק שאם הברייתא עוסקת רק בעליון לא היה נאמר 'אין חייבים עליו', אלא ודאי היא עוסקת בכל הטחול.

sub.desc_en: The response is: if it was taught, it was taught, accepting the baraita without further resolution.
sub.desc: לוי מקשה מברייתא של רב המנונא שאסרה את כל קרום הטחול, ומדייק שאם הברייתא עוסקת רק בעליון לא היה נאמר 'אין חייבים עליו', אלא ודאי היא עוסקת בכל הטחול.

items.text: קרומי הטחול והכליה
items.text_en: Resolving contradictions about membranes on spleen and kidney
items.desc_en: Rav Hamnuna's baraita states that the membrane on the spleen is forbidden but not liable, and the membrane on the kidney is forbidden but not liable. Another baraita says one is liable. The Gemara resolves: regarding the spleen, the contradiction is not difficult—one refers to opposite the teat (כנגד הדד), the other to not opposite the teat. Regarding the kidney, the contradiction is not difficult—one refers to the upper kidney (עילָּאָה), the other to the lower kidney (תַּתָּאָה).
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא האוסרת קרום שעל הטחול והכליה ללא חיוב כרת, ומקשה מברייתא אחרת המחייבת כרת. מתרצים: לגבי טחול, החיוב הוא כנגד הדד, והפטור שלא כנגד הדד; לגבי כליה, החיוב בעליונה והפטור בתחתונה.

sub.desc_en: Rav Hamnuna cites a baraita stating that the membrane on the spleen and the membrane on the kidney are forbidden but not punishable by karet.
sub.desc: רב המנונא מביא ברייתא האוסרת קרום שעל הטחול והכליה, אך ללא חיוב כרת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that another baraita states one is liable (חייבין) for these membranes, contradicting the first baraita.
sub.desc: רב המנונא מביא ברייתא האוסרת קרום שעל הטחול והכליה, אך ללא חיוב כרת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves: regarding the spleen, the contradiction is not difficult—one baraita refers to the membrane opposite the teat (כנגד הדד), the other to not opposite the teat; regarding the kidney, one refers to the upper kidney (עילָּאָה), the other to the lower kidney (תַּתָּאָה).
sub.desc: מתרץ לגבי טחול: החיוב הוא כנגד הדד, והפטור שלא כנגד הדד.

items.text: ביצים חבוטות
items.text_en: Dispute about boiled eggs (bei'ei chashilata)
items.desc_en: Regarding boiled eggs (בֵּיעֵי חֲשִׁילָתָא), Rav Ami and Rav Asi disagree—one forbids and one permits. The daf cuts off mid-sentence.
items.desc: מחלוקת בין רב אמי ורב אסי לגבי ביצים שנמעכו בעודן מחוברות: אחד אוסר ואחד מתיר, ומתחיל להסביר את טעם האוסר.

sub.desc_en: The gemara introduces a dispute between Rav Ami and Rav Asi regarding boiled eggs (בֵּיעֵי חֲשִׁילָתָא), with one forbidding and one permitting, but the text cuts off mid-sentence.
sub.desc: פותח במחלוקת בין רב אמי ורב אסי לגבי ביצים שנמעכו בעודן מחוברות, ומתחיל להסביר את טעם האוסר.

items.text: מחלוקת בביצים מרוסקות: האם הן אבר מן החי
items.text_en: Debate on the status of eggs from a terefah animal
items.desc_en: The Gemara debates whether eggs found inside a terefah animal are considered a limb from a living animal (אבר מן החי) or permitted. One view says they are forbidden because they do not grow, while another says they are permitted because they do not putrefy, indicating life. The counterarguments are that lack of putrefaction is due to lack of air, and lack of growth is due to weakness.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בביצים מרוסקות (אשכים כתושים) שנמצאו בתוך בעל חיים. יש הסוברים שהן אסורות משום שהן נחשבות לאבר מן החי, ויש הסוברים שהן מותרות משום שיש בהן חיות. מובאים טעמים לשני הצדדים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether eggs that do not grow are considered a limb from a living animal (אבר מן החי) and thus forbidden.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בטעם האוסר: מכיוון שהאשכים המרוסקים אינם מתרפאים, הם נחשבים לאבר מן החי ואסורים; ומביאה את טעם המתיר: מכיוון שאינם מסריחים, יש בהם חיות.

sub.desc_en: The first answer permits the eggs because they do not putrefy, indicating they have life.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בטעם האוסר: מכיוון שהאשכים המרוסקים אינם מתרפאים, הם נחשבים לאבר מן החי ואסורים; ומביאה את טעם המתיר: מכיוון שאינם מסריחים, יש בהם חיות.

sub.desc_en: The objection counters that the lack of putrefaction is due to lack of air, not life.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת את טענות שני הצדדים: האוסר מסביר שאי-הסרחון נובע מחוסר אוויר, והמתיר מסביר שאי-ההתרפאות נובעת מחולשה.

sub.desc_en: The objection counters that the lack of growth is due to weakness, not being a limb from a living animal.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת את טענות שני הצדדים: האוסר מסביר שאי-הסרחון נובע מחוסר אוויר, והמתיר מסביר שאי-ההתרפאות נובעת מחולשה.

items.text: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling on cooked eggs
items.text_en: Rabbi Yochanan's ruling on cooked eggs
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan tells Rav Shemen bar Abba that cooked eggs (ביעי חשילתא) are permitted, but advises him not to eat them out of respect for his mother's tradition (ואל תטוש תורת אמך).
