items.text_en: Derivation from bikurim and its refutation
items.desc_en: The Gemara suggests deriving from bikurim, citing Rabbi Yosei's teaching that the verse 'pri' excludes liquids, but 'tavi' includes them if one brought grapes and pressed them. However, this is refuted because bikurim require recitation and placement (kriyah vehanachah).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes deriving the rule from bikurim (first fruits), then asks how bikurim themselves are derived.
Rabbi Yosei teaches that the verse 'פרי' (fruit) excludes liquids, but 'תביא' (you shall bring) includes them if one brought grapes and pressed them.
The Gemara refutes the derivation from bikurim because bikurim require recitation and placement (קרייה והנחה), which other cases do not.

items.text: Derivation from terumah and its refutation
items.text_en: Derivation from terumah and its refutation
items.desc_en: The Gemara then suggests deriving from terumah, which is linked to bikurim via the verse 'uterumat yadecha'. But this is refuted because terumah carries the penalties of death and an additional fifth (chomesh).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests deriving the law of liquids from terumah (priestly portion) instead.
The Gemara asks how terumah itself is derived, and answers that it is linked to bikurim (first fruits) via the verse 'uterumat yadecha'.
The Gemara refutes the derivation from terumah because terumah carries the penalties of death and an additional fifth (חומש), which bikurim do not.

items.text: Derivation from both terumah and bikurim, or one of them with another case
items.text_en: Derivation from both terumah and bikurim, or one of them with another case
items.desc_en: The Gemara tries deriving from both terumah and bikurim together, but the same objection applies (both have death and chomesh). It then suggests deriving from terumah and one of the earlier cases, or from bikurim and one of them.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara suggests deriving the law from both תרומה (terumah) and ביכורים (first fruits) together, but immediately notes the objection that both share the features of death and חומש (the fifth penalty).
The Gemara proposes deriving the law from תרומה (terumah) combined with one of the earlier cases, or from ביכורים (first fruits) combined with one of them.

items.text: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on terumah liquids
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on terumah liquids
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a mishnah where Rabbi Eliezer obligates payment of principal and an additional fifth for liquids from various fruits in terumah, while Rabbi Yehoshua exempts. The dispute is explained: Rabbi Eliezer uses the method of 'don minah u'minah' (derive from bikurim both the principle and its application to all species), while Rabbi Yehoshua uses 'don minah v'okei b'atreh' (derive the principle but limit it to wine and oil, as in terumah itself).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a mishnah where Rabbi Eliezer obligates payment of principal and an additional fifth for liquids from various fruits in terumah, while Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

The Gemara asks what principle underlies their dispute, framing it as a disagreement between the methods of 'דון מינה ומינה' (derive from bikurim both the principle and its application to all species) and 'דון מינה ואוקי באתרה' (derive the principle but limit it to wine and oil, as in terumah itself).
Rabbi Eliezer holds the method of 'דון מינה ומינה' (derive from bikurim both the principle and its application to all species), so terumah liquids from all fruits are treated like bikurim liquids.
Rabbi Yehoshua holds the method of 'דון מינה ואוקי באתרה' (derive the principle but limit it to wine and oil, as in terumah itself), so only liquids from olives and grapes are included.

items.text: Application of Rabbi Yehoshua's view to bikurim and orlah
items.text_en: Application of Rabbi Yehoshua's view to bikurim and orlah
items.desc_en: The Gemara identifies that the mishnah stating bikurim are only brought from olives and grapes follows Rabbi Yehoshua's view, who derives bikurim from terumah via 'don minah v'okei b'atreh'. Similarly, the mishnah that lashes for orlah are only given for liquids from olives and grapes follows Rabbi Yehoshua's view.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: In accordance with whose opinion is the mishnah that bikurim are only brought as liquids from olives and grapes?
The Gemara answers: It is Rabbi Yehoshua, who holds the principle of 'don minah v'okei b'atreh' and derives the halakha of bikurim from terumah.
The Gemara asks: In accordance with whose opinion is the mishnah that lashes for orlah are only given for liquids from olives and grapes?
The Gemara answers: It is Rabbi Yehoshua, who holds the principle of 'don minah v'okei b'atreh' and derives the halakha of bikurim from terumah.

items.text: Definition of 'Alal'
items.text_en: Definition of 'Alal'
items.desc_en: The Gemara introduces the term 'alal' from the Mishnah and presents two definitions: Rabbi Yochanan says it is gristle (marteka), and Reish Lakish says it is flesh that the knife has detached.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces the term 'אלל' from the Mishnah and asks what it means.
Rabbi Yochanan defines 'אלל' as gristle (marteka).
Reish Lakish defines 'אלל' as flesh that the knife has detached.

items.text: Objection from a Biblical verse
items.text_en: Objection from a Biblical verse
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from a verse (Job 13:4) that uses 'elil' meaning worthless, which supports the gristle interpretation since gristle has no healing value, but the flesh-detached interpretation would imply it is healable. The Gemara resolves that the dispute is only about the 'alal' in the Mishnah, not in the verse.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from the verse (Job 13:4) 'רֹפְאֵי אֱלִל' (worthless healers), arguing that for Rabbi Yochanan's interpretation (gristle) the term fits since gristle has no healing value, but for Reish Lakish's interpretation (flesh detached by a knife) it would imply the flesh is healable, contradicting the verse.
The Gemara resolves that the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish is only about the 'alal' in the Mishnah, not about the 'elil' in the verse, where all agree it means worthless.

items.text: Support from Rabbi Yehuda's statement
items.text_en: Support from Rabbi Yehuda's statement
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Yehuda says that collected 'alal' the size of an olive incurs liability, and Rav Huna adds that it must be collected. This supports Reish Lakish's view that it is flesh, as gristle would not be significant. The Gemara notes that the dispute is only according to the Rabbis, not Rabbi Yehuda.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita where Rabbi Yehuda rules that collected 'alal' the size of an olive incurs liability, and Rav Huna adds that it must be collected.
The Gemara explains that this supports Reish Lakish's view that 'alal' is flesh, because an olive-sized amount of flesh is significant.
The Gemara objects that according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says 'alal' is gristle (מרטקא), an olive-sized amount would be mere wood and not significant.
The Gemara resolves that the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish applies only according to the Rabbis, not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

items.text: Dispute according to the Rabbis
items.text_en: Dispute according to the Rabbis
items.desc_en: The Gemara clarifies that the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish is according to the Rabbis: Rabbi Yochanan says gristle also combines for impurity, while Reish Lakish says only flesh detached by the knife combines, not gristle.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish is according to the Rabbis: Rabbi Yochanan holds that gristle (מרטקא) also combines for impurity, while Reish Lakish holds that only flesh detached by the knife combines, not gristle.

items.text: בירור דין בשר שפלטתו סכין
items.text_en: Clarification of 'flesh detached by a knife'
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the scenario of flesh detached by a knife: if one intended for it, it is susceptible to impurity even alone; if not, it is nullified. Rabbi Avin and Rabbi Meyasha offer two explanations: either part of it was intended, or part was detached by an animal and part by a knife.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת באיזה אופן מדובר בבשר שפלטתו סכין, ומתרצת בשני תירוצים: האחד שמדובר במקצתו שחישב עליו, והשני שמדובר במקצתו שפלטתו חיה ומקצתו שפלטתו סכין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks about the scenario of flesh detached by a knife: if one intended for it, it is susceptible to impurity even alone; if not, it is nullified.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על דין בשר שפלטתו סכין: אם חישב עליו הרי הוא מטמא בפני עצמו, ואם לא חישב עליו הרי ביטלו.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Avin explains that part of the flesh was intended for use, making it susceptible to impurity.
sub.desc: תירוץ אחד: מדובר במקצת הבשר שחישב עליו, ולכן אינו מטמא בפני עצמו אך מצטרף.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Meyasha explains that part of the flesh was detached by an animal and part by a knife, creating a mixed case.
sub.desc: תירוץ שני: מדובר במקצת שנחתך על ידי חיה (שאינו מבטל) ומקצת על ידי סכין (שמבטל), ולכן ספק מצטרף.

items.text: פירוש חלקי הגוף המצטרפים לבשר
items.text_en: Impurity of beak and claws
items.desc_en: The Gemara discusses a Mishnah that the beak and claws of a bird are susceptible to impurity and combine. It questions how the beak, which is wood-like, can be impure. Rabbi Elazar explains it refers to the lower beak, and Rav Papa specifies the lower beak of the upper jaw. For claws, Rabbi Elazar says it is the part embedded in the flesh. For horns, Rav Papa says it is where they cut and blood comes out.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בפירוש המשנה העוסקת בחרטום, ציפורניים וקרניים המצטרפים לבשר לטומאת אוכלים. רבי אלעזר ורב פפא מבארים שאין מדובר בחלק הקשה אלא בחלק הרך הסמוך לבשר.

items.text: דיני טומאת אוכלים בשחיטה לנכרי ובבהמה טמאה
items.text_en: Impurity of slaughtering an animal and need for preparation
items.desc_en: The Gemara discusses a case similar to the previous: one who slaughters an animal. Rabbi Asi says that Israelites slaughtering an impure animal and a gentile slaughtering a pure animal require intent and water-preparation from another source. The Gemara questions why water-preparation is needed if the meat will eventually become impure with severe impurity, citing a principle from Rabbi Yishmael's school that only items that do not become severely impure need preparation. A baraita with Rabbi Yosei's statement is introduced but cut off.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בדין השוחט בהמה טמאה לישראל או בהמה טהורה לנכרי, ודורשת מחשבה והכשר מים לקבלת טומאת אוכלים. הגמרא מקשה על הצורך בהכשר ומתרצת על פי הכלל שדבר שסופו לטמא טומאה חמורה אינו צריך הכשר, ומביאה ברייתא של רבי יוסי בעניין נבלת עוף טהור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces a case similar to the previous: one who slaughters an animal, and Rabbi Asi states that an Israelite slaughtering an impure animal and a gentile slaughtering a pure animal require intent and water-preparation from another source.
sub.desc: פתיחת חטיבה: הצגת דין המשנה בדומה לשוחט בהמה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why water-preparation is needed if the meat will eventually become impure with severe impurity, citing the principle that anything destined for severe impurity does not require preparation.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: מדוע צריך הכשר, הרי סופו לטמא טומאה חמורה ואינו צריך הכשר?

sub.text_en: Supporting baraita from Rabbi Yishmael's school
sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita from Rabbi Yishmael's school that derives from the verse 'וכי יותן מים על זרע' (and when water is placed on seed) that only items not destined for severe impurity require preparation.
sub.desc: הבאת ברייתא מדבי רבי ישמעאל המלמדת שרק דבר שאין סופו לטמא טומאה חמורה צריך הכשר.

sub.desc_en: A baraita with Rabbi Yosei's statement is introduced but cut off, questioning why a pure bird's carcass requires intent but not preparation.
sub.desc: הבאת ברייתא נוספת של רבי יוסי השואלת מדוע נבלת עוף טהור צריכה מחשבה אך לא הכשר.

items.text: Chizkiyah's answer to the opening question
items.text_en: Chizkiyah's answer to the opening question
items.desc_en: Chizkiyah explains why a convulsing animal can be exempt from severe impurity: because one can drag it and reduce it to less than an olive's bulk.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that a convulsing animal eventually becomes a נבלה (carrion) with severe טומאה (impurity), so how can it be exempt now?
Chizkiyah answers that one can drag the animal and reduce its bulk to less than a כזית (olive's bulk), preventing severe טומאה (impurity).

items.text: Rabbi Yirmeyah's challenge and resolution
items.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeyah's challenge and resolution
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeyah challenges Chizkiyah's view based on a dispute between Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan regarding whether a convulsing animal is subject to limb impurity. Rabbi Zeira resolves that the animal has left the category of living but not yet entered that of dead.

sub.text: Rabbi Yirmeyah's challenge to Rabbi Zeira
sub.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeyah's challenge to Rabbi Zeira
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeyah challenges Rabbi Zeira by citing a dispute between Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan regarding whether a convulsing animal after slaughter is subject to limb impurity (טומאת איברים).
The gemara explains the reasoning behind the dispute: Chizkiyah considers the animal dead, while Rabbi Yochanan considers it not yet dead.
Rabbi Zeira resolves the contradiction by stating that the convulsing animal has left the category of living but has not yet entered the category of dead.

items.text: The core dispute and Rabbi Elazar's ruling
items.text_en: The core dispute and Rabbi Elazar's ruling
items.desc_en: The Gemara presents the core dispute between Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan regarding limb impurity for a convulsing animal. Rabbi Elazar advises to hold Rabbi Yochanan's view, supported by a baraita of Rav Oshaya.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara restates the core dispute between Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yochanan regarding whether a convulsing animal after shechita has limb impurity.
Rabbi Elazar rules to adopt Rabbi Yochanan's view, citing that Rav Oshaya's baraita supports him.

items.text: Baraita of Rav Oshaya on impurity and Noahide laws
items.text_en: Baraita of Rav Oshaya on impurity and Noahide laws
items.desc_en: Rav Oshaya's baraita details the impurity status of a convulsing animal slaughtered by an Israelite for a gentile or by a gentile for an Israelite, including food impurity but not carcass impurity, and the prohibition of limbs for Noahides.

sub.desc_en: Rav Oshaya states the rule: an Israelite who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a gentile, cutting two simanim or their majority while the animal convulses, imparts food impurity but not carcass impurity.
Rav Oshaya rules that a limb separating from the convulsing animal is like a limb from a living animal, and is prohibited to Noahides even after the animal's death.
Rav Oshaya states that if only one siman or its majority was cut, or if the animal was stabbed, it imparts no food impurity.
Rav Oshaya rules that a gentile who slaughters a kosher animal for an Israelite, while it convulses, imparts food impurity but not carcass impurity.
Rav Oshaya repeats the rule that a limb from this convulsing animal is like a limb from a living animal, prohibited to Noahides even after death.
Rav Oshaya concludes that if only one siman or its majority was cut, or if the animal was stabbed, it imparts no impurity at all.

items.text: Laws of slaughter by a gentile and an Israelite completing it
items.text_en: Laws of slaughter by a gentile and an Israelite completing it
items.desc_en: The baraita rules that if a gentile slaughters in a place that does not make the animal a terefah and an Israelite completes it, it is valid; but if an Israelite slaughters and a gentile completes, it is invalid.

sub.desc_en: The baraita rules that if a gentile slaughters in a place that does not render the animal a טריפה (ritually unfit) and an Israelite completes the slaughter, it is valid.
The baraita rules that if an Israelite slaughters, whether in a place that renders the animal a טריפה (ritually unfit) or not, and a gentile completes the slaughter, it is invalid.

items.text: Permissibility of eating from the animal before death
items.text_en: Permissibility of eating from the animal before death
items.desc_en: The baraita describes how one may eat from the animal before its death by cutting an olive's bulk from the slaughter site, salting, rinsing, and waiting until death. This supports Rav Idi bar Avin's statement about health.

sub.text: Baraita — eating from a convulsing animal
sub.text_en: Baraita — eating from a convulsing animal
sub.desc_en: The baraita teaches that one who wishes to eat from an animal before death may cut an olive-sized piece from the slaughter-site, salt it, rinse it, wait for death, and then eat it; both Jew and gentile are permitted.

sub.text: Support for Rav Idi bar Avin
sub.text_en: Support for Rav Idi bar Avin
sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that this baraita supports Rav Idi bar Avin, who taught a similar ruling in the name of Rav Yitzchak bar Ashian for someone who wants to regain health.

items.text: Rabbi Elazar's inquiry about delay and pressing
items.text_en: Rabbi Elazar's inquiry about delay and pressing
items.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar asks about the status if one delayed or pressed during slaughter. An elder reports Rabbi Yochanan's ruling that it requires proper slaughter like a pure animal, and Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak explains this refers to checking the knife.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar inquires about the status of a convulsing animal if one paused (שָׁהָה) or trampled (דָּרַס) during the shechita.

sub.text: The elder (some elder) in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
sub.text_en: The elder (some elder) in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
sub.desc_en: An elder answers in the name of Rabbi Yochanan that the animal requires the halachic fitness of shechita like a pure animal; Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak explains that this refers to checking the knife (בְּדִיקַת סַכִּין).
The gemara asks what 'proper slaughter' (הכשר) refers to in this context.
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak explains that 'proper slaughter' (הכשר) refers to checking the knife.

items.text: Rabbi Zeira's question about saving swallowed items
items.text_en: Rabbi Zeira's question about saving swallowed items
items.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira asks Rav Sheishet whether a convulsing animal can save swallowed items from impurity. Rav Sheishet questions the logic, and Abaye concludes it does not save because it has food impurity, yet one who copulates with it is liable since it lacks carcass impurity.

sub.text: Rabbi Zeira's question to Rav Sheishet
sub.text_en: Rabbi Zeira's question to Rav Sheishet
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira asks Rav Sheishet whether a convulsing animal can save swallowed items from impurity.
Rav Sheishet objects: if the animal has food impurity (טומאת אוכלין), how can it save?
Rabbi Zeira counters: since it lacks carcass impurity (טומאת נבלות), it should save.
Abaye concludes: it does not save because it has food impurity, yet one who copulates with it is liable since it lacks carcass impurity.

items.text: Rabbi Yehudah on the alal and Rav Huna's statements
items.text_en: Rabbi Yehudah on the alal and Rav Huna's statements
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites Rabbi Yehudah's opinion on the alal (a certain part), and Rav Huna states it applies only when he gathered it. Rav Huna also rules that two half-olives on the skin are nullified by the skin.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites Rabbi Yehudah's opinion regarding the alal (a certain part).
Rav Huna states that Rabbi Yehudah's ruling applies only when he gathered the alal.
Rav Huna further rules that two half-olive-sized pieces on the skin are nullified by the skin.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא על רב הונה: אליבא דמאן?
items.text_en: Resolving the contradiction in Rabbi Yishmael's position
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whose opinion the previous Mishnah follows. It suggests that if it follows Rabbi Yishmael, he holds that skin does not nullify flesh, so the ruling is problematic. The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Yishmael only says skin does not nullify when the animal expelled the fetus alive, but if it was cut out with a knife, the skin does nullify.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת לאיזה תנא התכוון רב הונה בקביעתו, ומציעה שאם כרבי ישמעאל – הרי סבר שאין העור מבטל, ואם כרבי עקיבא – פשיטא. לבסוף מתרצת שדברי רב הונה כרבי ישמעאל, ובחלוקה בין פליטת חיה לפליטת סכין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whose opinion the Mishnah follows, noting that if it follows Rabbi Yishmael, he holds that skin does not nullify flesh, creating a problem.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת לאיזה תנא התכוון רב הונה באמרו שהעור מבטל את הבשר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Yishmael only says skin does not nullify when the animal expelled the fetus alive, but if it was cut out with a knife, the skin does nullify.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת שדברי רב הונה כרבי ישמעאל, ומבחינה בין פליטת חיה לפליטת סכין: בפליטת חיה העור אינו מבטל, בפליטת סכין – מבטל.

items.text: סיוע מהמשנה על אָלָל המכונס ומחלוקת רבי שמעון ורבי עקיבא
items.text_en: Analyzing Rav Huna's statement in light of the dispute
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Yehuda says that collected meat of a carcass requires a kezayit to impart impurity, and Rav Huna adds that this applies only if he collected it. The Gemara analyzes whether Rav Huna follows Rabbi Yishmael or Rabbi Akiva, concluding that Rav Huna follows Rabbi Akiva, who holds that skin nullifies flesh even when cut with a knife, as the Mishnah's reason is that the skin nullifies them.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה סיוע מהמשנה (רבי יהודה באָלָל המכונס) ופירוש רב הונה. דנה אם רב הונה כרבי ישמעאל (גם בפליטת סכין לא מבטל) או כרבי עקיבא (שהעור מבטל, ואף בפליטת חיה). מסיקה שרב הונה כרבי עקיבא, ומפרטת שסברת רבי עקיבא אינה תלויה בצורת הפליטה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita where Rabbi Yehuda rules that collected meat of a carcass requires a kezayit to impart impurity, and Rav Huna adds that this applies only if he collected it.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה את משנת רבי יהודה באלל המכונס ופירוש רב הונה כראיה לסוגיה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes that if the knife-cut case is not nullified even for Rabbi Yishmael, then Rav Huna follows Rabbi Yishmael.
sub.desc: אם נאמר שפליטת סכין אינה מבטלת לרבי ישמעאל, רב הונה כרבי ישמעאל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: if the knife-cut case is nullified for Rabbi Yishmael, then whom does Rav Huna follow?
sub.desc: אם נאמר שפליטת סכין מבטלת לרבי ישמעאל, במה יסביר רב הונה את דבריו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that the knife-cut case is not nullified for Rabbi Yishmael, so Rav Huna must follow Rabbi Akiva.
sub.desc: הגמרא קובעת: לרבי ישמעאל גם פליטת סכין אינה מבטלת, ורב הונה כרבי עקיבא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that it is obvious, but suggests that Rabbi Akiva's nullification might apply only to knife-cut cases, not to animal-ejection cases.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: פשיטא שרבי עקיבא מבטל, אך היינו יכולים לחלק בין פליטת חיה לפליטת סכין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that Rav Huna teaches that Rabbi Akiva's reason is that the skin nullifies the flesh, applying equally to both knife-cut and animal-ejection cases.
sub.desc: רב הונה משמיענו שטעם רבי עקיבא הוא שהעור מבטל, ואין חילוק בין פליטת חיה לפליטת סכין.

items.text: משנת 'אלו שעורותיהן כבשרן'
items.text_en: Mishnah: List of skins that are like flesh
items.desc_en: The Mishnah lists skins that are considered like flesh for impurity purposes: human skin, pig skin, the soft skin of a young camel, the skin of a calf's head, the skin of the hooves, the skin of the place of shame, the skin of a fetus, the skin under the tail, and the skins of certain reptiles. Rabbi Yehuda adds the skin of a wild pig. If these are processed or walked on sufficiently, they become pure, except human skin. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says eight creeping creatures have skins.
items.desc: המשנה מונה חיות ועורות הנחשבים כבשר לטומאה: עור אדם, עור חזיר (ישוב ובר), עור גמל רכה, עור ראש עגל רך, ועוד. מנמקת את החריגים ודיני טומאה בעיבודם.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by listing the skins that are considered like flesh for impurity purposes, including human skin, pig skin, soft camel skin, calf head skin, hoof skin, shame-place skin, fetus skin, under-tail skin, and reptile skins.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת ברשימת עורות הנחשבים כבשר לטומאה: עור אדם ועור חזיר ישוב.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yehuda adds the skin of a wild pig and identifies the לטאה (gecko) as being like a חולדה (weasel).
sub.desc: רבי יהודה מוסיף גם את עור חזיר הבר לרשימה.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah rules that if these skins are processed or walked on sufficiently, they become pure, except for human skin.
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שעיבוד העורות מטהר אותם, פרט לעור אדם שנשאר בטומאתו.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri states that eight creeping creatures have skins (that are considered like flesh).
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת שעיבוד העורות מטהר אותם, פרט לעור אדם שנשאר בטומאתו.

items.text: ביאור דיני עור אדם: גזירה שמא יעשה אביו ואמו שטיחין
items.text_en: Gemara: The decree regarding human skin
items.desc_en: Ulla states that by Torah law, human skin is pure, but the Sages decreed it impure lest one make a rug from his parents' skin. There are two versions of this teaching: one on the Mishnah's first clause (the list) and one on the latter clause (processing). The one who teaches it on the first clause applies it even more to the latter clause, while the one who teaches it on the latter clause holds that the first clause's impurity is Torah law.
items.desc: עולא מבאר שעור אדם טהור מן התורה, וחכמים גזרו טומאה שמא יעשה אדם עורות אביו ואמו שטיחין. הגמרא מביאה שתי גרסאות – על רישא ועל סיפא. מפרשת את המחלוקת: מאן דתני ארישא – כל שכן אסיפא.

sub.desc_en: Ulla states that by Torah law human skin is pure, but the Sages decreed it impure lest one make a rug from his parents' skin.
sub.desc: עולא פותח וקובע שעור אדם טהור מן התורה, וחכמים גזרו עליו טומאה שמא יעשה עורות אביו ואמו שטיחין.

sub.desc_en: There is a version that teaches Ulla's statement on the latter clause of the Mishnah (processing), applying the decree to processed human skin as well.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה גרסה חלופית, שבה עולא אמר את דבריו על הסיפא של המשנה (עור שעבדו).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the one who teaches Ulla's statement on the first clause applies it even more to the latter clause, while the one who teaches it on the latter clause holds that the first clause's impurity is Torah law.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת את ההבדל בין הגרסאות: מאן דתני ארישא – כל שכן אסיפא, ומאן דתני אסיפא – ברישא טומאה דאורייתא.

items.text: Dispute about pig skin
items.text_en: Dispute about pig skin
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the dispute is between the Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Yehuda regarding pig skin. One holds that the domesticated pig's skin is tough, while the wild pig's skin is soft, and the other holds that the wild pig's skin is also soft.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the dispute is between the Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Yehuda regarding pig skin.
The Gemara explains that one opinion holds the domesticated pig's skin is tough and the wild pig's skin is soft, while the other holds that the wild pig's skin is also soft.

items.text: Definition of a young camel and related inquiries
items.text_en: Definition of a young camel and related inquiries
items.desc_en: Ulla quotes Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that a young camel is one that has not yet been loaded. Rabbi Yirmeya asks about a camel that has reached the age of loading but has not been loaded, and Abaye asks about one that has been loaded before its time; these remain unresolved. Resh Lakish and Rabbi Zeira also inquire about this definition, with responses from their students, and the Gemara notes the difference between the powerful of Eretz Yisrael and the pious of Babylonia.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the definition of a 'young camel' whose hide is considered like its flesh.

sub.text: Ulla citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
sub.text_en: Ulla citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
sub.desc_en: Ulla reports in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that a young camel is one that has not yet been loaded.
Rabbi Yirmeya asks about a camel that has reached the age of loading but has not yet been loaded.
Abaye asks about a camel that has been loaded before its time.
Both inquiries remain unresolved, marked by 'תיקו' (let it stand).

sub.text: Resh Lakish's inquiry and Rabbi Yishmael bar Abba's response
sub.text_en: Resh Lakish's inquiry and Rabbi Yishmael bar Abba's response
sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish asks the same question, and Rabbi Yishmael bar Abba cites Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's definition; Resh Lakish rebukes him for not citing it in his own name.

sub.text: Rabbi Zeira's inquiry and Ravin bar Chinana's response
sub.text_en: Rabbi Zeira's inquiry and Ravin bar Chinana's response
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Zeira asks the same question, and Ravin bar Chinana cites Ulla's version; Rabbi Zeira criticizes him for merely repeating what he already knew.
The Gemara notes the difference between the powerful of Eretz Yisrael and the pious of Babylonia in how they handle such inquiries.

items.text: Definition of a young calf
items.text_en: Definition of a young calf
items.desc_en: The Gemara discusses the definition of a young calf for the skin of its head. Ulla says it is a year-old calf, while Rabbi Yochanan says it is any calf that is still nursing. The Gemara raises an inquiry about how Ulla's statement was phrased.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: How young is a 'young calf' whose head-skin is considered as its flesh?
Ulla answers: A calf within its first year (בן שנתו).
Rabbi Yochanan answers: Any calf that is still nursing.
The Gemara raises an inquiry: How was Ulla's statement phrased — does he require both that it is within its first year and that it is nursing?

items.text: מחלוקת עולא ורבי יוחנן על גיל העגל
items.text_en: Opening dispute: Rabbi Yochanan vs. Ulla on suckling vs. year-old calf
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan says a calf is impure only while it suckles; Ulla argues it is impure whether or not it suckles if it is within its first year. Rabbi Yochanan clarifies that his statement 'all the time it suckles' implies the condition of suckling is necessary.
items.desc: הגמרא מבררת את מחלוקת עולא ורבי יוחנן האם עגל נחשב 'רך' רק כשהוא יונק, או גם כשהוא בן שנה ואינו יונק. המסקנה היא שרבי יוחנן סובר שכל זמן שיונק נחשב רך, ועולא סובר שצריך גם בן שנה וגם יונק.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan states that a calf is impure only while it suckles.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת בפירוש אפשרי למחלוקת: רבי יוחנן אמר לעולא שעגל רך כל זמן שיונק.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether Ulla holds that a calf is impure within its first year regardless of suckling.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה אפשרות חלופית: אולי עולא סובר שעגל רך רק כשהוא בן שנה, ורבי יוחנן מצריך גם בן שנה וגם יונק.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan clarifies that the calf must be both within its first year and suckling.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה אפשרות חלופית: אולי עולא סובר שעגל רך רק כשהוא בן שנה, ורבי יוחנן מצריך גם בן שנה וגם יונק.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Yochanan's statement 'all the time it suckles' implies suckling is necessary, and if he meant otherwise he would have said 'and it suckles'.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ראיה ומכריעה: מדברי רבי יוחנן שסתם שאמר 'כל זמן שיונק', משמע שאינו מצריך 'והוא שיונק', ולכן המסקנה היא שרבי יוחנן סובר שכל זמן שיונק רך, אפילו לאחר שנתו.

items.text: עור הראש של עגל הרך – האם מטמא
items.text_en: Resh Lakish asks Rabbi Yochanan about the head skin of a young calf
items.desc_en: Resh Lakish asks whether the skin of a young calf's head is susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Yochanan answers it is not, and warns Resh Lakish not to challenge him because he teaches this as a singular statement.
items.desc: ריש לקיש שואל את רבי יוחנן האם עור הראש של עגל הרך מטמא. רבי יוחנן עונה שאינו מטמא, ומסביר שהמשנה הסוברת שעור זה כבשר היא דעת יחיד, ואין הלכה כמותה.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish asks Rabbi Yochanan whether the skin of a young calf's head is susceptible to impurity.
sub.desc: ריש לקיש שואל את רבי יוחנן האם עור הראש של עגל הרך מטמא.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan answers that it is not susceptible to impurity.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן עונה שאינו מטמא.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish objects by citing the Mishnah's list of skins treated like flesh, which includes the skin of a young calf's head.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן עונה שאינו מטמא.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan warns Resh Lakish not to challenge him, explaining that he teaches this as a singular statement (not as the accepted ruling).
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן עונה שאינו מטמא.

items.text: Tannaitic source: slaughtering an olah to burn a olive-sized piece of skin under the tail
items.text_en: Tannaitic source: slaughtering an olah to burn a olive-sized piece of skin under the tail
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches: slaughtering an olah to burn an olive-sized piece of skin under the tail outside its proper place disqualifies the sacrifice with no karet; outside its proper time makes it piggul and liable for karet.

sub.desc_en: A baraita teaches that slaughtering an olah to burn an olive-sized piece of skin under the tail outside its proper place disqualifies without karet, but outside its proper time makes it piggul with karet.

items.text: Elazar ben Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon on skins considered like flesh
items.text_en: Elazar ben Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon on skins considered like flesh
items.desc_en: Elazar ben Yehuda citing Rabbi Yaakov, and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda citing Rabbi Shimon, list specific skins (of soles, head of a young calf, under the tail, and the house of shame) that the Sages treat as flesh for impurity.

sub.text: Elazar ben Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda
sub.text_en: Elazar ben Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda
sub.desc_en: Elazar ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon, list the skins (of hooves, head of a young calf, under the tail, and the house of shame) that the Sages treat as flesh for impurity.
The baraita states the halakhic consequences for offering these skins outside the designated place (unfit, no karet) or beyond the designated time (piggul, liable for karet).

items.text: פירוש 'בית הפרסות'
items.text_en: Gemara's question: what is 'house of perasot'?
items.desc_en: Rav says it literally means 'house of perasot' (a place where hides are split); Rabbi Chanina says it refers to a saddle sold with the head.
items.desc: הגמרא מבארת את המונח 'בית הפרסות' שבמשנה: רב אומר הכוונה לפרסות ממש, ורבי חנינא אומר הכוונה לעור הרכובה הנמכרת עם הראש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the term 'בית הפרסות' (house of perasot) refers to in the mishna.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהו 'בית הפרסות' הנזכר בברייתא, ומביאה את פירושו של רב שכוונתו לפרסות ממש.

sub.desc_en: Rav says it literally means 'house of perasot' (a place where hides are split).
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהו 'בית הפרסות' הנזכר בברייתא, ומביאה את פירושו של רב שכוונתו לפרסות ממש.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Chanina says it refers to a saddle sold with the head.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהו 'בית הפרסות' הנזכר בברייתא, ומביאה את פירושו של רב שכוונתו לפרסות ממש.

items.text: Gemara on 'the unclean' skins and the exclusion of all skins
items.text_en: Gemara on 'the unclean' skins and the exclusion of all skins
items.desc_en: The baraita says 'the unclean' (in Leviticus 11) includes their skins like their flesh. One might think all skins are included, but the verse says 'these' — limiting to those listed. Rav says 'to their kinds' interrupts the context, excluding others.

sub.desc_en: The baraita teaches that the verse 'the unclean' includes their skins like their flesh.
One might think all skins are included, but the verse says 'these' to limit.
The gemara objects that 'these' is written regarding all the animals listed, not just some.
Rav resolves that the phrase 'to their kinds' interrupts the context, thereby excluding other skins.

items.text: Gemara considers including the tinshemet (chameleon/salamander)
items.text_en: Gemara considers including the tinshemet (chameleon/salamander)
items.desc_en: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak says Rav taught that the tinshemet is included. The local tanna does not teach it. Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi says the local tanna follows Rabbi Yehuda who goes by the gista (the general category), and they dispute over the gista of halata'a (the lizard).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the tinshemet (chameleon/salamander) is not included in the list of animals whose skin is like their flesh.
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak answers that Rav himself taught a baraita that includes the tinshemet.
The Gemara objects that the local tanna (תנא) does not teach the tinshemet in the Mishnah.

sub.text: Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi's resolution
sub.text_en: Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi's resolution
sub.desc_en: Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi resolves that the local tanna follows Rabbi Yehuda, who rules by the gista (general category), and they dispute over the gista of the halata'a (lizard).

items.text: Dispute on whether tanned hides are like flesh for impurity
items.text_en: Dispute on whether tanned hides are like flesh for impurity
items.desc_en: The baraita says 'and all that are worked' — tanned hides are like flesh if worked, but not if not worked. Rabbi Chiya teaches: a donkey's ear tanned and attached to its basket is pure even if not worked. The Gemara clarifies: tanned — yes, not tanned — no. How much tanning? Rav Huna citing Rabbi Yannai says 4 mil; Rabbi Avahu citing Resh Lakish says for plastering.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the baraita's implication that only tanned hides are like flesh, but not untanned ones.

sub.text: Gemara's objection from Rabbi Chiya's baraita
sub.text_en: Gemara's objection from Rabbi Chiya's baraita
sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects by citing Rabbi Chiya's baraita that a donkey's ear attached to its basket is pure even without tanning.
The Gemara resolves that Rabbi Chiya's baraita also requires tanning: the ear was tanned, just not fully worked.

sub.text: Gemara's question on the measure of tanning
sub.text_en: Gemara's question on the measure of tanning
sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks how much tanning is sufficient.
Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Yannai answers that the measure is four mil (a distance).

items.text: Rabbi Avahu and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak on tanning length
items.text_en: Rabbi Avahu and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak on tanning length
items.desc_en: Rabbi Avahu citing Resh Lakish says tanning is for plastering (gabal). For prayer and hand washing, the length is 4 mil. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak concludes the discussion.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Avahu in the name of Resh Lakish defines the tanning process as 'לגבל' (plastering).
The gemara states that for prayer and hand washing, the required distance for water is four mil (miles).
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak begins to speak, concluding the discussion (the rest of his statement is not provided in the section).

items.text: Opening statement about a legion
items.text_en: Opening statement about a legion
items.desc_en: A statement is cited about a legion passing through, and the house they enter becomes impure because they carry skulls. This is a preamble to the Mishnah.

sub.desc_en: A statement is cited about a legion passing through, and the house they enter becomes impure because they carry skulls, serving as a preamble to the Mishnah.

items.text: Rabbi Yosi and Rav Acha's dispute on returning
items.text_en: Rabbi Yosi and Rav Acha's dispute on returning
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina says the Mishnah's rule about returning only applies before the legion passes, but after it passes, even one mil away one does not return. Rav Acha bar Yaakov qualifies that only a mil is not returned, but less than a mil one returns.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina rules that the Mishnah's leniency to return applies only before the legion passes, but after it passes, even one mil away one does not return.
Rav Acha bar Yaakov qualifies that only a full mil is not returned, but less than a mil one does return.

items.text: Baraita about a legion and Rabbi Yishmael's skull
items.text_en: Baraita about a legion and Rabbi Yishmael's skull
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that a legion entering a house makes it impure because they always have skulls, and notes that Rabbi Yishmael's skull was placed before kings.

sub.desc_en: The baraita teaches that a legion passing through makes a house impure because every legion carries skulls, and notes that Rabbi Yishmael's skull was placed before kings.

items.text: Mishnah: Skinning for a mat or waterskin
items.text_en: Mishnah: Skinning for a mat or waterskin
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that one who skins an animal, whether domesticated or wild, pure or impure, small or large, for a mat requires enough skin for a handhold, and for a waterskin until the chest is skinned. The one who folds the skin entirely is connected for impurity. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Sages dispute whether the skin on the neck is connected.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by stating the general rule for one who skins an animal, covering all types (domestic/wild, pure/impure, small/large).
The Mishnah specifies that for a mat, the skinning must provide enough for a handhold (אחיזה).
The Mishnah specifies that for a waterskin, the skinning must extend until the chest is skinned.
The Mishnah states that one who folds the skin entirely makes it connected for impurity, both to receive and convey טומאה (ritual impurity).
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri rules that the skin on the neck is not connected for impurity.
The Sages rule that the skin on the neck is connected until one skins the entire animal.

items.text: Gemara's question and Rav vs. Rabbi Asi on the separated skin
items.text_en: Gemara's question and Rav vs. Rabbi Asi on the separated skin
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the status of the skin is after the measure. Rav says the separated skin is pure, while Rabbi Asi says the handbreadth near the flesh is impure.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the halachic status of the skin is after the measure of peeling has been completed.
Rav rules that the separated skin (המופשט) is pure (טהור).
Rabbi Asi rules that the handbreadth of skin adjacent to the flesh (טפח הסמוך לבשר) remains impure (טמא).

items.text: Objection and resolution from a baraita
items.text_en: Objection and resolution from a baraita
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita that says the separated skin is pure, implying even the handbreadth near the flesh. It is answered that it excludes that handbreadth. Another baraita is brought that says 'skin opposite the flesh' is impure, and it is clarified that this refers to the handbreadth near the flesh.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita stating that after the specified measure, the separated skin is pure, implying even the handbreadth near the flesh is pure.
The Gemara answers that the baraita excludes the handbreadth near the flesh, which remains impure.
Another baraita is brought that says 'skin opposite the flesh' is impure, implying the handbreadth near the flesh is pure.
The Tanna clarifies that the term 'skin opposite the flesh' refers specifically to the handbreadth near the flesh, resolving the apparent contradiction.

items.text: Another objection and resolution about the handbreadth
items.text_en: Another objection and resolution about the handbreadth
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings another baraita that explicitly states the handbreadth near the flesh is pure. It is answered that this refers to the first handbreadth (the one held), not the one near the flesh.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita that explicitly states the handbreadth near the flesh is pure, challenging the view that it is impure.
The Gemara resolves the objection by explaining that the baraita refers to the first handbreadth (the one held), not the handbreadth near the flesh.

items.text: Dispute about the measure of 'enough to hold'
items.text_en: Dispute about the measure of 'enough to hold'
items.desc_en: A baraita says 'enough to hold' is a handbreadth, but another says two handbreadths. Abaye resolves that it is a folded handbreadth, and a baraita supports this.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita that defines 'enough to hold' as a handbreadth.
The Gemara objects that another baraita states 'two handbreadths', creating a contradiction.
Abaye resolves the contradiction by explaining that the measure is a folded handbreadth, which equals two handbreadths when unfolded.
A supporting baraita is cited that explicitly defines 'enough to hold' as a folded handbreadth, confirming Abaye's resolution.

items.text: Digression: A torn cloak and its connection for impurity
items.text_en: Digression: A torn cloak and its connection for impurity
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a Mishnah about a cloak that is torn: once most is torn, it is no longer connected and is pure. Rav Nachman in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha says this only applies to a cloak that is a tevul yom (immersed that day), because since one did not spare it from immersion, one will not spare it from tearing most of it. Rabbah raises two objections: people might think immersion on the same day is effective, and another reason.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a Mishnah from another context: a cloak that one began to tear, once most of it is torn, it is no longer connected and is pure.

sub.text: Rav Nachman in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha
sub.text_en: Rav Nachman in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman in the name of Rabbah bar Avuha limits the Mishnah to a cloak that is a טבולת יום (one who immersed that day), because since one did not spare it from immersion, one will not spare it from tearing most of it.
The Gemara explains that for a cloak that is not a טבולת יום, the rule does not apply, as a גזירה (decree) lest one not come to tear most of it.
Rabbah raises two objections against Rav Nachman's limitation: first, people might mistakenly think that immersion on the same day is effective, and second, another reason (cut off in the source).

items.text: חשש גזירה בעולת העוף ובטבילה
items.text_en: Gemara's initial discussion on decrees
items.desc_en: The Gemara considers whether to decree regarding the bird-offering according to Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon, and Rav Yosef responds that the tear in the hide proves the case, and that priests are vigilant.
items.desc: רבה גוזר גזירות דרבנן על מעשים דקים מחשש שיבואו לעשות חצי סימנים או יטעו בעניין טבילה. רב יוסף משיב שהכהנים זריזים ואין לגזור, ושהקרע מוכיח על הבגד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks whether to decree regarding the bird-offering according to Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon, lest one come to perform the majority of two.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה שגם בעולת העוף לדעת רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון יש לגזור שמא יעשה חצי סימנים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef responds that regarding the decree about a טבילת בת יומא (same-day immersion), the tear in the hide proves the case.
sub.desc: רב יוסף משיב שבטבילה אין לגזור, כי הקרע מוכיח על הבגד.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef resolves that regarding the bird-offering, no decree is needed because priests are vigilant.
sub.desc: רב יוסף משיב שבעולת העוף אין לגזור, כי הכהנים זריזים.

items.text: Challenge from the Mishnah on skinning
items.text_en: Challenge from the Mishnah on skinning
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites a Mishnah about skinning animals for a rug, where if the hide is larger than needed for grasping, it is pure. It questions why no decree is made, and answers that this deals with rabbinic impurity, not Torah impurity.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a Mishnah about skinning animals for a rug, where only the hide needed for grasping is considered connected.
The Gemara questions why the Mishnah declares the excess hide pure, since one might mistakenly touch impurity while skinning only the needed portion.
The Gemara answers that the Mishnah deals with rabbinic impurity (טומאה דרבנן), not Torah impurity, so no decree is needed.

items.text: Clarification regarding a terefah animal
items.text_en: Clarification regarding a terefah animal
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions the case of a pure person skinning an impure animal, which involves Torah impurity, and resolves it by referring to a terefah animal, which according to Shmuel's father imparts impurity in the Temple.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the case of a pure person skinning an impure animal, noting that this involves Torah-level impurity.
The Gemara resolves the difficulty by referring to a טריפה (terefah) animal, which has a special status.
The Gemara objects that a טריפה (terefah) animal is generally not capable of imparting impurity.
The Gemara answers affirmatively, citing Avuh deShmuel's ruling that a טריפה (terefah) animal that was slaughtered imparts impurity in the Temple (במוקדשין).

items.text: הפשטת שרצים והבחנת גמל
items.text_en: Discussion on connection for creeping animals
items.desc_en: Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda says skinning a creeping animal is connected until fully skinned, implying for a camel it is not connected. The Gemara reinterprets this as referring to the neck hide, and attributes the view to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
items.desc: ברייתא של ר' דוסתאי קובעת שבשרצים העור חיבור עד שמפשיט כולו, אבל בגמל אינו חיבור. הגמרא דוחה שהמדובר בעור הצוואר, ויתכן שזו דעת ר' יוחנן בן נורי.

sub.text_en: Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda citing Rabbi Shimon
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda states that skinning a creeping animal (שרץ) remains connected until the entire hide is removed.
sub.desc: הבאת ברייתא בשם ר' דוסתאי המשמשת כראיה נגד שיטת רבא בר אבוה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers that for a camel (גמל), the hide is not considered connected, implying a distinction between creeping animals and larger animals.
sub.desc: הסקה מהברייתא שדין גמל שונה משרץ, ומכאן קושיא על שיטת רבא בר אבוה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara reinterprets the statement: it does not refer to a camel but to the neck hide (עור שעל הצואר), and attributes this view to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
sub.desc: דחיית ההבנה הפשוטה של הברייתא והסבר שהאינו חיבור מתייחס דווקא לעור הצוואר, וזו דעת ר' יוחנן בן נורי.

items.text: Rav Huna's distinction regarding the amount left
items.text_en: Rav Huna's distinction regarding the amount left
items.desc_en: Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yosei states that the ruling applies only if no amount the size of a ma'aporet was left; if such an amount was left, it is connected.

sub.text: Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yosei
sub.text_en: Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yosei
sub.desc_en: Rav Huna, citing Rabbi Shimon bar Yosei, resolves the earlier dispute by distinguishing whether a piece the size of a ma'aporet (a handbreadth) was left attached: if not, the skin is not connected; if so, it is connected.

items.text: Dispute between Resh Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan on hide firmness
items.text_en: Dispute between Resh Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan on hide firmness
items.desc_en: Resh Lakish says the rule about connection applies only to a garment, but a hide is firm and thus not connected. Rabbi Yochanan disagrees. Rabbi Yochanan challenges Resh Lakish from a Mishnah about a hide designated for straps, which becomes pure when cut, implying it is not firm. The Gemara resolves that the discussion is about cutting around the edges.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish states that the rule of connection applies only to a garment, but a hide is firm and thus not connected.
Rabbi Yochanan disagrees, asserting that even a hide is not considered firm.
Rabbi Yochanan challenges Resh Lakish from a Mishnah about a hide designated for straps, which becomes pure when cut, implying it is not firm.
The Gemara resolves that the discussion about firmness applies when cutting around the edges, not when cutting straight across.

items.text: קושיית ר' ירמיה על ריש לקיש
items.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeya's challenge and Rabbi Avin's answer
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya challenges from the Mishnah on skinning for a rug, asking why the excess hide is pure if it is firm. Rabbi Avin answers that each piece becomes a separate falling piece.
items.desc: ר' ירמיה מקשה על ריש לקיש מהברייתא על המפשיט: הפשיט יותר מכדי אחיזה העור טהור, ואמאי לא נחשב חלים? ר' אבין מתרץ שבהפשטה כל חלק נופל מיד ואינו ניתן לתיקון.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya challenges from the Mishnah on skinning for a rug: why is excess hide pure if it is firm (חֲלִים)?
sub.desc: רבי ירמיה מקשה על ריש לקיש מהברייתא: בהפשיט יותר מכדי אחיזה העור טהור, ואמאי לא נחשב חלים?

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Avin answers that each piece becomes a separate falling piece (נִיפּוּל), so the hide is not considered connected.
sub.desc: רבי ירמיה מקשה על ריש לקיש מהברייתא: בהפשיט יותר מכדי אחיזה העור טהור, ואמאי לא נחשב חלים?

items.text: קושיית רב יוסף על ריש לקיש בעניין עור הצוואר
items.text_en: Rabbi Yosef's challenge and Abaye's resolution
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yosef challenges from the case of the neck hide, which Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says is not connected, but it is firm. Abaye points out that the Sages disagree and say it is connected. He explains they dispute whether it is a guard that will detach on its own.
items.desc: רב יוסף מקשה על ריש לקיש שהרי עור הצוואר חלים ועומד אך ר' יוחנן בן נורי אומר שאינו חיבור. אביי משיב שזו מחלוקת אחרת בשאלה האם שמר העשוי לינתק נחשב שמר.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yosef challenges from the case of the neck hide, which Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says is not connected, yet it is firm, implying that firmness does not make something a connector.
sub.desc: רב יוסף מקשה על ריש לקיש מעור הצוואר, שלדעת רבי יוחנן בן נורי אינו חיבור, אף על פי שהוא חלים ועומד.

sub.desc_en: Abaye points out that the Sages disagree with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and say the neck hide is connected, so the challenge is only according to the minority opinion.
sub.desc: אביי דוחה את הקושיה באומרו שיש להביא את סוף דברי המשנה, שחכמים חולקים ואומרים שהעור חיבור.

sub.desc_en: Abaye explains that the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Sages is about whether the neck hide is considered a guard (שומר) that will detach on its own, with one holding it is a guard and the other holding it is not.
sub.desc: אביי מיישב את המחלוקת: היא אינה תלויה בשאלת חלימה, אלא בשאלה אם עור הצוואר נחשב 'שומר העשוי לינתק' אם לאו.

items.text: דיני טהרת תנור טמא
items.text_en: Rabbi Yirmeya's challenge from the oven purification
items.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya challenges with a Mishnah about purifying a contaminated oven by dividing it into three and scraping off the clay, implying a different principle.
items.desc: הגמרא פותחת בסוגיית טהרת תנור על ידי חלוקתו וגירור הטפילה, אך קטע זה נקטע ואינו מפותח.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yirmeya challenges with a Mishnah about purifying a contaminated oven by dividing it into three and scraping off the clay, implying a different principle.
sub.desc: רבי ירמיה מקשה מברייתא העוסקת בטהרת תנור טמא על ידי חלוקתו וגירור הטפילה, כהכנה לדחיית שיטת ריש לקיש.

items.text: Opening Mishnah: Oven purification dispute
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah: Oven purification dispute
items.desc_en: The Mishnah presents a dispute about how to purify a contracted oven: the first opinion requires scraping the clay and reducing it to the ground, while Rabbi Meir says one need only reduce it from inside to four handbreadths.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah presents a dispute: the first opinion requires scraping the clay until the oven is level with the ground, while Rabbi Meir says one need only reduce it from inside to four handbreadths.

items.text: Gemara's question and Rava's initial answer
items.text_en: Gemara's question and Rava's initial answer
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why reducing to four handbreadths purifies, since the oven is still intact. Rava suggests that the first opinion is rabbinic, requiring scraping to the ground.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why reducing the oven from four handbreadths purifies it, since the oven is still intact and functional.
Rava initially answers that the first opinion is rabbinic, requiring scraping the clay coating down to the ground.

items.text: Rava's corrected explanation of the Mishnah
items.text_en: Rava's corrected explanation of the Mishnah
items.desc_en: Rava reinterprets the Mishnah: it discusses how to purify a contracted oven, with the first opinion requiring division into three parts and scraping to the ground, while Rabbi Meir says one need only reduce it from inside to four handbreadths.

sub.desc_en: Rava introduces a corrected explanation of the Mishnah: the first opinion requires dividing the oven into three parts and scraping the clay down to the ground.
Rava adds that one who wishes to prevent the oven from becoming susceptible to impurity must also divide it into three and scrape the clay to the ground.
Rabbi Meir rules that one need not scrape the clay or go down to the ground, but only reduce the oven from inside to four handbreadths.

items.text: Contradiction about oven dimensions and resolution
items.text_en: Contradiction about oven dimensions and resolution
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes a contradiction: Rabbi Meir says an oven's initial size is four handbreadths and its remnants are four, but the Mishnah says remnants are in its majority. The resolution distinguishes between a large oven (nine handbreadths) and a small one (seven).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by citing the Mishnah's rule that one divides the oven into three parts.
The Gemara raises a contradiction: a baraita states that Rabbi Meir says an oven's initial size is four handbreadths and its remnants are four, conflicting with the Mishnah's implication.
The Sages resolve the contradiction by distinguishing between a large oven (nine handbreadths) and a small one (seven), where the small oven's remnants are in its majority.
Bei Rabbi Yannai specifies that 'any amount' for a small oven is one handbreadth, as they make small portable ovens of that size.

items.text: Distinction between cutting and making a gistra
items.text_en: Distinction between cutting and making a gistra
items.desc_en: The Gemara resolves the contradiction by distinguishing between cutting the oven (which requires remnants of four) and making it into a gistra (which purifies even without four).

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers from the Mishnah that if the oven's remnants are not four handbreadths, it is pure, implying a contradiction with the earlier baraita.
The Sages resolve the contradiction by distinguishing between cutting the oven into pieces (which requires remnants of four) and making it into a gistra (a frame, which purifies even without four).

items.text: Abaye's resolution for majority of a handbreadth
items.text_en: Abaye's resolution for majority of a handbreadth
items.desc_en: Abaye explains that 'remnants in its majority' refers to a large oven's remnants, while the Sages' four handbreadths applies to a seven-handbreadth oven.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions the statement that the remnants of a small oven are measured by its majority, asking what purpose the majority of a handbreadth serves.

Abaye resolves the difficulty by distinguishing between a nine-handbreadth oven, where the majority of a handbreadth applies, and a seven-handbreadth oven, where the Sages' four handbreadths rule applies.

items.text: Alternative version: Rav Huna's statement
items.text_en: Alternative version: Rav Huna's statement
items.desc_en: An alternative version cites Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Yishmael ben Rabbi Yosei, saying that even if one left a ma'aporet's worth, it is significant.

sub.desc_en: An alternative version cites Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Yishmael ben Rabbi Yosei, stating that even if one left a ma'aporet's worth, it is significant.

items.text: מחלוקת רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש בעור טמא מדרס
items.text_en: Dispute between Resh Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan on hide significance
items.desc_en: Resh Lakish says the Mishnah's rule about nullification applies only to a garment, not a hide, while Rabbi Yochanan says even a hide is not significant. Rabbi Yochanan challenges Resh Lakish with a baraita about a hide designated for straps, which becomes pure when cut, but the Gemara explains it refers to a seat for a zav.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה מחלוקת בין ריש לקיש לרבי יוחנן: האם עור שנקרע נחשב 'חשיב' ונשאר בטומאתו. רבי יוחנן מקשה מברייתא על עור טמא מדרס, וריש לקיש מתרץ שמדובר במושב זב.

sub.desc_en: Resh Lakish states that the Mishnah's rule about nullification applies only to a garment, but a hide is considered significant.
sub.desc: ריש לקיש מבדיל בין טלית לעור: בעור נחשב חשיב; רבי יוחנן חולק ואומר שגם עור אינו חשיב.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan counters that even a hide is not considered significant.
sub.desc: ריש לקיש מבדיל בין טלית לעור: בעור נחשב חשיב; רבי יוחנן חולק ואומר שגם עור אינו חשיב.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan challenges Resh Lakish with a baraita about a hide designated for straps, which becomes pure when cut, implying it is not significant.
sub.desc: רבי יוחנן מקשה לריש לקיש מברייתא על עור טמא מדרס: לדברי חכמים, רק כשממעיטו מחמישה טפחים טהור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the baraita refers to a hide designated for a seat for a zav, which is significant, so it does not contradict Resh Lakish.
sub.desc: ריש לקיש מתרץ: מדובר בעור המיועד למושב זב, ולכן פחות מחמישה טפחים אינו חשוב.

items.text: משנה: טומאת עור ובשר – חצאי זיתים ומחלוקת רבי ישמעאל ורבי עקיבא
items.text_en: Mishnah: Hide with meat and impurity
items.desc_en: The Mishnah discusses a hide with an olive's bulk of meat: touching the protruding flesh or corresponding hair conveys impurity. With two half-olives, Rabbi Yishmael says it conveys impurity through carrying but not contact, while Rabbi Akiva says it conveys neither, because the hide nullifies them.
items.desc: המשנה דנה בטומאת עור שיש עליו כזית בשר. אם יש שני חצאי זיתים, רבי ישמעאל מטמא במשא ורבי עקיבא מטהר לגמרי, משום שהעור מבטל את הבשר.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens with the case of a hide bearing an olive's bulk of meat: touching the protruding flesh or corresponding hair conveys impurity.
sub.desc: פותח בדין עור שיש עליו כזית בשר: הנוגע בציב או בשערה שכנגדו טמא.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yishmael rules that two half-olives on the hide convey impurity through carrying but not through contact.
sub.desc: רבי ישמעאל קובע: על שני חצאי זיתים, מטמא במשא ולא במגע.

sub.desc_en: Rabbi Akiva rules that two half-olives convey neither through contact nor through carrying, but concedes impurity if they are skewered on a stick and moved.
sub.desc: רבי ישמעאל קובע: על שני חצאי זיתים, מטמא במשא ולא במגע.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah explains that Rabbi Akiva declares the hide pure because the hide nullifies the two half-olives.
sub.desc: רבי ישמעאל קובע: על שני חצאי זיתים, מטמא במשא ולא במגע.

items.text: Ulla's statement and Rav Nachman's challenge
items.text_en: Ulla's statement and Rav Nachman's challenge
items.desc_en: Ulla says in Rabbi Yochanan's name that the Mishnah's rule applies only when an animal expelled the meat, but if a knife cut it, it is nullified. Rav Nachman challenges: even if it is as large as a tarta or a nafya? Ulla confirms, and Rav Nachman swears he would not listen even if Rabbi Yochanan said it directly.

sub.desc_en: Ulla states in Rabbi Yochanan's name that the Mishnah's rule of impurity applies only when an animal expelled the meat, but if a knife cut it, the meat is nullified.
Rav Nachman challenges Ulla: does Rabbi Yochanan's ruling apply even to a piece as large as a tarta or a nafya?
Ulla confirms that Rabbi Yochanan's ruling applies even to pieces as large as a tarta and a nafya.
Rav Nachman swears that even if Rabbi Yochanan himself told him this directly, he would not listen.

items.text: Rav Oshaya's report and the dispute's resolution
items.text_en: Rav Oshaya's report and the dispute's resolution
items.desc_en: Rav Oshaya reports the dispute to Rabbi Ami, who criticizes Rav Nachman for disrespecting Rabbi Yochanan. Later, Rabbi Yochanan himself teaches the statement on the latter clause, and Mar challenges whether it was taught on the latter clause. Ulla confirms it was on the first clause, leading to a strong rejection.

sub.text: Narrative: Rav Oshaya's report to Rabbi Ami
sub.text_en: Narrative: Rav Oshaya's report to Rabbi Ami
sub.desc_en: Rav Oshaya reports the exchange between Ulla and Rav Nachman to Rabbi Ami, who criticizes Rav Nachman for disrespecting Rabbi Yochanan's teaching.

sub.text: Narrative: Rabbi Yochanan teaches the statement on the latter clause
sub.text_en: Narrative: Rabbi Yochanan teaches the statement on the latter clause
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Yochanan is found teaching the same statement (that only if an animal expelled the meat, but if a knife cut it, it is nullified) in the context of the latter clause of the Mishnah.
Mar challenges whether Rabbi Yochanan taught the statement on the latter clause, and receives confirmation.
Ulla confirms that he had taught the statement on the first clause, leading Mar to declare that even if Joshua bin Nun said it in Rabbi Yochanan's name, he would not listen.

items.text: Ravin's resolution and Rav Pappa's explanation
items.text_en: Ravin's resolution and Rav Pappa's explanation
items.desc_en: When Ravin and others came, they taught the statement on the first clause, and the Gemara notes the difficulty is resolved as Rav Pappa said.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves the difficulty by citing Ravin's teaching on the first clause, consistent with Rav Pappa's explanation.

items.text: הסבר מרודד
items.text_en: Reassertion of the 'smoothed' case
items.desc_en: The Gemara reiterates that the earlier ruling about two half-olives on a hide is specifically in a case where the flesh is flattened (מרודד).
items.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שהדיון הקודם עוסק במקרה של בשר מרודד (דק) המחובר לעור, שבו הבשר מתבטל לעור.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara reasserts that the earlier ruling about two half-olives on a hide applies specifically when the flesh is flattened (מרודד).
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שהדיון הקודם עוסק במקרה של בשר מרודד (דק) המחובר לעור, שבו הבשר מתבטל לעור.

items.text: The Mishnah's case introduced
items.text_en: The Mishnah's case introduced
items.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Mishnah's phrase 'They were upon him' to set up the debate about touching from front vs. back.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Mishnah's phrase 'הָיוּ עָלָיו' (they were upon him) to introduce the case of two half-olive-sized pieces of neveila on a person.

items.text: Bar Peda vs. Rabbi Yochanan on 'touching and returning to touch'
items.text_en: Bar Peda vs. Rabbi Yochanan on 'touching and returning to touch'
items.desc_en: Bar Peda limits the ruling that there is 'no touching and returning to touch' to touching from behind, but from the front one may. Rabbi Yochanan disagrees, holding that there is no such possibility at all from any direction. He links this to Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas, who similarly denies 'overshadowing and returning to overshadow'.

sub.desc_en: Bar Peda states that the mishna's ruling (no joining of touches) applies only when touching from behind, but from the front, one may touch and return to touch.
Rabbi Yochanan disagrees, asserting there is no 'touching and returning to touch' at all, and links this to the agreement between Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas.
The Gemara cites the mishna in Oholot where Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas rules that divided corpse-parts do not join to impart tent impurity, while the Sages disagree.
The Gemara infers that just as Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas denies 'overshadowing and returning to overshadow', so too Rabbi Yochanan denies 'touching and returning to touch'.

items.text: קושיה ותירוץ על שיטת רבי עקיבא
items.text_en: Counter-challenge: Rabbi Dosa's opinion implies Rabbi Akiva's?
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions: if Rabbi Dosa aligns with Rabbi Yishmael, do the Sages then align with Rabbi Akiva? It answers that Rabbi Akiva only purifies in the case of hide, but in general he deems impure, as the Mishnah's continuation shows that he agrees regarding two half-olives on a stick.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם רבי דוסא כרבי ישמעאל, הרי רבנן צריכים להיות כרבי עקיבא, אך רבי עקיבא מטהר בעור. מתורצת: רבי עקיבא מטהר רק בעור משום שהעור מבטל את הבשר, אבל בעלמא מטמא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges: if Rabbi Dosa aligns with Rabbi Yishmael, do the Sages then align with Rabbi Akiva, even though Rabbi Akiva purifies in the hide case?
sub.desc: מקשה: אם רבי דוסא כשיטת רבי ישמעאל שאין נוגע וחוזר ונוגע, ממילא רבנן החולקים עליו כאילו מחזיקים כשיטת רבי עקיבא, והלא רבי עקיבא עצמו מטהר בעור?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that Rabbi Akiva only purifies in the case of hide because the hide nullifies the flesh, but in general he deems impure, as the Mishnah's continuation shows he agrees regarding two half-olives on a stick.
sub.desc: מבאר: רבי עקיבא מטהר רק בכה

items.text: קושיית רב עוקבא בר חמא ותירוץ רבא
items.text_en: Objection from Baraita and Rava's explanation
items.desc_en: Rav Ukva bar Chama challenges: the verse exempts hide with two half-olives from impurity touching, but includes carrying. Rabbi Akiva's rule about 'what comes into the category of touching comes into carrying' is explained by Rava: it means touching on every side, not just the front.
items.desc: רב עוקבא בר חמא מקשה מברייתא על בר פדא: אם יש צירוף נגיעה מלפנים, מדוע רבי עקיבא חולק על רבי ישמעאל? רבא מתרץ: הכוונה לנגיעה בכל צד, לא רק מלפנים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ukva bar Chama raises an objection from a baraita: the verse 'בנבלתם' (in their carcass) excludes a hide with two half-olive-bulks from impurity via contact, but includes impurity via carrying according to Rabbi Yishmael.
sub.desc: רב עוקבא בר חמא מקשה מברייתא על בר פדא: אם יש צירוף נגיעה מלפנים, מדוע רבי עקיבא חולק על רבי ישמעאל?

sub.desc_en: The baraita cites Rabbi Akiva's principle: what enters the category of contact enters the category of carrying; what does not enter contact does not enter carrying.
The Gemara questions: if bar Padda's view holds, the hide enters contact from the front, so why does Rabbi Akiva disagree?
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה את הקושיה: אם יש צירוף נגיעה מלפנים, הרי העור בא לכלל מגע.

sub.desc_en: Rava explains: Rabbi Akiva means that only what enters contact on every side enters carrying; the hide does not enter contact on every side, so it does not enter carrying.
sub.desc: רבא מתרץ: הכוונה לנגיעה בכל צד, לא רק מלפנים.

items.text: שאלת רב אויא סבא על קולית סתומה
items.text_en: Question of a sealed bone for Rabbi Yishmael
items.desc_en: Rav Avya the Elder asks Rabbah bar Rav Huna whether a sealed bone (קולית סתומה) conveys impurity for Rabbi Yishmael, given the principle of 'coming into touching from the front'. Rabbah deflects, and Rava his son expresses disappointment that such a great man asked a simple question.
items.desc: רב אויא סבא שואל את רבה בר רב הונא: האם קולית סתומה מטמאה במשא לרבי ישמעאל? רבה מתחמק בתשובה 'עורבא פרח', ומסביר שהיה עייף.

sub.desc_en: Rav Avya the Elder asks Rabbah bar Rav Huna whether a sealed bone (קולית סתומה) imparts impurity according to Rabbi Yishmael.
sub.desc: רב אויא סבא שואל את רבה בר רב הונא מה דינה של קולית סתומה לרבי ישמעאל—האם מטמאה במשא או לא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Avya the Elder presents one possibility: Rabbi Yishmael holds the principle that what enters contact enters carrying, and here the bone enters contact from the front, so it would be impure.
sub.desc: רב אויא מציג אפשרות שלרבי ישמעאל יש כלל שרק מה שבא לכדי מגע בא לכדי משא, ובקולית סתומה יש מגע מלפנים.

sub.desc_en: Rav Avya the Elder raises the alternative: perhaps Rabbi Yishmael does not hold that principle, so the sealed bone would not impart impurity.
sub.desc: רב אויא מעלה אפשרות הפוכה—שאולי לרבי ישמעאל אין כלל כזה, והקולית מטמאה במשא אפילו בלי מגע.

sub.desc_en: Rabbah bar Rav Huna deflects the question with a distraction, saying 'a raven flies'.
sub.desc: רבה בר רב הונא מתחמק מהשאלה באמירה סתומה 'עורבא פרח'.

sub.desc_en: Rava expresses disappointment that his father treated Rav Avya the Elder, a great man, with such a distraction.
sub.desc: רבא תמה על אביו מדוע התחמק, ורבה מסביר שהיה עייף מכדי לעסוק בעניין המצריך טעם ועיון.

sub.desc_en: Rabbah bar Rav Huna explains that he was tired and the question required careful reasoning, so he could not answer immediately.
sub.desc: רבא תמה על אביו מדוע התחמק, ורבה מסביר שהיה עייף מכדי לעסוק בעניין המצריך טעם ועיון.

items.text: דין שני חצאי זיתים תחובים בקיסם
items.text_en: Ulla's ruling on two half-olives on a stick
items.desc_en: Ulla rules that two half-olives on a stick are pure even if moved all day, because the verse requires a single lift. The Gemara challenges from the Mishnah (half-olives on a hide) and from Rabbi Akiva's admission, both answered by saying the cases involve flattened flesh (מרודד).
items.desc: עולא פוטר מטומאת משא בשני חצאי זיתים תחובים בקיסם, משום שצריך 'נושא' ו'נישא' בבת אחת. הגמרא מקשה מהמשנה ומתרצת שמדובר במרודד.

sub.desc_en: Ulla rules that two half-olives impaled on a stick remain pure even if moved all day, because the verse requires a single lift (נישא בבת אחת).
sub.desc: עולא פוטר מטומאת משא בשני חצאי זיתים תחובים בקיסם, משום שצריך נושא ונישא בבת אחת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara challenges Ulla from the Mishnah that two half-olives on a hide convey impurity through carrying, even though they are not lifted as a single unit.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מהמשנה ששני חצאי זיתים שעל העור מטמאים במשא, אף שאינם נישאים בבת אחת.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa answers that the Mishnah's case involves flattened flesh (מרודד), which is considered a single unit.
sub.desc: רב פפא מתרץ שהמשנה עוסקת במרודד, שבו הבשר מחובר ברצועה דקה ומתאחד לכדי נישא בבת אחת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a second challenge from Rabbi Akiva's admission that two half-olives on a stick convey impurity, and resolves it similarly by invoking flattened flesh (מרודד).
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה סיוע מעדות רבי עקיבא המטמא בהסטת שני חצאי זיתים תחובים בקיסם, ומתרצת שגם שם מדובר במרודד.

items.text: ברייתא על נוגע ומסיט ונושא
items.text_en: The Tannaic dispute over 'one who carries' vs. 'one who moves'
items.desc_en: The Gemara examines a braita where Rabbi Eliezer states that 'one who carries' is included beyond just moving, but the Gemara reinterprets it to mean that carrying with a single lift is required.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא: נוגע ומסיט טמאים, ורבי אליעזר מוסיף נושא. הגמרא מבררת: הכוונה שמסיט בלא נישא, ורבי אליעזר מצריך נישא בבת אחת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces a Tannaic dispute (כְּתַנָּאֵי) where Rabbi Eliezer adds 'one who carries' (אַף הַנּוֹשֵׂא) beyond 'one who touches' and 'one who moves', and immediately questions how carrying differs from moving.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה ברייתא המציגה עמדות תנאים: תנא קמא מטמא נוגע ומסיט, ורבי אליעזר מוסיף אף נושא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves the difficulty by reinterpreting the braita: Rabbi Eliezer's 'one who carries' actually means that the object must be carried with a single lift (נִישָּׂא), not merely moved.
sub.desc: הגמרא מיישבת: הברייתא עוסקת במקרה שהאיסור אינו נישא בבת אחת; תנא קמא מטמא אף אז, ורבי אליעזר מצריך נישא בבת אחת.

items.text: משנת הפתיחה: טומאת קולית בקדשים, נבלה ושרץ
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Mishnah distinguishes between bones of sacrifices, which are impure whether sealed or perforated, and bones of carcasses or creeping things, which are impure only when perforated. It derives that impurity through carrying applies only where contact applies.
items.desc: המשנה קובעת שקולית מוקדשים מטמאת במגע בין סתומה בין נקובה, ואילו קולית נבלה ושרץ מטמאת רק בנקובה. הגמרא מסיקה שמגע ומשא נקשרים זה לזה מהפסוק.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that bones of sacrifices (קוּלִית הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין) are impure whether sealed or perforated.
sub.desc: המשנה קובעת דיני טומאת קולית בקדשים, נבלה ושרץ, ומקשרת מגע ומשא מהפסוק.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah contrasts that bones of carcasses or creeping things are pure when sealed but impure when perforated, even minimally, through contact.
The Mishnah derives from the verse 'הַנּוֹגֵעַ … וְהַנּוֹשֵׂא' that impurity through carrying applies only where contact applies.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא: מדוע קולית המת אינה מטמאה באוהל?
items.text_en: Gemara's question on overshadowing
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah only mentions contact and not overshadowing. It considers scenarios with an olive's bulk of flesh or marrow, concluding that marrow inside does not produce a healing scab on the outside, as stated by Rav Yehuda bar Rabbi Chiyya.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם יש כזית בשר או מוח, או שמוח מעלה ארוכה, הרי העצם צריכה לטמא באוהל. רב יהודה בר רבי חייא מתרץ שמוח בפנים אינו מעלה ארוכה מבחוץ.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah only mentions contact (מגע) and not overshadowing (אוהל), and considers whether there is an olive's bulk of flesh or marrow.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מדוע המשנה דייקה 'נוגע' ולא 'מאהיל', ומשמע שקולית המת אינה מטמאה באוהל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that there is no olive's bulk of flesh and no olive's bulk of marrow inside the bone.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת: אם יש כזית בשר על העצם, הרי היא מטמאה באוהל; על כרחך מדובר שאין כזית בשר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that if the marrow inside produces a healing scab on the outside, the limb would be considered a complete organ and should transmit impurity through overshadowing.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם מוח בפנים מעלה ארוכה מבחוץ, הרי העצם נחשבת איבר שלם ומטמאה באוהל אף בלא כזית.

sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda bar Rabbi Chiyya's statement
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda bar Rabbi Chiyya resolves that this teaches that marrow inside does not produce a healing scab on the outside.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם מוח בפנים מעלה ארוכה מבחוץ, הרי העצם נחשבת איבר שלם ומטמאה באוהל אף בלא כזית.

items.text: קושיה על האוקימתא: קולית מוקדשים ונבלה
items.text_en: Resolution of the Mishnah's two parts
items.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the first part (sacrifices) deals with less than an olive's bulk, while the second part (carcass) deals with an olive's bulk. It explains that sacrifices teach that bones used for leftover (notar) are impure, citing Mari bar Avuh in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak.
items.desc: אם האוקימתא היא כשאין כזית, מדוע קולית מוקדשים מטמאה? ומדוע קולית נבלה מטמאה בנקובה? מתרץ: רישא בלי כזית, סיפא עם כזית; ומפרש שמוקדשים מטמאים משום ששימשו נותר, ונבלה מטמאה רק בנקובה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions: if the first clause deals with less than an olive's bulk, why do sacrificial bones impart impurity?
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם האוקימתא היא שאין כזית מוח, מדוע קולית מוקדשים מטמאה?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara further questions: why do carcass and creeping animal bones impart impurity when perforated, if there is no olive's bulk?
sub.desc: הגמרא מוסיפה קושיה: מדוע קולית נבלה ושרץ מטמאות כשנקבו?

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers: it is not difficult; the first clause lacks an olive's bulk, the latter clause has an olive's bulk, and the mishna teaches separate matters.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: אין קושיה, הרישא עוסקת באין כזית והסיפא בכזית, והתנא משמיע עניינים נפרדים.

sub.text: הגמרא מביאה מאמר מרי בר אבוה
sub.text_en: Mari bar Avuh citing Rabbi Yitzchak
sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains: the first clause teaches that marrow inside does not heal; the sacrificial clause teaches that bones used for notar are significant, citing Mari bar Avuh in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak that such bones transmit impurity to hands.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבארת: הרישא מלמדת שמוח מבפנים אינו מעלה ארוכה מבחוץ; לגבי מוקדשים, שימוש נותר הוא דבר חשוב, כדברי מרי בר אבוה בשם רבי יצחק שעצמות קדשים ששימשו נותר מטמאות את הידיים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes: regarding a carcass, even with an olive's bulk, only a perforated bone imparts impurity, not a sealed one.
